name: Cinders
description:
The beautiful Cinders is a 6 year old Greyhound with the sweetest, loveliest personality. She’s a gentle, affectionate girl who loves people, greeting everyone with a wagging tail and accepting soft fusses. She enjoys engaging in enrichment and likes soft, squeaky toys - she can usually be seen flinging them around and chasing them! Cinders is happy with a little potter about but she’s a couch potato at heart, happiest just being at home with her people, curled up beside you and snoozing the afternoon away.

Cinders would be happy living in a variety of environments, from a town to a residential area, given there is access to quieter roads and calm walking areas. As Cinders currently finds the car quite scary, she would benefit from a home with a driveway where she can continue her car training and build her confidence. She would be happy living with another dog, given a successful meet at the centre, and would be able to live with secondary school aged children given they are sensible and respectful of her space. She will need adopters who can build up her time spent alone and allow her to settle into the home environment.

name: Lipton
description:
Meet Lipton our lively 3yr old French Bulldog. He is a friendly chap who loves being around people, but is sometimes protective of his things. An adult only home will suit him best for this reason. Lipton can share his home with another dog. He is a playful boy so would like any doggy friend to match this.

Lipton originally found his way into our care as a stray, but has since spent a little time in a home. He would benefit from an introduction to the basics, though is happy to jump into a car. Lipton hasn’t had much experience of being left but was  fine being home alone for an hour or so in his last home.

name: Sonny
description:
Sonny is suitable to live with secondary school children and is looking to be the only pet. He may benefit from some further training and would enjoy his brain being kept busy.

Sonny is the life and soul of the party. He approaches life with a lot of enthusiasm and may just need this channelling into appropriate outlets. He loves the car so is now ready to go on his next big adventure.

name: Peroni
description:
Peroni is a gorgeous 9 week old Italian Corso Crossbreed who is looking for his first and forever home. He will be fine to live with other pets and older children as long as they are comfortable around big, strong dogs as he may be small now but he's going to grow a lot! He will need his new family to be ready to do all the basic training a young pup needs from house training to lead walking and general settling.

Peroni is a real bundle of energy and once he's picked up a good and consistent routine he should thrive. Add him to your favourites if you love BIG dogs and have the time to settle him in properly and continue all his training.

name: Hugo
description:
Hugo would like to be the only pet in the home, but he could live with secondary school aged children. He could be left for a full working day with a toilet break in the middle.

Hugo is an absolute delight who has settled amazingly into his foster home. He would make a great addition to a household that would love outdoor walks and adventures closely followed by plenty of cuddles on the sofa!

name: Margot
description:
Margot is a 11 month old Whippet X Lurcher. She could join a home with another dog pending meets at the centre and has previously lived with cats. She is a friendly girl but can be worried so could live with children of Primary School age who can understand her nervous nature. She would like access to a secure garden so she has somewhere to run around and play and to help with housetraining. Once settled, leaving hours could be introduced.

Margot is a lovely girl who has come into our care through no fault of her own. She is a friendly girl who loves being with people and having the opportunity to explore on walks. She can be worried and is looking for a loving family to help her settled into her new home and build confidence.

name: Henry
description:
Henry is a fabulous, wriggy, bouncy boy! He is friendly and can live with children of primary school age as long as they’re happy with him and the spring in his step. He can also live with dogs provided they get on well during centre meets first.

Henry is a 3 year old Lurcher who came into our care through another charity. He’s a really sweet boy but we don’t know if he’s ever been in a home before. This means a lot of the basics are unknown, and he might benefit from some housetraining and other basic skills. He’ll jump into a car though, and was so happy on the back seat he didn’t want to leave when we hadn’t driven anywhere! Henry settles well in his kennel so we think he’ll be ok being left for a couple of hours once he’s settled in.

name: Apollo
description:
Apollo is a handsome boy and still just a youngster at 8 months old. He's on the search for home with fun and active adopters who can match his wonderful zest for life! Apollo LOVES his toys and chews, sometimes a little bit too much and he doesn't like to share. For this reason he needs a home with college aged children who are understanding and can learn to read his body language. Apollo is a clever boy and enjoys learning new things. Apollo has spent a few hours home alone, which could be gradually built up and has been housetrained. He's also social with other dogs, so could share his home with one following a meeting here at the centre and providing mealtimes are carefully managed. Apollo also has history of living with a cat previously, so could do again following gradual introductions.

Apollo is a wonderful lad and is always up for fun, adventure or learning new things. He would thrive in an active home where he can enjoy exploring new places and lots of fun exciting walkies. He's friendly meeting new people and enjoys a bum scratch too! It's important his new family are committed to his ongoing training and are happy to continue his education, but with his love of food we're sure he'll be the paw-fect student!

name: Tywin
description:
Sweet and loving boy Tywin is a 2 year old Shepherd cross with a heart of gold. He takes a little time to warm up to new people but once he has a bond with you, you have a friend for life. Once he knows and trusts you he is an absolute cuddle bug, if you give him a gentle scratch on his back he will lean into you for more. Tywin hasn’t really figured out toys yet, but he does love a quick zoom around followed by a good roll around like a total goof! This super cute guy is ready to find his new home.

Tywin is looking for a calm and predictable home with loving and understanding adopters who can take him on sniffy adventures, who will take the time to help him settle in and give him all the love and care he deserves. He is a sweet boy who finds the world rather overwhelming at times, so would like to live in an adult only home, if there is a quiet area in the home he can take himself off to the rest and relax, that would be the best. Tywin is a friendly boy who would be happy with polite and friendly walking buddies to help further build his confidence. Tywin is smart cookie and has picked up a few skills already, he is eager to engage in training in short, sweet sessions if he gets lots of praise and encouragement. He will need to be on a lead at all times in public so would like a home with a private, secure garden for him to have some quality off lead time pottering about in at his leisure with no worries or distractions. Tywin can be worried being left, so is looking for someone to be home the majority of the time to begin with, he can settle when provided with enrichment so could potentially be left in future up to 4 hours, any leaving time would need to be built up slowly once he has had time to settle into his new home. Tywin will need to meet his adopters multiple times prior to going home with potential home visits to make sure he is settling in ok, so please bear all of this in mind when applying.

name: Mabel
description:
Mabel is a very young and bouncy pup who could live with another dog who will be tolerant of her boisterous play, but no cats.  She could join a family with children of upper primary school age who will be confident around her giddiness!  Mabel is house trained and once settled could be left for around 4 hours, although she will likely need somebody at home to build this up gradually in her new environment.

Mabel is a sociable gal who loves to greet everybody out on her walks and is always up for making doggy pals to play with.  She loves her toys and will play fetch but will let you know when the game is over by taking her ball off for a wander instead!  Mabel already knows all of her basic training and has good recall.  She is a happy to travel in the car and is just waiting for a fun loving family to take her on adventures and enjoy life with.

name: Lydia
description:
Lydia is a beautiful and friendly girlie who is ready to find her paw-fect forever home. She is a big and bouncy girl, so is looking for a home with upper secondary aged children. Lydia has shown herself to be quite a social and we think she could share her new home with a calm, but playful dog following a meeting here at the centre. Lydia is super clever and is making lots of progress, but it's important her new family are committed to continuing this training and helping her learn lots of new things. She would thrive with an active family, with whom she can enjoy lots of new adventures.

Lydia is a fantastic girl who is sure to bring lots of love and fun to any family. She has been in a home previously where she was housetrained. Lydia is also happy to be left for up to 5 hours, which could be gradually built up as she settles into her forever home. This wonderful girlie will make such a fun, loving and affectionate member of the family.

name: Scout
description:
Meet Scout, a gorgeous 4.5-year-old Labrador X. Scout would love active adopters who can provide her with lots of mental and physical stimulation. She is looking for adopters who can continue working on Scout's dog socialisation and help her learn to be polite around other dogs. She has made amazing progress with our team and is looking to carry this on in her future home! She will need to be the only pet in the home, due to her dog reactivity, and can live with secondary-aged children. She is best suited in a neighbourhood where there won't be dogs or dogs/people walking by.

Scout is the best girl! She is very sweet and loves to have her favourite people around as much as she can. If you enjoy peaceful walks, she would make the perfect walking buddy. She absolutely adores going out on adventures and has lots of energy to burn off. She can be bouncy and loves getting her nose to the ground as much as she can. Scout knows her name and shows off a great sit and down. She would benefit from learning to keep all four paws on the floor. Scout enjoys her enrichment as well as any form of engaging training. Treats are the true way to Scout’s heart! Scout is a great girl who is sure to bring her forever family lots of joy! Apply to adopt today and favourite Scout!

name: Saffron
description:
Meet Saffron! At 8 years old she is the perfect combination of affectionate, gentle and adventurous. She has a super sweet nature and loves spending time with her favourite people. Saffron loves to go out for walks and explore the world around her then is happy to curl up for a snooze after. Saffron is friendly with new people and is a social dog, meaning she could live with a calm dog after successful meets here at the centre. Saffron is very food motivated, which will make continuing her training both enjoyable and rewarding.

If you are looking a settled dog who can also join you on adventures, Saffron may be the girl for you! She would love a quiet home that she can make her own. She would enjoy a garden to potter about in and a sofa to curl up on. Saffron could live in either an adult only home or a home with older dog-savvy children. If Saffron sounds like a good addition to your family, just fill in an application and don't forget to 'Favourite' her!

name: Coco
description:
Meet Coco!  When Coco first meets new people she can be a little unsure, but once she gets to know you, her lovely personality really shines through.  She is a friendly, affectionate and sweet girl who absolutely loves a fuss and being around people.  Coco is a very energetic, lively and giddy girl who loves life!  She has plenty of enthusiasm and would thrive in a home where she can enjoy lots of exercise, fun and attention.  She is also a strong girl on the lead, so her new family will need to be prepared to continue working with her and help her develop her walking skills.  Coco is looking for an active home where she can enjoy plenty of long walks, adventures and mental stimulation.  Alongside her physical exercise, she would really benefit from ongoing training and positive reinforcement to help her learn and channel all that wonderful staffie energy.  She will need a private secure garden.

Coco has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel she could potentially live with another dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Coco came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Oscar
description:
Meet Oscar! He is a lovely boy with a huge personality and plenty of puppyish energy!  Oscar is a very lively, energetic and friendly boy who is always ready for his next adventure.  He is a big puppy at heart – giddy, playful and full of enthusiasm and he loves being around people.  Oscar can be quite an excitable boy and does jump up, particularly when he is happy or excited.  He is also very vocal, so his new family should be prepared for a dog who likes to make his presence known!  Oscar has a very playful side.  When staff are cleaning his kennel, he thinks the hose pipe and brushes are fantastic toys and will chase them around.  His enthusiasm can sometimes get the better of him, so he will need patient guidance to learn more appropriate ways to channel his energy.  On walks, Oscar does pull on the lead and will need continued training to help him develop his loose-lead walking skills.  He would really benefit from an owner who enjoys training and can provide consistent positive reinforcement.  Oscar is looking for an active home where he can enjoy plenty of exercise, enrichment and mental stimulation.  He is not a couch-potato kind of boy!  His ideal family will enjoy getting out and about with him and be prepared to give him the time and training he needs to mature into a well-mannered adult.  His new adopter should be willing to work on his impulse control, socialisation and general training.  As a young Lurcher, Oscar will need patience, consistency and plenty of appropriate outlets for his energy.  Underneath all that excitement is a loveable, friendly and very giddy young boy who is still learning about the world.  He will need a private secure garden.

Oscar has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care and is very playful.  We do feel he could potentially be rehomed with another lively and energetic dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Oscar came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Rudy
description:
Meet Rudy!  Don’t let his age fool you, this lively, energetic boy has plenty of energy and enthusiasm. Rudy is a friendly, excitable and affectionate boy who absolutely loves attention and fuss.  He has a big personality and is not shy about letting you know when he wants you to interact with him!  Rudy can be quite vocal when he wants your attention or, more importantly, when he thinks it’s time for you to throw his ball.  One of Rudy’s favourite things is chasing his toys, and he could happily spend plenty of time playing and having fun.  He also enjoys his long walks and would love an active home who can provide him with plenty of exercise and opportunities to explore.  Rudy is a strong boy on the lead, so his new adopters will need to be confident handling him and willing to continue on his lead manners.  He does know his basic commands and, with the right guidance, could continue to build on these.  Rudy is looking for an active home where he can enjoy lots of walks, playtime and mental stimulation.  He would suit someone who enjoys getting out and about and is looking for a fun, lively companion with a larger-than-life personality.  Rudy will need a private secure garden.

Rudy has interacted well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel he could potentially be rehomed with another lively dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Rudy came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Gidget
description:
Gidget is a very lively and friendly pup. She loves to jump around for a fuss and doesn’t stay still. Gidget came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on her. She could also be a cross breed so could grow bigger than a standard border terrier. Terriers are known to have cheeky personalities so she needs a family that is happy to work with her and train her as she is growing up.

She is going to need an active family that can take her on lots of adventures to introduce her to the world. Due to her boisterous character she would be best suited to children who are 14 years and over – subject to a successful meet.

Gidget hasn’t met any dogs yet due to waiting for her vaccinations so will need to be introduced to dogs. She could potentially be rehomed with another dog that is happy to deal with her high energy levels – subject to a successful meet.

Please ensure that you have considered everything around owning a dog before applying for her, she is looking for a happy, loving forever home.

Please do not apply for Gidget if you are going on holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Baloo
description:
Baloo is looking for a very special home that understands his need for patience, space and trust.  Baloo is a very nervous boy and new people can be quite overwhelming for him.  When he first arrived with us, it took him a couple of weeks to start coming around, and initially he could be a little growly when he felt unsure or uncomfortable.  He is still wary of new people and can sometimes be very avoidant.  Fast movements can scare him, so everything needs to be taken slowly and calmly around him.  Baloo needs people who will allow him to approach in his own time, without pressure, and who understand that building a relationship with a nervous dog takes time and patience.  Once Baloo feels more comfortable, we get to see glimpses of the lovely boy underneath that uncertainty.  He really enjoys his off-lead time in our compound, where he loves running around and chasing his toys.  Seeing him relax and enjoy himself has been incredibly rewarding.  Baloo will need an adopter who is prepared to put time into building his trust and allow him to settle at his own pace.  We are looking for a Chow Chow breed experienced home where his behaviour and body language will be understood and respected.  Because of his nervous nature, several meet and greets will be required before adoption.  We want Baloo and his potential family to have plenty of opportunities to get to know one another and for trust to develop naturally.  Baloo isn’t going to be the dog who instantly runs up to you and asks for a cuddle.  He needs to earn your trust – slowly, quietly and on his terms.  But for the right person, watching a nervous dog begin to feel safe can be incredibly rewarding.  He will need a private secure garden.

Baloo has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, although he can be barky at times he seems more comfortable around quieter dogs but still very unsure. We feel he would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where his new adopter can commit to building up his confidence around other dogs in a controlled environment with lots of positive reinforcement.

As Baloo came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him and as he is a nervous boy we would prefer any children/visiting children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Poppy
description:
Meet Poppy!  She is looking for an active and loving forever home.  Poppy can be a little nervous when she first meets you, but once she gets to know you, her lovely, friendly personality really shines through.  She absolutely loves lots of fuss and of course tasty treats!  This is a very energetic and bouncy young girl who will need a home that can keep up with her.  An active family who enjoys plenty of walks, outdoor adventures and playtime would be ideal.  Breed experience would be an advantage, particularly for someone who understands the energy and needs of Husky type dogs.  Poppy loves running around our compound with her toys and will happily drop it for you to throw again.  She also has a funny, playful side – she likes playing in her water bowl and will happily spend time splashing about in it. Like any young dog, Poppy is still learning and will need continued patience, training and guidance.  She does know lots of commands, which is a fantastic starting point, although she can be strong on the lead and will need someone confident and capable of helping her improve her lead manners.  Poppy is also still working on her house training and does occasionally use her bed as a toilet, so her new adopter will need to be prepared to continue working with her patiently and positively.  Despite these little quirks, Poppy is a lovely, affectionate and fun-loving girl with so much potential.  She will need a private secure garden.

Poppy has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care and is very giddy and playful with them, so we feel following a successful meet and greet she could be rehomed with another dog of similar size and energy levels (must be neutered).

As Poppy came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 12+ years.

name: Hugo
description:
Hugo was found as a stray so we don’t have any background information about him. He has been a happy boy from the moment he arrived and loves all of the staff here. He is an extremely excitable and energetic boy with a big personality! He can be quite a handful pulling on his lead when he is out and about on walks, so will need a family that has the time and patience to help him work on his basic obedience and lead training. He will need an active home that can provide plenty of exercise, mental stimulation and enrichment to give him ways to express his enthusiasm. Hugo loves being off lead in our enclosed compound area zooming around and playing with toys.

He is taller than either of the breeds typically are, making him more of a medium sized dog. This should be taken into consideration before applying.

Hugo has interacted well with staff whilst in our care but due to his energy levels we believe it would be best for Hugo to be rehomed to an adult only home.

Hugo has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care so we believe that he could potentially be rehomed with another dog of a similar size and temperament – Subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Hero
description:
Hero is an ex racing greyhound who is now looking for his forever home with a family that can help him settle into life beyond the kennels. He is a confident, lively boy with plenty of personality. He gets very excited when it’s time for a walk and can jump around on the lead, so will need someone who is comfortable handling a tall strong greyhound. With a little training and consistency this is something that can be worked on. Although he is confident in many ways, he does need help building his confidence when it comes to being touched and handled as he can get a little worried.  Hero deserves the chance to learn, grow and discover just how good life can be outside of kennels.

Hero can be rehomed with mature children who are 16 years and over, due to his size and bouncy nature. This will be subject to a successful meet.

Hero is currently paired with another greyhound and has interreacted well with dogs whilst in our care, so we believe that he would be rehomed with another dog- subject to a successful meet and greet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Soul
description:
Soul is looking for a special home where she can begin the next chapter of her life. She has come straight from the racing kennels so has never lived in a home before so will need some training to help her adjust. Soul is a sweet, gentle girl who is happy to be fussed all over. She can be a little timid at first in new environments but soon comes around. Once she is in her new home everything is going to be new to her, so she will need a patient family who understands that she needs time to settle and build her confidence.  Once she is settled she has so much potential to blossom into a wonderful companion.

Soul is looking for a home with children who are 14+ who understand that she will need her own space and time to adjust to being in a home. This will be subject to a successful meet.

Soul is paired with another greyhound currently and has socialised well with other dogs in our care, we believe that she can be rehomed with another dog – Subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Bruce
description:
Meet gorgeous Bruce!  Bruce has had a very difficult start in life.  When he first came into our care, he was in a truly sorry state.  He was extremely thin, and his skin was in a terrible condition.  His body was bald, red and very inflamed, and it was clear that he had not had the care he desperately needed.  After lots of veterinary visits, treatment, time and plenty of TLC, we are so pleased to see the changes in him.  His fur is beginning to grow back, he is gaining weight, and he is slowly starting to feel better in himself.  Bruce is a very frightened and timid boy.  The world is a scary place for him, and he can be extremely nervous and shut down.  He will need someone who understands that building his confidence will not happen overnight.  However, once Bruce learns to trust you, you see a completely different side to him.  He is a very affectionate, playful and loving boy who enjoys being close to the people he feels safe with.  Bruce will need lots of time, patience, understanding and reassurance.  His new adopter must be prepared to give him the space he needs and allow him to progress at his own pace.  This could take some considerable time, and there may be setbacks along the way.  He is looking for an experienced owner who has previous experience with very nervous and fearful dogs and understands the commitment involved in helping a dog like Bruce learn that the world can be a safe place.  Bruce has already come such a long way, and we believe there is a wonderful, affectionate boy waiting to emerge as his confidence grows.  He deserves a quiet, patient and loving home where he can finally feel safe, secure and cherished.  The potential adopter must commit to multiple regular meet and greets for Bruce to get to know then before the adoption can take place.  He will need a private secure garden.

Bruce has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, he can be ok with some and very unsure around others, so we feel he would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where he can get 100% of the love and attention.

As Bruce is so timid we would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Frenchii
description:
Meet Frenchii.  When Frenchii first meets you, she can be nervous and unsure, so she will need a little time, patience and reassurance to feel comfortable.  Once she knows she is safe, her sweet personality really begins to shine.  Frenchii absolutely loves a fuss and attention and is a wonderfully affectionate little girl.  She has a gentle, loving nature and will happily soak up all the affection she can get.  She is also a real foodie! Treats and tasty snacks are definitely the way to her heart.  When she is feeling happy and settled, her playful side comes out too.  She loves getting her toys and having a good old zoomie around, and she can be quite giddy when she gets excited.  Frenchii would love a calm, patient home where her new family can give her the time she needs to build confidence and settle in at her own pace.

Frenchii has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel she could potentially be rehomed with another similar sized dog following a successful meet and greet.

As Frenchii came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her and as she can be a little nervous we would like any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Shep
description:
Shep is an older boy who is looking for a calm retirement home. Shep is an affectionate boy who roles over for belly rubs and paws at you for attention. He does have unusual eyes but that just adds to his charm. Shep needs a home with a family that has previous experience with herding breeds.

Shep needs an adult only home so that he can spend his golden years relaxing in a calm environment.

Shep can be a little unsure around certain dogs, usually big and boisterous dogs, but can interact well with smaller calm dogs. Due to this we feel that it would be best for Shep to be the only dog in the home. Shep would benefit from socialisation training to help his confidence.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Bear
description:
Bear is a very nervous boy when he meets new people for the first time. It takes a little while for him to come around but with patience and yummy treats he slowly starts to trust you. Once he has gained your trust and is comfortable he is an affectionate boy and loves to give out kisses. He will need to have multiple regular meets before going home.

Bear is a big dog who doesn’t understand his size, he is constantly jumping up for cuddles and doesn’t know what personal space is. Bear is going to require a lot of training to help him learn manners. He can be a very cheeky boy at times! He will need socialising in different environments and around people to help him build his confidence up. Bear gets super excited when going for walks and is very strong on the lead, this is another area that will need more training. Bear loves playing with his toys, splashing around in water and zooming around our enclosed area.

Bear is after an adult only home that has previous experience with big boisterous dogs. No regular visiting children either please. He is going to need a very active home with a family that is able to provide him with plenty of exercise and mental stimulation to keep him busy. As he is still only a young dog he can get up to mischief when he is bored. Bear’s new family need to be committed to putting in the training that he needs not only initially but keeping it up for the rest of his life.

Bear needs to be the only dog in the home so that he can have all of attention to help get him settled. Bear can interact well with dogs whilst out on walks but will need further training to help improve this.

We know that Bear is going to require a lot of work at first but once he is trained he will make a lovely family dog who will love going on plenty of adventures. Taking on a dog this size is a big commitment, please ensure that you are serious and have thought about the future before applying.

name: Heidi
description:
Heidi is a sweet girl who loves attention and a cuddle! She is very much a typical spaniel, full of energy and always ready for an adventure! She is going to need a very active home that has a lot of extra time to put in the training that she needs to become a well mannered girl. Heidi is still a young dog so can be very cheeky at times. Her new family will need to have Spaniel experience as the  behaviours she has been showing are typical to the breed. Heidi will need a lot of exercise and mental stimulation every day to keep her mind and body active and to prevent her from causing mischief. Heidi is going to require a lot of hard work to train her to become a great family dog but with time, patient and a lot of energy we believe that she will get there.

Heidi needs to be in an adult only home with no regular visiting children.

Heidi is a friendly girl and loves to meet dogs out and about on walks but we believe that she needs to be the only dog in the home so that her new family can focus on her training and she can get all of the attention she needs.

If you think that you can provide a patient and loving home for Heidi please apply today!

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Tuco
description:
This handsome boy is Tuco! (21kg)  He has a big personality and an even bigger zest for life!  This friendly lad loves meeting people and is always ready for his next adventure.  Tuco is full of energy and would thrive in an active family who can give him plenty of exercise, long walks, and exciting days out exploring.  Whether it’s hiking, woodland walks, or trips to the beach, Tuco will be your enthusiastic companion every step of the way.  In kennels, Tuco can be very vocal and loud, but this is just his way of expressing himself.  Once he’s out and spending time with people, his affectionate and loving nature really shines through.  As a young, energetic dog, Tuco still has a few manners to learn.  He can be quite strong on the lead and would benefit from continued training to improve his lead walking and learn some basic commands.  He can also be a little humpy when he’s over-excited, so his new adopter will need to be patient and consistent in helping him channel his enthusiasm in more appropriate ways.  Grooming isn’t Tuco’s favourite pastime, and he’s not particularly keen on being brushed, so this is something his new owner will need to work on gradually using positive reinforcement.  Tuco is a lovely boy with so much potential.  With the right active home, ongoing training, and plenty of love, he’s sure to grow into an amazing companion.  If you are looking for a fun-loving, energetic best friend to share life’s adventures with, Tuco could be the boy for you.  He will need a private secure garden.

Tuco has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, he can be a little unsure at first and does prefer a calmer female.  We do feel he could potentially be rehomed with another dog following a successful meet and greet.

As Tuco came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Ell
description:
Meet Ell!  She is looking for a loving home where she can continue to build her confidence.  When you first meet Ell, she can be very nervous and timid.  New people and unfamiliar situations can be overwhelming for her, but once she knows and trusts you, her sweet personality begins to shine.  She simply needs an experienced, patient owner who will give her time and space to settle at her own pace.  Once she’s comfortable, Ell is incredibly friendly and affectionate.  She loves belly rubs and enjoys lots of fuss.  She’s not particularly interested in toys, but she does love exploring the world and having a good sniff on walks.  In kennels, Ell can be very vocal, so she will need understanding neighbours and owners who appreciate that she may bark at first but this is just her way of expressing herself.  She can sometimes be a bit growly when she’s at the vets, but this is fear-related, and she benefits from calm, gentle handling during stressful situations.  Ell is currently carrying a little extra weight, so her new adopter will need to help her on a healthy weight-loss journey with sensible exercise and a balanced diet.  This will help improve her overall health and wellbeing.  Ell is looking for a kind, patient home that will see past her initial nerves and give her the chance to blossom. She would benefit from a private secure garden.

Ell has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, she can be a bit barky around them so we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where she can continue to learn her manners around other dogs in a controlled environment with lots of positive reinforcement. This barking behaviour has only started over the last couple of weeks so it could be frustrations of being in a kennel environment.

As Ell came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her and as she can be a little nervous we would like any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Ripley
description:
Meet Ripley!! He is a gorgeous boy looking for an active, committed home where he can continue to learn and thrive.  He’s a friendly, affectionate boy with a fun-loving personality and is always ready for a game with his favourite toys.  He is full of energy and loves to play, so he will need an active family who can provide plenty of exercise, enrichment, and ongoing training.  Like many young dogs, he can become a little mouthy and nippy when he’s excited, so he will benefit from patient guidance and positive reinforcement to help him learn appropriate manners.  He is still working on his basic commands and will need someone willing to continue his training.  He can also occasionally rag his lead, so further lead training will be important.  Previous experience with Shar-pei’s would be a real advantage, as they can have their own unique characteristics and training needs.  He currently has a cherry eye, which will be surgically repaired before he goes to his new home, so he’ll be ready to start his next chapter feeling his best.  If you’re looking for a playful, lively young dog and have to time and commitment to help him become the wonderful companion we know he can be, Ripley could be the boy for you.

Ripley has socialised well with other dogs and is very playful with them.  He can sometimes get frustrated and bark if he can’t get to them straight away.  We feel he could potentially be rehomed with another playful dog of similar size following a successful meet and greet.

As Ripley came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him and as he can be a little nippy when over-excited we would like any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Morgan
description:
Morgan came into our care through no fault of his own. Due to him being a rehome we do have some knowledge of what he was like in the home and he is already toilet trained. Morgan is a very friendly boy and loves to say hello to everyone he meets. Morgan spends most of his day relaxing on his comfy bed surrounded by his fluffy toys, which he likes to show off. Morgan is currently on a weight loss journey and will need to continue this when he goes home. Morgan is after a loving retirement home where he can spend his days lounging on his own comfy sofa. Morgan loves to go out for little walks and lots of sniffs!

Morgan can be rehomed with children who are 16 years and over – subject to a successful meet.

Morgan needs to be the only dog in the house as he is after a peaceful and calm retirement home.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3 months.

name: Bob
description:
Bob is a sweet and friendly boy. When Bob first came into our care he was very nervous but during his time with us he has built up his confidence massively. Once bob is comfortable his goofy personality soon comes out, he loves to play with his toys and all of the staff here. Bob loves his walks, due to his size he can be strong on the lead but with a little more training that would improve. Bob loves his treats and enrichment activities in between walks. Bob is a clever boy as he already knows a few tricks such as sit, down and paw. Bob will need continuous training to help with his socialisation skills.

Bob needs an adult only home where he can have plenty of space to settle in and gain more confidence. He will need an experienced home that has had large breed dogs before and can handle his size and boisterous behaviour once he is settled.

Bob has interacted well with dogs whilst in our care, he is still only young so he does like to bounce around and try and play with dogs. Further training is needed to help him improve his manners. Bob could potentially be rehomed with another dog – subject to a successful meet.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Arlo
description:
Meet Arlo! Arlo is a gorgeous, sweet-natured boy who is very friendly and absolutely loves lots of fuss.  He’s a real people dog and enjoys getting plenty of attention and affection.  He is a very energetic and boisterous lad who can get extremely giddy when he’s excited.  He sometimes forgets just how big he is and will jump up to say hello, so he would benefit from some basic training to help him learn his manners and channel all that enthusiasm.  Arlo recently had a bath, and although he was a little nervous to begin with, he was a very good boy.  Once it was all over, he celebrated in true Arlo style with a case of the zoomies!  He also has a funny habit of rearranging his bed and moving it to wherever he thinks it should be.  Arlo is a loveable, fun, lively character with bags of personality.  He would thrive in a very active home with someone who can give him plenty of exercise, long walks and consistency with his training.  He would need a private secure garden so he can practice his zoomies!

Arlo has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care and is very playful, so we feel following a successful meet and greet he could live with another dog of similar size and energy level.

As Arlo came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Tara
description:
Meet Tara!  This gorgeous girl is looking for an active, understanding home where she can continue to grow in confidence and enjoy everything life has to offer.  When Tara first meets new people or finds herself in unfamiliar situations, she can be nervous and unsure and may need a little time and patience to feel comfortable.  Once she gets to know you, though, her affectionate personality really starts to shine.  She is a friendly and loving girl who enjoys being around people she trusts.  Tara is still very much a youngster and is playful, energetic and full of enthusiasm.  She would love an active home with people who can give her plenty of exercise, playtime and positive mental stimulation.  She already knows some basic commands and is keen to learn, but she will benefit from continued training to help her become the best version of herself.  Tara can also be strong on the lead, so her new adopters will need to be comfortable handling her and willing to continue working on her lead manners.  Most importantly, Tara needs adopters who will give her the time, patience and reassurance she needs to build her confidence.  With consistent, positive training and a secure home, we feel this affectionate young girl has so much potential.  She will need a private secure garden.

Tara has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care.  She can be nervous initially and is then very jumpy and boisterous with them, with no off switch, so we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where her adopters can work with her on her manners around other dogs.

As Tara came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Star
description:
Star is a typical Patterdale Terrier who is always raring to go! She loves being outdoors, exploring new smells and trying to chase any wildlife she comes across. Star would love a fully enclosed garden where she can enjoy plenty of secure off-lead time and burn off some of her energy. Terrier or Patterdale experience would be beneficial, as she can have her cheeky moments and will need a family who understands her spirited nature.

We have found that Star struggles when left alone, so her new family will need to be around for much of the time. She will need someone who has the time, patience and commitment to help her settle into her new life and feel comfortable in a home environment. As Star was found as a stray, we don’t have much background information about her. However, we know she is an energetic, characterful girl who will thrive with the right family, plenty of exercise and lots of love.

Star may require multiple meets so she can get to know her new family before going home. Her new family will need to be patient and understanding whilst she is settling in and getting used to her new surroundings.

We think that it is best for Star to be rehomed to an adult only home.

Star has interacted well with other dogs but can be very vocal so can potentially be rehomed with another dog of a similar temperament – subject to a successful meet.

We wouldn’t recommend Star to be rehomed with cats due to her breed.

Please do not apply for a dog if you have a holiday within the next 3  months.

name: Ziggy
description:
Ziggy is full of life  and energy as he is a young boy. He is a super friendly boy, with a big personality and absolutely loves playing in our enclosed area chasing balls around. At times Ziggy can get a little mouthy and will need his new family to continue helping him learn manners. With Ziggy still being young and high energy, he would need an active home who are able to give him the exercise he needs along with mental stimulation.

Whilst in our care Ziggy has socialised really well with other dogs and often enjoys his daily walks alongside them. For this reason, we do believe he could potentially live with another dog, able to keep up with his high energy levels – subject to a successful meet.

Ziggy wouldn’t be suitable to live with cat or any small animals.

Due to Ziggy coming into our care as a stray, we don’t have any previous history on him. Ziggy would be best suited to an experienced home, ideally having knowledge of his breed, with children no younger than 16 years old – subject to a successful meet.

name: Lyra
description:
Meet Lyra!  This beautiful girl is looking for an active, experienced home where she can thrive.  She is a lovely, sweet-natured girl with a very giddy and playful personality.  Lyra absolutely loves attention and fuss and is always happy to be involved in whatever is going on.  She has lots of enthusiasm for life and certainly isn’t shy about showing it! Lyra can jump up quite a lot when she gets excited, so this is something her new adopter will need to be prepared to work on.  She is also very strong on the lead and will need someone confident and capable of handling her while they continue training.  As you would expect from a Malinois, Lyra is an active, energetic dog who will need plenty of physical exercise, mental stimulation and ongoing training and socialisation.  Due to the needs and characteristics of the breed previous knowledge and experience of the breed or similar high-drive working breeds is required. Underneath all that energy is an incredibly sweet girl who loves affection and companionship. She will need a private secure garden.

Lyra has socialised well with other dogs, and is very giddy and playful with them.  We do feel she could potentially live with another dog of similar size and energy levels following a successful meet and greet. (must be neutered).

As she came into the home as a stray, we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Elias
description:
Elias is a very sweet and friendly boy. He came into our care as a stray so we don’t have any background information on him. He has always been friendly with staff and volunteers whilst here. Elias can be a little strong on the lead due to his size so some basic lead training would be beneficial for him. We are looking for an active home for Elias as he has a lot of energy and would enjoy going on lots of adventures. Elias is a calm boy in his kennel and loves to have some down time with a tasty chew.

Elias is a friendly boy but due to his size we believe that it would be best for him to be rehomed with children over 14 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

Elias needs a little more training around dogs since his castration as he has become a little unsure, therefore we believe that Elias would benefit from being the only dog in the home as he would prefer all the attention on him.

name: Jasper
description:
Jasper is an ex-racing greyhound that has spent all of his life in kennels. Jasper is now ready for a comfortable and cosy forever home to call his own. Jasper is a friendly and loveable boy who likes attention and a cuddle. Jasper has a high prey drive still so does pull when he sees ducks, birds and wildlife when out on walks. Jasper has never lived in a home before so he will need time to settle and get used to unfamiliar sounds and objects.

Jasper has interacted well with dogs and is currently paired with another greyhound so we believe that he can be rehomed with another dog of a similar size – Subject to a successful meet.

Jasper is a sweet boy so can potentially be rehomed with children who are 12 years and over – Subject to a successful meet.

name: Dakota
description:
Dakota is looking for her forever home, and she has so much love to give.  She’s an incredibly sweet, friendly girl who absolutely adores people.  If you’re happy to give her plenty of fuss, she’ll be in her element!  Despite her size, she is a gentle soul with a lovely nature and enjoys spending time with her favourite humans.  She already knows some basic commands and is very eager to please so would benefit from further training.  Being a young, strong dog, she can be powerful on the lead, so her new adopter will need to be confident and committed to continue her lead training.  Because of this, she will be best suited to an active home where she can enjoy plenty of exercise, adventures and mental stimulation.  If you are looking for a loyal, affectionate companion with a heart as big as she is, this lovely girl could be the one for you.  She will need a private secure garden.

She has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, and is very playful and can be too much for other dogs as she does get in their face so for this reason we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home where she can continue to learn manners and boundaries around other dogs will the full support of her new adopter with lots of positive reinforcement.

As Dakota came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 14+ years.

name: Jax
description:
This stunning boy is Jax! we are looking for an experienced home for this fantastic lad.  He is a friendly and affectionate boy who absolutely loves attention and enjoys a good fuss.  He has a wonderful nature and is always happy to spend time with his people. This clever lad is exceptionally well behaved at the vets, taking examinations and handling in his stride, which is a testament to his temperament and trainability.  Like many dogs, he has his own little quirks – one of his favourites is enthusiastically ragging his blankets and rearranging them to his liking!  As a typical Belgian Malinois, he is highly intelligent, energetic and thrives on both physical exercise and mental stimulation.  He loves charging around our compound and would be happiest in a home where he has plenty of opportunities to stay active and engaged.  Because of his breed traits, he will need an owner who has previous experience with Belgian Malinois and understands their needs.  He is not a dog that will be content with a short walk around the block, he requires ongoing training, enrichment and a lifestyle that allows him to use both his body and brain.  He will need a private secure garden.

Jax was rehomed but sadly has been returned to us as his prey drive was too much for his new owners. He cannot be rehomed with cats or small furries.  He will need an owner that has previous experience with large breed high prey dogs.

He has socialised well with other dogs whilst in our care, so we feel he could possibly be rehomed with another dog (similar size) following a successful meet and greet.

As Jax came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on him so would prefer any children in the home to be 16+ years.

name: Cali
description:
Cali was a very nervous girl when she first arrived at the home, which was over 200 days now! It has taken a lot of time for staff and volunteers to get to know Cali and bring out her excitable, bubbly personality. Cali loves going for walks and off lead runs in our compound area, she will always be found with a football in her mouth. She loves to dodge past you whilst you try and catch her, her tail never stops wagging. Cali loves her treats and sits nicely whilst you give them to her. She has been toilet trained whilst in our care, which is a bonus for when she goes home.

Cali can be strong on the lead at times due to her excitement to get outside and enjoy the fresh air but can walk nicely after her initial excitement is over, especially on a harness. Cali would love a fully enclosed garden with someone around most of the time so that she can come and go as she pleases. Cali spends most of her day relaxing on a comfy bed watching people come and go. She can be a little barky in her kennel at first but this is due to her wanting to say hello to everyone.

Cali isn’t a cuddly kind of girl but would love a family that is willing to keep her entertained and will play with her toys. We believe that Cali needs to be in an adult only home, with a family that has experience with rescue dogs or bull breeds.

Cali was nervous of dogs when she first came into our care so we think that it is best that she is the only dog in the house. With a lot of socialisation she now is a friendly girl that is happy to say hello to most dogs that she meets.

We think that it would be best for Cali to not be in a house with cats.

If you think you can give this gorgeous girl her forever home please apply!

name: Pearl
description:
This talkative girl is Pearl.  She is a very affectionate, confident and friendly girl that is always up for lots of fuss and strokes.  She can be very vocal when she wants your attention so probably not suitable for an apartment/flat.  She enjoys her walks everyday having a sniff about and saying hello to everyone she meets.  She is very strong on the lead so will need an experienced owner that is used to powerful dogs. Pearl would benefit from a private secure garden.

Pearl has socialised with other dogs whilst in our care, she can be a little unsure at first but does come around after a bit, so we feel she may be best suited as the only dog in the home where she can take her time getting used to other dogs with lots of positive reinforcement from her new adopter.

As Pearl came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer any children in the home to be 12+ years.

name: Willow
description:
This stunning girl is Willow.  Willow was very nervous and unsure for the first few weeks she was with us.  She was very vocal when the staff went in her kennel and would hide in the back.  The staff have worked hard with her to gain her trust and she has come out of her shell now and is showing her playful friendly side.  We are looking for an experienced owner for Willow that have had nervous large breed dogs previously and will work with her on her confidence, doing this at Willow’s pace and not too rushed.  She is a very independent girl who will come to you when she wants some attention, her toys are her number 1 priority in life.  Willow is very food orientated and will sit nicely for her treats.  This said she is a little bit chunky at the moment so is on weight management food to help her loose a few pounds, and well done to Willow and the staff as she has managed to lose 3kg up to now!  She will need continued training and socialisation. Willow will benefit from a private secure garden where she can have off lead time to relax and have a sniff about.

Willow has socialised ok with other dogs whilst in our care but we feel she would be best rehomed as the only dog in the home as she does prefer her own space.

As Willow came into the home as a stray we have no previous history on her so would prefer an adult only household.

name: Bruce
description:
Bruce is a very active and playful boy who absolutely loves chasing around our compound with his toys.  He can be quite boisterous and bouncy when he is excited so would definitely benefit from continued training and socialisation. He can be quite a strong boy on his lead too.

He will need an active home where he can get all the exercise and mental stimulation he will need every day. Bruce would benefit from a private secure garden where he can have off lead time with his toys in between his walks.

Bruce has interacted well with most dogs whilst in our care but can be very dominant with them so we feel he would be best suited to be the only dog in the home.  The new adopter will need to continue his socialisation with other dogs to improve his interactions with them.

As Bruce can get nervous and overwhelmed meeting new people, especially men, we feel that it would be best for him to go to an adult only home. He will need time to get to know you before going home. His new family will need to be able to commit to multiple meets.

Bruce is a wonderful, vibrant boy with lots of love to give to his new family! He has spent a while in kennels now so would love to find his forever home and someone to be the person to throw his ball endlessly! Do you think this could be you?

name: Pandora
description:
I need a calm and quiet home & I can live with teens, aged 16+.

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and harness will enjoy to go for walks with my new family.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Pandora has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she arrived, she was a scared little girl who was worried to find herself here but was trying incredibly hard to be brave. Since then, she has really come out of her shell and is blossoming into the sweetest little girl.

She recently moved to a wonderful foster home where she is getting to experience home life for the very first time and is settling in so well and now absolutely loves having a fuss and attention. She gets on very well with the other dogs in foster, but especially loves the humans! She sleeps soundly all night with the other dogs and is happy to be left for a few hours.

Pandora will be looking for a calm and quiet home and would benefit from adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need love and TLC as she settles into her new home. She loves other dogs and would love to have another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend, but in the right circumstances and with adopters who are around most of the time, we would consider homing her as an only dog. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

She had never lived in a home before moving to foster, so everything is still fairly new to her and she will need kindness and patience as she continues learning about home life and new skills like house training. She can now walk well on a lead and harness and enjoys her walks and adventures so would benefit from an active home. She has even visited a secure field, which she loved! She will need a secure garden with 6ft fences.

Our vets have noted that she has a Grade 1 heart murmur, which doesn't require any medication but will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet going forward. She also came to us with a fluid-filled swelling on the side of her face, which our vets diagnosed as a salivary mucocele. This occurs when a salivary gland becomes damaged, allowing saliva to leak into the surrounding tissue, where it collects and forms a soft, usually painless, pocket of fluid. Our vets have drained this, however it has started to gradually refill again and may need to be drained again in the near future. The only permanent treatment is surgery to remove the affected salivary gland, which would need to be carried out by a specialist. Pandora's adopters would need to be aware that any vet treatment surrounding this would not be coverable by insurance as it's pre-existing.

Pandora has been given the Gift of Life by Lynne Hughes

Pandora has been here for a week and I feel like she has always lived here. She really is an incredibly sweet girl who just lights up a room. She has so much love to give.

She sleeps in kitchen all night and is happy to be left for a few hours in the crate. She LOVES food and being fussed and is just everything you would expect a Labradoodle to be.

She loves being out in my secure field and happily came and found me for a fuss. She also travels well.

She plays nicely with all the dogs, even the small pupster but is not dependent on them. Pandora just simply wants to be loved!

Pandora has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She is a scared little girl who is worried to find herself here at the moment, but she is trying ever so hard to be brave. If approached slowly and gently, Pandora is happy to enjoy a little fuss and is beginning to show what a sweet girl she is.

Pandora is looking for a calm and quiet home and would benefit from adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need plenty of time, patience and reassurance as she settles into her new life. She gains confidence from the company of other dogs and will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help show her the way. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who are sensible and will allow her time to settle in at her own pace.

Having never lived in a home before, everything will be new to Pandora and her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she learns all about home life. She will need help with house training. She walks well on a harness but it is advised to initially further practice around the safety of the garden to help build her confidence. She will need an extra secure fence of at least 6ft to ensure her safety.

Although Pandora is not yet walking on a lead, we feel she will be best suited to an active home where, once she has gained confidence and learned all about the world around her, she will be able to enjoy lots of adventures with her family. With time, patience and the support of her doggy friend, we are sure Pandora will blossom into a wonderful companion.

Our vets have noted that she has a Grade 1 heart murmur, which doesn't require any medication but will need to be monitored by her adopters and their vet going forward. She also came to us with a fluid-filled swelling on the side of her face, which our vets diagnosed as a salivary mucocele. This occurs when a salivary gland becomes damaged, allowing saliva to leak into the surrounding tissue, where it collects and forms a soft, usually painless, pocket of fluid. Our vets have drained this and it has remained stable so far. However, it is likely to gradually refill over the coming weeks or months and would need to be drained again if this happens. The only permanent treatment is surgery to remove the affected salivary gland, which would need to be carried out by a specialist. Pandora's adopters would need to be aware that any vet treatment surrounding this would not be coverable by insurance as it's pre-existing.
