name: Clippa
description:
I’d like an active home home filled with love and kindness!

I can be an only dog or live with others. No cats or small furries please!

I would love a secure garden with 6ft+ fences that I can run and play in!

I walk on a lead but need some training as I'm strong and can pull.

I did have some separation anxiety which my fosterers have worked on.

I have been spayed! Please read below for more information.

Clippa is a wonderful girl who came to us from a breeder in search of a fresh start. From the moment she arrived, she showed us what a loving and affectionate little girl she is. Whilst in our care at the rescue, Clippa quickly became a favourite with staff and volunteers thanks to her happy nature and love of human attention. She adored going out on walks with volunteers, loved exploring the Welsh countryside and was always happiest when she was close to people getting cuddles and fuss. She also got on brilliantly with her kennel friends and enjoyed the company of other dogs.

She has now moved to a foster home where she has continued to blossom and has settled beautifully into home life. On arrival, she immediately made it her mission to explore every single inch of the garden, showing just how adventurous and inquisitive she is! Because of this, she will need a very secure garden with minimum 6ft fencing as she is an active little spaniel who loves to investigate everything around her.

We think that Clippa is a bit hard of hearing and doesn't hear human voices easily. This doesn't slow her down, but, for this reason future adopters will need to be aware that she will likely need to be on lead for her walks and be let off only in secure fields to keep her safe.

Clippa is an incredibly affectionate and people orientated dog who absolutely adores human company. Visitors are instantly greeted by Clippa demanding cuddles, belly rubs and attention, and she will happily snuggle into you whenever given the opportunity. Although she enjoys playing with polite dogs and gets on wonderfully with the resident dogs in foster, people will always be her favourite. When first in foster she did experience some separation anxiety, her fosterers have already worked hard on building her confidence and independence, and her future adopters will need to continue this, gradually building up the time she is left.

She has taken to home life brilliantly and despite having never lived in a home before, she has been clean around the house, with no accidents indoors. She settles beautifully overnight and loves curling up somewhere warm and cosy with her foster family. In fact, she gets so comfortable at bedtime that convincing her to go outside for her final toilet trip can sometimes be a challenge!

Clippa absolutely LOVES her walks and thrives on getting out and exploring the world around her. She would love an active home that understands the busy, intelligent and inquisitive nature of spaniels and can provide her with plenty of mental and physical stimulation. She already walks well on lead most of the time, although she can sometimes be strong and excitable when out and about. At the moment, her recall is non-existent in secure fields as she is far too busy exploring to pay attention, so her adopters will need to be committed to continuing her training with this.

She could happily be homed as an only dog as long as her adopters were around most of the time and had plenty of time to spend with her, but she could also be homed with another kind and playful resident dog. She could live with gentle dog savvy teenagers but cannot live with cats or small furries.

Clippa arrived in our care with bilateral conjunctivitis which responded very well to treatment and continues to be monitored. She also had one tooth removed at the time of her spay.

Clippa is such a happy, loving and affectionate little girl who has embraced her new life with enthusiasm. Whether she is out exploring, making new friends, or snuggled up for cuddles, she throws herself wholeheartedly into everything she does. We think she will make an absolutely wonderful companion for a very lucky family.

Clippa has been given the Gift of Life by Carol Unsworth

Clippa is the friendliest girl that we have ever fostered. All she wants to do is be with you for cuddles. She has been clean in the house from day 1 and sleeps soundly all night in her bed in our bedroom (although she does like to see if you are awake at 5:30am in case you can give her early breakfast!) She also gets super excited for her bedtime snack routine.Despite her age, Clippa still has quite a lot of pep in her step and LOVES going on long walks and exploring the local countryside, woods and beaches that we have local to us. She is also a huge tennis ball fan! Although Clippa isn't particularly strong, she is very 'busy' so will need someone that can handle her to let her 'Spaniel' to her full potential.Clippa gets on really well with our 2 dogs and likes to snuggle with our Labrador but we also think that she could be an only dog for someone that is around most of the time and willing to build up being left gradually.We think that Clippa is a bit hard of hearing and doesn't hear human voices easily. For this reason future adopters will need to be aware that she will likely need to be on lead for her walks and be let off only in secure fields.Clippas perfect adopters would be someone who is home most of the time, loves snuggly dogs and going for long walks. Some experience of gundog breeds would be useful.

Clippa has now moved into foster and is settling in brilliantly! On arrival, she made it her mission to explore every inch of the garden, so she will definitely need a very secure garden with a minimum of 6ft fencing as she is an adventurous and inquisitive girl.

She has settled beautifully into home life and gets on really well with the resident dogs, although her true preference is definitely humans! Every visitor is instantly greeted by Clippa demanding cuddles, belly rubs and attention. She is such a happy, affectionate little girl who absolutely adores people.

Clippa LOVES her walks and exploring the world around her. She would thrive in an active home that understands the busy, inquisitive nature of spaniels and can keep both her mind and body stimulated. She enjoys playing with polite dogs too, but people will always be her favourite.

At the moment, Clippa has zero recall in secure fields and is far too busy exploring to pay any attention to you! She will need lots of training and practice with this before potentially being allowed off lead and her adopters must be prepared to put the work in.

She has met older children calmly and could be homed with kind and gentle, dog savvy teenagers. She has taken everything in her stride. Around the home she is very clean, has never had a single accident indoors, and settles beautifully overnight sleeping upstairs in the bedroom. In fact, she gets so cosy at bedtime that getting her outside for her final toilet trip can be a challenge and her Foster Dad often has to carry her out because she doesn’t want to leave her warm snuggle spot!

Meal times can sometimes be entertaining as Clippa tends to take a bite, wander off to investigate something else, then come back for another bite as there is always something more exciting to check out! Her absolute favourite things in life are walkies, cheese, and snuggling up with Foster Daddy.

Since arriving in foster, Clippa has decided she loves people so much that she finds being away from them difficult, even for 30 seconds. Her fosterers are already working on her separation anxiety with her and gradually increasing the time she is left, but any future adopters will need to continue working with her and making this a priority with patience, consistency and understanding.

Clippa is an absolute angel girl. She is lovely and affectionate and will snuggle right in for cuddles. Clippa also loves going on long walks and meeting new people.

This week Clippa has been enjoying the sunshine at the rescue, and has been out on some super walks with our lovely volunteers and having plenty of sniff time in our play yards.

Clippa would love a home where she will be able to join in on all the family adventures and have plenty of cuddles.

Clippa is an absolutely lovely Springer Spaniel who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is a very affectionate girl who loves human company and will happily snuggle right into you for a cuddle.

Clippa gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends and enjoys their company, so would be happy to share her home with another kind resident dog. She is also confident enough that we would consider homing her as an only dog in the right circumstances, as long as her adopters were around most of the time. She couldn't be homed with cats or small furries. We would consider homing her with dog savvy teenagers.

As Clippa has never lived in a home before, she will need support with house training and learning the basics of home life. With her friendly and affectionate nature, she is likely to enjoy this learning process with her new family.

Clippa can already walk on a lead and enjoys getting out and about, though she can be a little strong at times and can pull, so she will benefit from ongoing guidance and gentle training to help her with her lead manners. She would love to find an active home where she can go on lots of walks and adventures!

Clippa arrived with bilateral conjunctivitis which is already looking much better following veterinary care and will continue to be monitored. She has had 1 tooth removed at the time of her spay.

Clippa is a loving, affectionate girl who clearly enjoys being close to people and other dogs and we think that she will make a wonderful companion!

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Trixie
description:
I'll need an adult only home with adopters with experience of ex-breeding dogs.

I am looking for a home where I can be the only dog & get all the love and attention.

I need an extra secure garden and home that can accommodate my needs.

I walk on a lead but will need my adopters to be extra secure.

I understand toilet training, but will need a reminder in a new home!

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home! Read below for more info!

Trixie is an amazing little lady who came to us from a breeder. She found kennel life quite overwhelming at first and took some time to settle in, but she has gradually grown in confidence and is now beginning to let her wonderful personality shine. Once Trixie learns to trust you, she becomes incredibly affectionate and loves nothing more than being close to her favourite people. She will happily climb into your lap for cuddles and enjoys soaking up as much attention as possible.

Trixie spent some time in a foster home, where she began to experience life in a home environment. This helped to build her confidence and allowed her to start learning that the world isn't such a scary place. Despite the progress she has made, she will still need time to adjust and would much prefer a calm, quiet home without too much hustle and bustle, allowing her to settle at her own pace and build a strong bond with her new family.

Trixie has returned to the rescue after we discovered that she would be happiest as the only dog in the home. Since returning, it has been lovely to see her personality continue to blossom. She enjoys spending time with other dogs in the yard and gets very excited to see her canine friends each day. She is happy to socialise with calm dogs while out and about, but within the home she can become jealous when attention is shared and has occasionally reacted towards other dogs.

For this reason, Trixie will need a home where she is the only pet, with no resident dogs or cats. She will also need an adult-only home with adopters who understand the needs of ex-breeding dogs and can give her the time, patience, and one-to-one attention she truly deserves.

In the garden, she displayed digging behaviours and has previously tried to escape a foster home, so very secure boundaries are essential. Her new home will need to have 6ft minimum fencing height and her new adopters will need to keep her on lead in the garden until she gains confidence outside. Trixie had been mostly clean in the house in her foster home, and seemed to be a star at toilet training. However, she may need some reminders in her new home as she settles in new surroundings. She is walking on a lead and harness, but can still become startled and may try to back out if frightened.

She has had a small lump removed from her left mammary gland and is recovering well.

Trixie has been given the Gift of Life by Tanya Player

Hello, my name is Trixie and I'm living at Many Tears whilst I wait for my forever home to find me.

My perfect home would be with lovely, gentle people, that enjoy a quiet life. I am easily worried by new sounds and loud noises and so I will need lots of time to adjust to my new home and environment. I love a squishy bed to lie on and one of those sofas I hear about sounds perfect to try.

I would be very happy in a secure garden where I won’t be bothered by other people, just my family, sitting with me and a few toys for little plays. Perhaps when I get used to my new people we could go for walks in quiet places together - but I will need time before I’m fully ready to do this.

I enjoy my food, so a good supply of tasty meals would make me very happy. I really don’t want much just a simple, safe and loving home.

Side note from my kennel mum:Trixie is a wonderful loving dog once she feels safe with you. She is a flight risk when startled - and she is easily startled!

If every day was a Trixie day, life would be lovely. Trixie is the sweetest and loveliest of dogs. Her favourite pastimes include tummy rubs and cuddles, and if there’s a home out there with a Trixie-sized spot on the sofa and a human to shower her with fusses, she would be in heaven.

When Trixie is happy, you know it, and she will bounce around you outside for a little play before parking herself next to you for more belly rubs. She loves sitting outside and just relaxing with you.

Trixie does also enjoy a walk (in very quiet areas); however, she can be very, very easily spooked and, if startled, will bolt and has done so previously. Any adopters would need to be very aware of this and work on building her confidence at home before considering outings. Adopters will also need to ensure a very secure setup for her at home, i.e. secure entrances and exits from the house.

Trixie prefers to have a human all to herself and, for this reason, she would like to be the only dog with a human who will be home most of the time.

Trixie truly is a gem of a girl with a heart of gold. A special and sweet lady, who longs for safe hands (and laps) to snuggle into. This super dog needs a little time and a lot of security,  give her that and you will have a bond for life.

Trixie is looking for a home that is quiet, gentle, patient and super secure on a practical level. Trixie is incredibly spooky and even if she trusts you, the slightest of frights in her environment and she will bolt. Because Trixie is a high flight risk she would be suited to a dog experienced home, ideally with knowledge of flighty and/or ex-breeding dogs.

It’s important that her new people have a secure plan for getting her out of the car on arrival home after adoption and are able to keep entrance and exits to the house escape safe. In return for your kindness Trixie will be the cutest of best friends. Trixie is looking to be the only dog and is suited to an adult home with no visiting children.

Trixie has been in foster with me for three weeks now and is settling into our routine fairly well.

When she first arrived, Trixie was very human-oriented and showed signs of jealousy towards other dogs, which led to a few altercations. She would often growl if another dog came close to me, as she wanted all the attention for herself. This is something we’ve been working on, but we still feel it is best if she is homed as an only dog in her new home.

From her interactions with my resident dogs, it’s clear that Trixie isn’t comfortable with small, yappy dogs. She does seem to prefer female human company, although she is continuing to build confidence more generally. She currently sleeps downstairs in an open, covered crate, which she uses as her safe space.

For the first couple of weeks, Trixie has slept downstairs quietly through the night with no accidents. Over the last few nights, she has been a little more unsettled and has had a couple of accidents, which seems to be linked to wanting more human attention.

Trixie is fed on dry Arden Grange and is currently fed separately, as she will try to eat other dogs’ food if given the chance. She was also caught eating poo, so I have started soaking her food in hot water and letting it cool, which she seems to prefer.

In her first week, Trixie did try digging in the garden and looking for ways to escape, but this behaviour has now settled. She clearly recognises me and gets very excited when she sees me, running over happily for fuss and attention.

She has been out on walks and does reasonably well when accompanied by another dog, but she is still quite flighty and easily startled. For now, she should only be walked in secure areas, as she will try to back out of her harness if she feels unsure and has demonstrated this once already.

Trixie can be complex at times, so she will need a calm, experienced adopter who understands nervous, ex-breeding dogs and can handle her with patience and care. It will be important to give her time to settle at home and build trust before introducing too many new experiences, especially.

Trixie absolutely craves human attention and is happiest curled up next to me on the sofa. As her confidence continues to grow and her jealousy is managed, she has all the makings of a very loyal and loving companion who simply wants to feel safe and adored.

Trixie is now in foster and is settling in well. She travelled well and was clean on arrival with no issues noted in the car or on entering the home.

Once in the foster home, Trixie has shown herself to be a very nervous little girl who is still unsure of new environments and needs encouragement to engage with people. She will often hang back and watch, but once she feels a bit more secure she will come forward and seek interaction. On these occasions she has chosen to snuggle close to me and will sit gazing and enjoying contact, although she does need to be gently encouraged each time as confidence doesn’t yet seem consistent.

It has quickly become apparent that Trixie is quite a complex girl in the home. She is very focused on attention and has already shown signs of jealousy when sharing human interaction. On one occasion, when another foster dog came onto the sofa, Trixie reacted strongly and became defensive. She can also be particular about other dogs in general and can be especially reactive to barking dogs, and has shown a clear dislike of a small dachshund in the home. For this reason, she will now be looking for a home as an only dog where she can get all of the attention for herself.

Outside of this, she is an active little girl and has already shown she is a determined digger, having previously managed to dig under fencing and patio areas. This will need careful management going forward with very secure boundaries required.

Overall, Trixie is settling in but is still very much finding her feet.

name: Archie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been neutered and have had 21 teeth removed.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive and patient way.

He is a cuddly and affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

As Archie has lived in a home before, he will already be familiar with the sights and sounds of home life. However, he may need a little reminding of his house training in a new environment. He walks well on a lead and enjoys his walks with volunteers.

Archie is looking for a quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of the breed and of rescue dogs. He will need people who are happy to give him the time and space he needs to settle and understand that he is safe.

Archie is doing really well since returning to us and his confidence is growing all the time. He is such a loving little dog, and in the right home, we hope he will continue to thrive and become a devoted companion.

Archie is an absolute pleasure to work with! It’s been some time now, and our bond continues to grow stronger every day.He absolutely loves smothering you with kisses and will do anything to get himself onto your lap! Archie has been kennelled with a few dogs and socialised with plenty more, but he has become particularly taken with a Cocker called Trixie. They share some similar traits, including not wanting to share their humans, although neither has displayed any jealousy towardsthe other so far. They absolutely love running laps around the yard together before heading straight into your lap for some fuss. Archie will even stand on Trixie’s back just to make sure he gets in on the action and doesn’t miss out on any attention!As mentioned, Archie is yet to display any jealous traits towards either dogs or humans, but that doesn’t mean he won’t potentially show this once settled into a home. It’s something any potential adopter should be mindful of and prepared to manage appropriately.

What I can promise, though, is that Archie will become your best friend. He has so much love to give and, once he trusts you, he will love you unconditionally.This gorgeous boy deserves someone who will give him the love, patience and understanding he needs — and in return, you’ll have a loyal companion who will want nothing more than to be by your side.

Archie is the funniest and cheekiest of little Dachshunds. Archie needs a little time to warm to you (but not all that long), and once he does, he is the most lovely of boys. I have been caring for him for a few weeks now, and I am totally smitten.

Archie walks beautifully on lead and loves nothing more than when we venture out for a stroll along the lanes around the rescue. Archie is very fond of his toys and will happily run around the yard with a ball in his mouth. He will also spend much time organising his cuddly toys, making sure they are in just the right place.

Archie has been kennelled with other small female dogs. He seems to do best with robust smaller females, as he can be a little frisky with the more timid dogs. Archie could go as an only dog in the right home, one where there are humans who will have lots of time for him.

Archie is very enthusiastic with his kisses once he knows you and will desperately clamber over you for fusses. Archie is an all-round lovely little dog, best suited to a quiet adult home where there is plenty of love, time, and patience for him to truly settle in.

Archie is such a sweet little man who came into our care from a breeder. He was adopted but has sadly been returned after his adopters felt they were not the right match for him. Archie formed a very strong bond with his female owner, but found it much harder to build a relationship with her husband, who was frequently away from home and therefore had very little opportunity to gain Archie's trust. When Archie becomes closely bonded to his favourite person, he can become protective of them. In his previous home, he nipped when he was sitting with his owner and her husband approached, so his new adopters will need to understand this behaviour and be prepared to continue building his confidence in a positive, patient way.

He is a cuddly, affectionate little dog once he feels comfortable, although he isn't quite brave enough to take treats from our hands just yet. Although Archie gets on well with other dogs, he can become protective of his favourite person around them, so we think he would be happiest as the only dog in the home, where he can relax and build a close bond with his new family.

Archie is a gorgeous little boy who came to us from a breeder and was understandably unsure of the world around him. It was truly heartbreaking to see how frightened he was as he would shy away from human contact and retreat when approached. Archie needs gentle handling, patience, and calm, slow movements to help him feel safe. Already, we are seeing progress. He enjoys a gentle fuss and has grown some confidence wagging his tail enthusiastically.

He gains reassurance from other dogs and will need a kind, confident resident dog in his new home to help guide him, boost his confidence, and show him that people and home life can be safe and rewarding.

Archie has never lived in a home before, so his adopters will need to be patient and understanding as he learns the basics, including house training and walking on a lead. He could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over, who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and his own space to settle in.

Since arriving with us, Archie has undergone extensive and much-needed dental treatment and has had 21 teeth removed. He is now recovering well and feeling much more comfortable.

name: Emrys
description:
I am looking for an adult only home with experienced adopters.

I could live with other dogs or be the only dog. I cannot be homed with cats.

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden to let off steam.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Emrys is such a wonderful boy. He’s currently living in a foster home where has been for a year now and has absolutely flourished with them. He originally came to us from a farm so had very little in the way of training and socialising. This meant he could find new people worrying and during a short adoption of just a few months, he struggled to get used to a male visitor and would react towards him and redirected onto another person while stressed. He was returned to his foster home following this and hasn’t put a paw out of place since.

In foster, Emrys does very well, he absolutely adores his three collie best friends and we think he would thrive in a home with a resident dog to keep him company. We would consider an experienced home adopting him as an only dog however he loves having doggy friends so would need regular playdates. Unfortunately Emrys cannot live with cats. He is looking for a collie and rescue experienced home to help him thrive. He absolutely loves his walks and as he is such a clever lad, he will need brain games to wear out his mind too! If an active home is looking for a dog to join in on a sport like agility, we are sure he would do well!

Once Emrys trusts you, he is a wonderful companion and after an exciting walk where he gets to play with his friends, he does really enjoy a cuddle and a snooze on the couch. He is looking for a quiet, adult only home who understands collie behaviour, especially collies bred to work. When introduced to people with plenty of space to move away if he gets worried, he makes friends quickly. His amazing foster home have done so well in bringing out his silly, confident side and absolutely love his quirks. He is such a brilliant boy and has been waiting very patiently for his forever family.

Emrys has a fatty lump on the right flank that does not pose as an issue and is being monitored.

Emrys has been in foster with us for the past 10 months and has proven to be a confident, affectionate collie. He loves his walks just as much as he enjoys relaxing on the sofa afterwards.

He gets along well with both dogs and people, is clean in the house, and travels happily in the car. During his time with us, Emrys has shown no signs of reactivity and has greeted all visitors kindly.

He is a truly lovely dog and would make a fantastic, loyal companion.

Emrys has been in foster with us for seven months now, and he’s a real character. He gets on well with all dogs and, since being back with us, has shown no reactive or guarding behaviours. In the right home, he will truly thrive and make a wonderful companion.

Emrys can occasionally feel nervous around new people, and when this happens he takes himself off to his safe space, which is in the garden. From there, he’ll assess the situation at his own pace before coming back inside when he’s ready to meet someone new. It’s important that he’s given the time and space to do this calmly.

Once he knows you, Emrys is an absolute joy to be around. He loves his walks and secure field runs, is calm and settled in the evenings, and is incredibly affectionate.

With his wicked personality and loving nature, Emrys will make a fantastic companion for the right person.

Emrys has been back in foster for 11 weeks now and has settled in beautifully with no problems at all. He gets on very well with the three resident dogs as well as visiting dogs, and he is friendly with visitors and strangers outside the home. Emrys is totally house clean, travels well in the car, and is very treat-orientated, which makes him easy to train. After his walks, he loves nothing more than relaxing with his foster family.

Emrys has settled back in beautifully with his foster family and hasn’t shown any issues at all. He loves racing around the garden with the resident dogs and is starting to enjoy playing with toys and bringing a ball back.

He’s now completely house trained, walks very nicely on the lead, and is happy to travel in the car.

Emrys is such a lovable boy and is coming along wonderfully. He’ll make a fantastic companion for the right home.

Emrys is a striking, high-energy Collie who came to us from a farm where his owner could no longer give him the time he needed. After arriving he quickly found himself in foster, where he received plenty of exercise, mental stimulation, and affection, everything a clever Collie thrives on.He was adopted for a short time, but sadly returned to us after displaying behaviours in the home that hadn’t been seen while in foster. His adopters told us that Emrys exhibited some guarding tendencies and could react negatively when he felt backed into a corner or overwhelmed. Because of this, he’s looking for a calm, adult-only home with experienced adopters who understand the needs of a sensitive, intelligent dog and can support him with firm but kind guidance.Emrys will need a secure garden with space to run, and a home that can provide him with plenty of structured physical and mental activity to keep him happy and settled. He’s a bright boy who’s eager to please and loves learning. With patience, consistency, and the right support, Emrys has every potential to thrive.Emrys is now back with his original foster where he has shown many lovely qualities, he is clean in the house, travels well in the car, walks nicely on the lead, and is affectionate with those he trusts. He’s also food-motivated and already learning basic commands. We believe that Emrys thrives on activity and as he has not displayed these behaviours in foster it may be because he is provided with so much stimulation and exercises. His adopters will need to keep this in mind, and ideally be very active and willing to provide him with different games and activities to keep his mind busy.Emrys could live with another confident resident dog or be the only dog in the right home. He cannot live with cats, and due to his sensitivity, he will need a home without children or visiting children.This boy has so much potential and is just waiting for the right people to help him blossom.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Kaia
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy teens who are sensible.

I would prefer to be an only dog! No cats please!

I am a large lady, so would love a garden to accommodate for my size and 6ft fences.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I may know a little bit of house training, but might need a refresher.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home! Read below for more info!

10-09-26 Kaia is a very friendly girl who has come into our care from Romania in search of a fresh start. She is a confident and happy dog who is always ready to roll over for a belly rub and adores affection and attention! Although she is a big girl, she is surprisingly gentle and takes treats very nicely. She has a lovely personality, and gets very wiggly and excited when she meets people.

Kaia would would prefer to be homed as the only dog where she can get all of the fuss and attention for herself. She does mix well with dogs of a similar size to her but wouldn't enjoy sharing her home with them and isn't too keen on smaller dogs. She will also need a home without cats. She can live with older-dog savvy teens who are sensible and understanding of her size. Kaia doesn’t quite realise her own size and can be a little enthusiastic when she wants your attention, sometimes using her paws to get your focus. This could be a bit much for a younger child, although she means no harm and is simply looking for some attention (or perhaps a treat)!

We are told that she lived in a foster home in Romania, but she may still need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. She can already walk on a lead and does this well. However, she can be a bit strong and will need her adopters to work with her on this so that she can comfortably go on walks. Once she is settled, she would love to go on plenty of walks and explorations. She will need an extra-secure garden with fences of at least 6ft that will keep a lady of her size and energy safe.

Kaia is such a happy, affectionate girl who seems to love everyone she meets. She has a big personality, a very sweet nature and plenty of love to give, and we think she will be a wonderful companion for a family looking for a fun and loving dog.

Kaia has been tested for Leishmania, Giardia, heartworm disease, Lyme disease, ehrlichiosis, anaplasmosis, and Brucellosis, all of which are negative.

name: Whimsey
description:
I can live with older, dog savvy teens who are sensible and will allow me to settle.

I could live as an only dog, or with a similar sized canine friend. No cats please!

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I walk well on a lead, but will need guidance in the outside world.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

Whimsey came to us from a breeder as a very worried little girl who found the world quite overwhelming. When she first arrived, she was unsettled and skittish, needing plenty of time and reassurance to help her feel safe. Since then, she has made wonderful progress and has really started to show what a special girl she is.

Whimsey has formed a lovely bond with her carers and now greets those she knows and trusts with enthusiastic cuddles and kisses. It has been a joy to watch her confidence grow, and she is becoming more comfortable with the people around her every day.

While Whimsey has come on tremendously, she can still be nervous and unsure around new people. She will need a calm, patient and understanding home that is willing to give her the time and space she needs to build trust and settle at her own pace. Once she feels safe, her affectionate and loving personality truly shines through. She could also live with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can respect her need for a gentle introduction and allow her to settle in at her own pace.

Whimsey walks nicely on a lead, but as she can still be sensitive to new experiences, her adopters will need to continue introducing her to the world gently and at a pace she is comfortable with, helping her build confidence without becoming overwhelmed.

Whimsey really enjoys spending time with other dogs and loves socialising with her canine friends in the exercise yards. We now feel she could happily live with another resident dog of a similar size, provided they get along well during a successful meet and greet. Like many dogs, Whimsey can be a little selective about her friendships, so finding the right canine companion will be important. She would also be perfectly happy as the only dog in the home, where she could soak up all the love and attention from her family while continuing to enjoy opportunities to socialise with other dogs on walks. She cannot live with cats.

Whimsey has such a sweet heart and has already shown just how much progress she can make when given kindness, patience and understanding. With the right home behind her, we know she will continue to blossom into a wonderfully affectionate companion and a much-loved member of the family.

Whimsey arrived with an abscess on the right side of her jaw, which has been treated by our veterinary team. Our vets have also noted that she has a fractured canine tooth with no root or nerve exposure. At this stage, no treatment is required, but it should be monitored by her adopters and their own vet. She has also received treatment for a urinary tract infection, which has been successfully managed under veterinary guidance.

Oh, my heart. Whimsey has completely stolen it.

She is honestly one of the most loving, affectionate, and gentle girls I've ever met. The moment I walk into her kennel or sit with her in the yard, she melts into me. All she wants is kisses, cuddles, and to be as close to you as possible. She has so much love to give!

She's doing so well with her dog socialising too and absolutely adores her best friend, Royal.

Whimsey is going to make the most incredible addition to a very lucky family. She deserves so much more than just being someone's dog. She deserves to be a cherished member of the family, included in all of life's little moments, loved unconditionally, and never made to wonder if she's enough again.

I truly can't wait for the day she finds the home she's been waiting for. Whoever gets to call this beautiful girl theirs is going to be incredibly lucky.

Whimsey has come on so well since she first arrived. She’s bonded with me so much and always welcomes me with a big kiss and cuddle.

She can be nervous and unsure around new people, but with time, patience, and understanding, she’s going to make the most wonderful addition to someone’s home.

Although she needs to be the only dog in the home, she can happily socialise with other dogs and loves going down to the big yard with her friends.

Whimsy has come to us from a breeder and is a very worried girl. When she first arrived, she was very unsettled at the moment and could be quite skittish, finding so many of the sights and sounds of the world quite overwhelming. Since arriving she has started to settle in and come out of her shell, but will still need time and TLC as she settles in to her new life. Once she gets to know you, she will quietly approach you and allow a gentle fuss.

Whimsy needs time to learn and to trust, and needs a calm and quiet home home that understands ex-breeding dogs and will allow her the space she needs to learn about trust at her own pace. She will need a calm, patient, and understanding family who are willing to let her take things slowly and gently as she begins to discover the comforts of home life.

She will need a kind and confident resident dog in her home that she can look to and rely on as she learns about home life and settles in. Having a canine companion to guide her will really help build her confidence and show her that the world can be a safe and happy place.

Whimsy does walk well on a lead, but as she can be a bit skittish, her adopters will need to take the outside world at her own pace, allowing her the time she needs to gain confidence in her surroundings without feeling pressured.

Whimsy seems like she has such a sweet heart, and with time, patience, and kindness, she will begin to show her loving and gentle nature. She just needs someone special to help her learn about trust and companionship and to show her that she is safe and loved.

Whimsy has come to us with an abscess on the right side of her jaw, which is being treated by the vets. Our vets have noted that she has one fractured canine, but no root or nerve exposure and so it is advised to leave it at this time, but will need monitoring by her adopters and their vet. She is currently being treated for a UTI and will be rechecked once the course of medication has finished.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Orange Blossom
description:
I could live with older, dog-savvy children who respect my space.

I could live with other dogs, or be the only dog. I don't mind.

Please be patient with me, I need to learn the basics.

My adopters will need to have me spayed once I am of age!

09-09-26 Orange Blossom is a super sweet little girl who was brought into our care as part of a litter seized by the local police as they were living in poor conditions. She is a lovely, friendly pup who adores people and is always happy to have attention and fuss.

She is a typical young puppy with lots of energy and will need plenty of playtime, training and enrichment as she grows. She is good with other dogs and could live with another suitable dog, although she could also be happy as an only dog with adopters who are around for plenty of company.

Orange Blossom will need all the usual puppy training, including house training and lead work, and her new family should be prepared for the time and patience this takes. We would also recommend puppy classes to help her learn how to behave appropriately and build her confidence out and about.

She is gentle and easy to handle and could live with older, sensible children who are used to dogs. As with all puppies, she will need continued socialisation, training and guidance to help her grow into a happy and well-mannered adult.

Orange Blossom will need to be spayed when she is old enough, and her adopters will need to agree to this as part of her adoption. She is a lovely little girl with plenty of personality, and we hope she finds a family who will enjoy watching her grow and learning all the fun things that come with puppy life.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Doodle
description:
I can live with older children, aged 13+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I can be an only dog or live with female dogs. I have never met cats.

I would love a garden to run and play in!

I can walk well on a lead and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be neutered before finding my forever home.

02-09-26 Doodle has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for his forever home. He is a friendly, confident boy who is an absolute delight to spend time with. He has a lovely, happy personality and is just wonderful!

Doodle is confident enough that we would consider homing him as an only dog, provided his adopters are around for most of the time and can give him plenty of company and attention. He could also happily live with a kind female resident dog, but he cannot be homed with another male dog.

Doodle is a very bouncy and lively boy who will be looking for an active home where he can enjoy plenty of fun, exercise and adventures with his new family. His adopters should be prepared for his enthusiasm and be willing to help him learn some manners and new skills as he settles in. He can already walk on a lead, which is a great start! He can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged 13+ who are sensible and will allow him time to settle in. He will need an extra secure garden of at least 6ft that can keep him safe as he settles.

He has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to him and his adopters will need to be kind and understanding as he learns all about home life and house training.

Doodle is a lovely, fun-loving boy with plenty of personality, and we are sure he is going to bring lots of laughter and happiness to his new family. We can't wait to see him enjoying the wonderful life he deserves!

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Winnie
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I haven't tried walks just yet and will find this a bit overwhelming at the moment.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home!

Winnie is a very scared girl who has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. She has clearly had some very difficult experiences in her past, and at the moment she finds it incredibly hard to trust people or believe that we mean her no harm. She is an extremely frightened little girl who needs a very special and experienced home where she can begin to learn that life can be safe and that human hands can be kind.

Winnie is currently finding human interaction and handling exceptionally overwhelming. If someone approaches her too closely, she can become extremely distressed and will bark continuously as she panics. Being picked up is particularly frightening for her, and when she feels trapped or unable to escape, she will bite wherever she can reach. She may also toilet through fear when someone attempts to pick her up. These behaviours are coming from a place of extreme fear and a desperate attempt to protect herself, but they are very real behaviours that her adopters will need to understand and be prepared to manage safely. Winnie is not currently a dog who can be handled casually, and her future family will need to be very experienced with severely frightened ex-breeding dogs and confident in reading her body language and respecting her boundaries.

Winnie will need a very calm and quiet, adult-only home with no pressure placed upon her to interact before she is ready. Her adopters will need to understand that building a relationship with Winnie is likely to be a long journey, and progress may be very gradual. She will need people who are willing to allow her to take things completely at her own pace, while providing a safe, predictable environment where she can slowly learn that she is not going to be hurt.

Despite how frightened Winnie is of people, she is already showing us some lovely glimpses of the little dog underneath her fears. She absolutely loves toys and food, and although she isn't yet brave enough to take treats directly from our hands, she is more than happy to join in with treat time when treats are gently thrown towards her. She is also beginning to enjoy the simple comfort of being cosy in a big, comfy duvet. These small things are incredibly important for Winnie and give us hope that, as she begins to feel safer, we will see more and more of her personality emerge.

Winnie will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home who she can look to for reassurance and companionship. Having another dog around may help her feel safer and give her a familiar canine friend to follow as she learns about her new life. Her adopters will need to ensure that any resident dog is calm, confident and able to give Winnie the space she needs.

Winnie has never lived in a home before, so absolutely everything will be new to her. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she learns about home life, including house training and the everyday sights and sounds of a household. Lead walking is not something Winnie is ready for at this stage, and her new home will need a very secure garden where she can begin to explore safely without being overwhelmed.

Winnie is not going to be an easy dog, and she will require a significant level of commitment, experience and patience from her adopters. However, she is not a lost cause. She is a deeply frightened little girl who has not yet had the opportunity to understand that people can be trusted. Seeing a dog like Winnie slowly begin to feel safe and choose to engage with the people around her can be incredibly rewarding, but her adopters must be prepared for this to take time.

Winnie needs someone truly special who understands just how serious her fears are and is willing to give her the space, security and patience she needs. Beneath all that fear is a little girl who loves food, adores toys and is beginning to discover the comfort of a cosy bed. With the right experienced home and plenty of time, we hope Winnie will one day feel safe enough to let her true personality shine.

Winnie has been given the Gift of Life by Jo Rowlands

name: Jasmine
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy children, aged 16+ who are understanding.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I am clean in my foster home, but may need some reminders in my new home!

Jasmine has come to us from a breeder to find the loving forever home she deserves. Jasmine is now in a foster home, where she has settled wonderfully and is showing us just how much progress she has made. She was adopted for a short period of time but was reluctantly returned to us as the resident dogs in her previous home were unable to accept her. She is still a sensitive little lady who can become skittish when worried, but she is beginning to relax and show more of her sweet personality.

Jasmine is looking for a calm, quiet and stress-free home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time, patience and reassurance to settle into her new life. A quieter area would be preferable, as she can find too much going on overwhelming. There is no quick fix for Jasmine, but she is already showing that with the right environment and plenty of understanding, she can continue to grow in confidence.

She takes great comfort from other dogs and will need friendly resident dog or dogs in her new home. They can be any size or breed, but they will need to be kind and happy to have Jasmine around, allowing her to follow them and curl up alongside them without being fazed if she becomes a little skittish. She sleeps quietly through the night in a dog bed close to her foster family's dogs and clearly finds having other dogs around a great source of comfort and security.

Jasmine would love a secure garden to explore, although she found a very large garden overwhelming in foster, so a smaller area would be preferable. She has been doing wonderfully with her toileting and will take herself outside when the back door is open. In fact, she has been completely clean since arriving in foster, which is fantastic progress. She also enjoys exploring and has even been known to make her way into raised flower beds for a snooze!

Jasmine has also made lovely progress with her confidence and is becoming much more relaxed in her foster home. She loves her food and treats and is now eating her meals more calmly. As she arrived very thin, she is currently having three meals a day to help her gain weight. She can be a little particular about drinking and currently needs a tiny amount of grated cheese added to her water to encourage her, but she is otherwise doing well. She can live with older, dog-savvy teens aged, 16+, who are sensible and allow her time to settle in.

Jasmine can give you the runaround when she needs to be picked up, but once she is safely in your arms she relaxes and seems to really enjoy being cuddled. She has even started to play with her octopus toy when nobody is looking, which is such a lovely glimpse of the playful little character hiding underneath her worries.

Jasmine's back leg is doing wonderfully and does not cause her any problems. She happily pings up the back steps and even climbs into the raised flower beds for a comfortable snooze. When Jasmine first arrived, she was walking with a noticeable limp and struggling to use her right hind leg. Our vets found that an old injury had healed with significant scar tissue, which was restricting her movement and preventing her from fully extending her leg. Jasmine underwent surgery to remove some of the excess scarred tissue and has continued to recover well. She will need to continue building up the muscle in her leg and may always have a slightly unusual gait due to her old injury, but it certainly doesn't stop her from getting on with life. Jasmine also has an old healed break in her tail.

Jasmine is a truly sweet little girl who has already come such a long way. She will need a special home that is willing to give her the time, patience and understanding she needs to continue building her confidence. With friendly canine companions to lean on, a quiet environment and plenty of love, we are sure Jasmine will continue to blossom. She may take a little more time than some, but we truly believe this sweet little girl will be worth it.

Jasmine has been given the Gift of Life by Marjory Dexter

Jasmine has reluctantly been returned due to the resident dogs not accepting her.  She needs friendly dog/s to live, any size or breed but ones that will allow her to follow and curl up with and aren't fazed if she becomes skitish.

Jasmine would love a garden to explore, but not too big as she found ours overwhelming so we've sectioned off a smaller area.  With the back door open she will take herself outside to do her toileting, in fact she's been clean since she arrived. Her back leg doesn't give her any problems, she pings up our back steps and even into our raised flower beds for a snooze.

She sleeps quietly all night in a dog bed near our own two dogs.  She has now started eating her meals more relaxed, and is having three meals a day due to being so thin, but the only way i can get her to drink water is to add a very small amount of grated cheese to it.Jasmine does give me the runaround when i need to pick her up, but once in your arms she relaxes and seems to enjoy it.  She has also started to play with her Octopus toy when no one is looking.

There is no quick fix for Jasmine, she will take time, patience and a quiet stress free home, preferably in a quiet area, but i guarantee this sweet little girl will be worth it in the end..

Jasmine has come to us from a breeder to find the loving forever home she deserves. She is a lovely little lady who is understandably a little worried by all the recent changes in her life. Despite this, she is growing in confidence each day and will slowly approach you for a gentle fuss, showing the sweet nature that is waiting to blossom.  Jasmine is looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and understand that she will need time, patience and reassurance to settle into her new life. She is a gentle soul who will thrive with a family who are happy to let her build confidence at her own pace.

She will need another kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help show her the ropes and reassure her as she adjusts to her new life. Having a canine companion will give Jasmine the confidence she needs as she learns that the world can be a safe and happy place.  She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and understanding while she learns all about home life and new skills like house training. She has not yet learnt to walk on a lead or harness, so this will need to be introduced gradually and positively once she has settled into her new surroundings. Jasmine is a truly sweet little girl who is already beginning to come out of her shell and we think whoever adopts her will adore her.

When Jasmine arrived, she was walking with a noticeable limp and struggling to use her right hind leg. Our vets found that an old injury had healed with significant scar tissue, which was restricting her movement and preventing her from fully extending her leg. Jasmine has since undergone surgery to remove some of the excess scarred tissue. She is recovering well and is now using her leg much more. She will need to continue building up the muscle in her leg, but we are really pleased with her progress. She may always have a slightly unusual gait due to her old injury, but this certainly doesn’t stop her from getting on with life! Jasmine also has an old healed break in her tail.

name: Cooper
description:
I would like a calm and quiet, adult only home in a semi-rural area.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I don't mind cats!

I would love a good sized garden to explore and will need 6ft fences.

I am a beginner to walking on a lead, but would like an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who was quite overwhelmed when he first arrived, but is starting to come out of his shell more and more each day. He could initially be worried when he first met new people, but his circle of friends has grown and he is making lots of human friends daily and is a friendly, affectionate boy.

Cooper absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort from having canine friends around him, so he will need another kind, confident and playful resident dog in his new home to be his companion and show him the ropes. He is also beginning to discover the joy of toys and is enjoying learning how to play, which is so sweet. He has met cats at the rescue fine, and we may consider homing him with a dog-savvy cat.

As Cooper has never lived in a home before, his adopters will need to be patient, kind and understanding while he settles in and learns all about home life, including new skills like house training. He is very much a beginner when it comes to walking on a lead and harness, but he is already starting to enjoy his walks and would love an active home where he can continue exploring the world at his own pace.

Cooper would love to find adopters who are experienced with dogs and, whilst not essential, experience with Romanian rescue dogs would be a bonus. He would be happiest in a calm, quiet, adult only home where he can settle in at his own pace and continue building his confidence. Cooper would be best suited to a home in a rural or semi-rural location and would prefer to go for walks in quiet areas. He will need a secure garden with 6ft fences.

With patience, understanding and plenty of love, Cooper will start to discover just how wonderful his life can now be. In return, this gentle boy will reward his family with the privilege of watching him blossom into the happy and loved companion he was always meant to be.

He has tested negative prior to arrival for heartworm, lyme disease, ehrlichia, anaplasma, giardia, leishmania and brucellosis.

It’s been just over a month since I last did an update on our handsome boy Cooper and since then his confidence has grown even more!

Cooper is now the centre of attention in our big play group, he will engage in play with all the dogs who attend, and even greet any new ones with very good manners! Cooper is also now making lots of human friends with numerous members of staff that he used to be scared of!!

It’s absolutely crazy to see how confident Cooper is being, compared to the day he first arrived! It just goes to show all it take is time, patience and love!

I literally love Cooper with all my heart, watching him turn into the happiest, friendliest boy makes my heart so full!

I really hope his time to be in a home comes soon, he really does have so much love to give when he knows you!

When Cooper first arrived, his world was filled with fear. He would quietly tuck himself away at the back of his kennel, very unsure of all his surroundings and who we all were. It was so heartbreaking to see how scared cooper really was.

But every day, with kindness, patience and love, Cooper has taken another tiny step forward. Those tiny steps have turned into giant leaps. Today, the Cooper who once hid away greets his kennel mum with a wagging tail every morning and spends his days happily playing or relaxing with his kennel friends. His personality is really staring to come through and he is slowly learning that the world isn't such a scary place.

When Cooper first arrived, he'd had very little experience walking on a lead. Now he is improving so much more, he even happily takes trips down to our big play yard!

Cooper still finds unfamiliar places and new people a little scary, but it doesn't take long for him to realise he's safe. Once he trusts you, you see the sweetest, gentlest soul who simply wants to love and be loved.

Cooper has done everything we've asked of him. He's been brave. He's learned to trust. He's opened his heart. Now, we're asking for someone to do the same for him.

This beautiful young boy shouldn't be growing up behind kennel doors. He should be learning about the world from the comfort of a sofa, chasing toys around a garden, falling asleep after long walks, and knowing what it feels like to be in a home.

I am so incredibly proud of the progress Cooper has made and I have no doubts in a home with all the patience and kindness he will blossom into the most amazing loving family member anyone could wish for.

Meet Cooper, a lovely boy who has travelled all the way from Romania to begin his new life and search for his forever home. He is a sweet boy who is quite overwhelmed to find himself here, but is starting to settle in and adjust to his new surroundings. Understandably, he is feeling quite scared at the moment, especially when he first meets new people. With those he knows, he is starting to come out of his shell and its lovely to see his confidence growing. Despite his worries, he is easy to handle and in the right home we think he will truly thrive.

Cooper absolutely adores other dogs and takes great comfort from having canine friends around him, so he will need another kind, confident and playful resident dog in his new home to be his companion and show him the ropes. He is also beginning to discover the joy of toys and is enjoying learning how to play, which is so sweet.

Cooper would love to find adopters who are experienced with dogs and, whilst not essential, experience with Romanian rescue dogs would be a bonus. He would be happiest in a calm, quiet, adult only home where he can settle in at his own pace and continue building his confidence. With patience, understanding and plenty of love, Cooper will start to discover just how wonderful his life can now be. In return, this gentle boy will reward his family with the privilege of watching him blossom into the happy and loved companion he was always meant to be.
