name: Lassie
description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I cannot live with cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk well on a lead and would love an active home.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed and am ready for my forever home.

Lassie has come to us from a breeder to find her forever home. When she first arrived she was a very nervous girl as she had not had much experience with people, so everything felt very new and overwhelming to her. She could be quite skittish when approached and was worried about meeting new people and being handled. Since then her confidence has started to really grow. Once she gets to know you, she is the most loyal, loving and affectionate girl and it's so wonderful to see.

Lassie will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult only home where she can settle in at her own pace. She would benefit from adopters who have breed experience and experience with worried dogs.

She will be looking for a home where there was at least one other kind and playful resident dog to be her friend and guide. She gets on brilliantly with all dogs here out and about and socialises well with a variety of breeds and sizes. However, we have found that she is most comfortable sharing her home with other Collies and will therefore need a home with at least one resident Collie. She cannot be homed with cats or small furries. She doesn't like to share her food with other dogs, so her adopters would need to ensure she was fed separately and would need to separate when feeding any long last treats or chews too.

Lassie now walks well on a lead and would love to find an active home where she can go on lots of walks and adventures with her new family and where her clever collie brain can be kept both mentally and physically stimulated. She is only used to walking in quiet areas, so would need gentle introduction to any busier places. Lassie has never lived in a home before so her adopters will need to be kind and understanding as she settles into the home and learns all about home life and new skills like house training.

With time, patience, and lots of love, Lassie will blossom. Once she has settled and gained confidence, she will become a cracking addition to her new family and will enjoy all the adventures life has to offer.

Lassie will need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Lassie spent some time in the office today and coped really well. She happily tucked into a chicken foot for a tasty treat, although she couldn't resist pinching her kennel friend's one too! She was very curious about everything going on around her and enjoyed exploring her surroundings.

A member of staff she hadn't met before came into the office, and although Lassie was a little wary at first, she quickly settled and went back to happily enjoying her chicken foot. It was lovely to see her take the new experience in her stride and continue growing in confidence.

Beautiful beautiful Lassie! What a collie she is, she is so bright and has really come on so much with her basic training. Now knowing "sit" and "lie down". When we're out walking and a car is approaching, all I have to do is ask her to the verge and she sits and waits beautifully until we're able to start walking again. She really doesn't seem to be fazed by much traffic, but is very fixated with sheep if she comes across any. She passes horses lovely and will happily walk past other dogs no issue, but isn't keen on them approaching her. She's a big fan of food which helps with her training.She just needs people that understand that the girl she is when they first meet her is very worried but once she trusts you, her true personality really shines through.

Lassie is such a pretty girl who would do anything for you when she trusts you but is still wary of people initially. She did take treats off of a new person yesterday which was amazing to see. She needs to be in a collie experienced home with someone who will allow her the time to trust them at her own pace. She does love having a playfriend and she seems to be happiest when amongst other collies and collie crosses. She doesn't like sharing her food but is happy to share toys, beds and treats.

Lassie absolutely loves going out for her walks and gets very excited when she knows it’s time to head out. She really enjoys having a good sniff along the way and is always very interested in watching what’s going on in the fields as she passes by. Once she gets to know you, she is incredibly loving and affectionate, although she can take a little bit of time to warm up to new people. Lassie would still need a home with a resident dog, and she would truly thrive in a collie-experienced home where her needs and personality can be well understood.

Lassie is such a beautiful girl and once she knows you, she is the most affectionate, loyal and loving companion. She now walks well on a lead and absolutely loves her walks.

She will need a home with at least one other kind and confident resident dog who is a similar size to her and who loves to have a good play sometimes.

She doesn't like to share her food bowl, so he will need to be fed separately and this is something that her adopters will need to manage. In the right home she'll be someone's absolute best friend.

Lassie is a worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She has not had much experience with people, so everything feels very new and overwhelming to her. She can be quite skittish when approached, so she will need a calm, experienced home where she can be given the time and patience she needs to learn to trust.

At the moment, Lassie is scared of being touched, but she has already started to build a bond with her kennel mum and now allows gentle strokes from her. This shows that with consistency and kindness, shecanlearn to trust, and once she feels safe, she will begin to show her sweet side.

Lassie does walk on a lead, though she finds new experiences worrying, so she will need gentle introductions to the big wide world. She will also need to learn about house training and all the basics of living in a home, as these are things she has never known before.

Because Lassie is such a sensitive soul, she will need an adult-only home with no visiting children, and adopters who are happy to take things slowly at her pace. She will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home who can help her feel secure and show her the ropes. She gets on brilliantly with all dogs here and socialises well with a variety of breeds and sizes. She cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. name: Toby
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog and no cats please!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I can walk well on a lead but can be reactive to bikes.

I was born with deformed toes which have been amputated and I have a luxating patella

Toby is a handsome Cocker Spaniel who has been through a lot in his young life and is now looking for a special someone to help him write his next chapter. Originally coming to us from a breeder at just three months old, Toby was a very scared little puppy who found the world overwhelming. Although he found a loving home, he was sadly returned to our care after his adopters felt unable to manage some of his behaviours.

Toby is still a sensitive soul and will need a calm, adult-only home with no visiting children. His new family should have experience with worried or complex dogs and be confident in helping him feel safe. He will need a home without cats as he has met them at the rescue and was too interested. While Toby had previously shown some resource guarding tendencies in his home, we have not seen any guarding behaviour from him while he has been with us. He has spent time in the office with staff members and has been completely comfortable with people coming in and out, which has been lovely to see.

Toby does enjoy playing with tennis balls and can be reluctant to drop them, but this is not a guarding issue. If we offer him a tasty treat in exchange, he is more than happy to swap his ball!

Since returning to us, Toby has come out of his shell beautifully. He greets staff with a wagging tail and absolutely loves attention, affection and food – especially food! Those who work with him absolutely adore him and think he is the most special and wonderful boy.

Toby will be looking for a home where he can be the only dog. He did live with another dog previously and while they got along, he could sometimes guard his adopter's attention, so for this reason he is best suited to being homed as an only dog.

Out and about, Toby enjoys his walks and is lovely on and off the lead. He has good recall and mixes well with other dogs, although he can be reactive to bicycles, so should only be let off lead in safe, secure areas away from the public.

Toby was born with some deformed toes that were later amputated. He has always had a slightly unusual gait due to this, but our vets have noted that he also has a luxating patella, although it may improve with gentle exercise. He also has a naturally short tail, which just adds to his unique charm.

Toby is a sweet, loving boy who truly wants to connect. He has already won the hearts of everyone here, and we're all rooting for him to find a calm, understanding home where he can feel safe, build trust and thrive. If you have the time, patience and experience to offer Toby the gentle guidance he needs, he will reward you with loyalty, love and plenty of cuddles.

Tobywill need more than one meet and greet with his prospective adopters to allow him time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

Over the last 3 days and nights, I picked up some night shifts and thought it would be the perfect opportunity to bring Toby into the cabin with me and see what he was really like in a home environment.

When I first brought Toby into the cabin, he settled almost instantly. He had a little explore, took everything in, and then happily climbed onto the sofa, curled up, and went to sleep.

I also wanted to use this time to assess Toby around any guarding behaviours that were mentioned in his previous home, particularly as he was going to be in an environment with sofas, beds, and all those lovely home comforts.

During his second day, Toby found himself a very comfy dog bed. He still had his lead attached, and when I went to remove it, he gave a little grumble and snapped towards my hand. Toby immediately removed himself from the bed and came over to me for reassurance.

This wasthe only guarding behaviour Toby displayed during the entire 3 days, and it was incredibly easy to manage.

Toby is a boy who just needs a home that will understand that he can be a worried boy. If he is happily relaxing on his dog bed, he simply needs to be left alone and given his own space. With this in place, he was a dream throughout his stay.

Whenever I wanted to sit or lie down on the sofa or bed and Toby was already there, I would simply call him off, give him a treat, and then invite him back up once I was settled. Toby also coped brilliantly with being left alone while I went off to do the night rounds. In fact, I’m pretty sure he just slept the whole time!

Toby slept all night in bed with me, and he absolutely loved it. He was so calm, content, and relaxed and, yes, he even snored!

Watching Toby in the cabin has made me realise even more how much love he has to give. This is the side of Toby that I wish everyone could see. I honestly cannot put into words how heartbreaking it was to then put him back into his kennel while he continues to wait for his person to find him.

Toby doesn’t need someone to be perfect. He doesn’t need someone to constantly fuss over him. He simply needs someone who will understand him, give him a little structure, and allow him the time and space to settle.

In return, you get the most gorgeous, loving boy who just wants to be part of your life.

These last 3 days have given me a little glimpse into what Toby’s life should look like! Toby deserves the absolute world. He is an incredibly special boy who just needs someone to understand him!

This week, Toby’s kennel mum celebrated his 1 year anniversary by breaking him out of the rescue for a couple of hours of fun!!Toby travelled good as gold in the car, and happily climbed into the back of the car and had his seatbelt harness fitted with no issues at all.He travelled to Pupstars Paddock with his kennel mum and another staff member who was new to him. He was absolutely brilliant with that staff member who could only sing his praises!!Toby absolutely LOVED the secure field, his tail did not stop wagging, he followed his kennel mum around everywhere and was (very gently) taking treats of both staff members.Once Toby bonds with you, he is the most loyal boy in the world. His circle of trust is only getting bigger, with more and more staff members falling in love with him as time goes on. He may have a stricter criteria than most, but it just means he is just an incredibly special boy in need of a special home. He is such a darling and we wish more people would be able to see it!

Toby’s one year anniversary with us is slowly approaching, and it honestly breaks my heart every day knowing he’s still not curled up on a sofa in a home of his own.

Toby is literally such an amazing dog when he knows you, all he wants to do is spend time with you, whether that be sitting with you, or going out for a gentle stroll!

Recently, I’ve been working on Toby’s lead reactivity, and he’s been doing incredibly well. He’s making such good progress, and I’m so proud of how far he’s come!

I really hope this is the last update I have to write about toby, hopefully his next updates will be coming from his new pawrents, showing us him blossoming in a home and how truly special he really is!

I’ve had the absolute joy of working with Toby for a couple of months now, and he truly is one of my more sensitive, special boys!

Once Toby gets to know you, he turns into the happiest, most affectionate little soul you could ever meet! He absolutely loves zooming around our big play yard, or heading out for a calm, gentle stroll along the lanes taking everything in at his own pace, Toby can be reactive towards passing cars or other dogs, it is something we are currently working on with him!

With the weather getting nicer, I decided it was the perfect day for a little adventure down to the river! To get there, we walk through a huge open field, so I popped Toby on a long line to give him some extra freedom to explore.I don’t think I’ve ever seen a dog so happy he spent most of his time rolling around on his back in the grass with the biggest grin on his face!

When we reached the river, Toby was a little unsure at first. He sat at the edge, watching the water. But after a few minutes of building up his courage, he dipped his paws in and that was it, he was happily paddling back and forth, enjoying every second. It was such a special moment to watch.

I truly adore Toby with my whole heart, he’s one of those dogs who just stays with you, always on your mind.

He can still feel a bit unsure when meeting new people and might bark or back away at first, but give him a little time and patience, and he’ll become your most loyal, loving best friend.

I honestly can’t believe Toby is still waiting for his forever home. He is such a gentle, beautiful soul who deserves the absolute best life has to offer!

Toby is a sweet older gentleman who truly enjoys the quieter side of life. He loves nothing more than snuggling up for a nap and being close to his people.

Toby still has a playful spark and enjoys his daily walks as well as pottering around the yard. He would thrive in a calm, peaceful home and is best suited to a household with no children or cats, where he can relax and enjoy his golden years in comfort.

I love Toby. He is so loved by many of us here at the rescue. He's a confident boy once he knows you, but until he feels comfortable around you he can bark and sometimes be a bit standoffish.

Toby is a big cuddle bunny, he absolutely loves a fuss, and will happily accept butt scratches any time of the day.

He enjoys going out for walks but absolutely loves being off lead and running around the big play yard, when his butt wiggles with happiness and excitement it really doesn't stop, it's super adorable. He likes chasing a tennis ball but he won't bring it back, instead he rolls around with it usually in his mouth and will then lay with it and play with it, he's a comical boy.

Again, once he's comfortable with you he's very easy to handle, I can get a coat or a jumper on him with no problems, I can pick him up and I can brush him with no problems, he had a groom recently and he was no issue at all.

It's a shame he keeps getting overlooked, yes he might have some typical cocker issues such as guarding, but it hasn't been a huge issue since he's been here, I can go in and out of his kennel, pick things up etc and he's been fine. I've also been yarding him with other dogs to try and socialise him more, and although he can be selective of who he likes, once he's found a friend then he just wants to play. He is a beautiful boy inside and out, and in my opinion anyone would be lucky to have him as part of their family.

Also he is kennel clean so house training shouldn't take any time at all.

Please, don't let Toby spend another year in kennels, he truly deserves to find his forever home, as they all do. It's getting colder, it's been snowing, a nice warm, cosy house with a loving family is what he wants, I know his forever home is out there somewhere so please come and find him.

Toby is still doing incredibly well with us here and hasn’t shown any signs of guarding, while this has stopped with us here we still are unsure how he will react in a home environment.

It is an absolute pleasure working with Toby and he always brings a smile to your face throughout the day. Toby is a gentle, loving and happy boy and is desperate to have somebody he can give all his love to.

Toby has definitely come out of his shell since he's been here, he still barks when you first see him but it's a happy bark and his tail doesn't stop, before he would stay for scratches for a little bit, but now he doesn't want to leave you and wants all the attention. He is a very loving dog.

Toby originally came to us from a breeder when he was around 3 months old. He was a terrified puppy who was worried about everything and would even squeak in fear when being handled. He was quickly adopted and found a loving home, but he has sadly been returned to our care as he was displaying some behaviours that his adopters felt unable to cope with.

Toby was homed with another dog and while they got along well, he did show some signs of guarding his adopter from the other dog, for this reason we now think he would be most suited to being homed as an only dog.

Toby can also sometimes grumble if people walk past the sofa or his bed and he is on them, so he will be looking for an adult only home with no visiting children, with adopters who have experience with dogs with similar issues and will be able to work on this with him. He did nip his adopter once around 18 months ago, but that was the only time that resulted in more than a grumble.

Toby is still quite a scared boy in some aspects and certain things will make him extremely nervous, such as the hoover or sometimes even minor things like the sounds of a drawer closing, but with confident owners with experience of scared dogs we do believe he will progress further. He would be best suited to a calm and quiet home, where he can settle in at his own pace and follow a routine.

He enjoys going for walks and is very good both on and off lead. He has good recall and gets along well with other dogs outside of the home. He can be reactive to bikes, so his adopters would need to be mindful of this and keep him on lead in any areas where he may encounter bikes and only let him off lead in secure areas.

As he has lived in a home before, we believe he is house trained, but he may need some reminders.

Toby is a sweet boy at heart and in the right home and with the right adopters we think he will thrive. Since his arrival with us he has been on his best behaviour and already adores all of the staff that work with him and they adore him too. He absolutely loves his food and has a true zest for life which makes us smile each day, so we are so hopeful that his perfect home is out there and will find him soon.

Toby was born with some deformed toes, which have since been amputated but don't seem to bother him, though he does walk with a slightly abnormal gait. He also has a short tail.

name: Tadpole
description:
I can live with older, dog-savvy kids aged 13+ who allow me time to settle in.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I can be a little nervous, and will need a secure garden to learn about the outdoors.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have been spayed & have had an umbilical hernia repaired.

26-08-26 Tadpole is a sweet little lady who has come to us from a breeder. She will approach you if you sit quietly and give her time to sniff and get comfortable, but she can quickly lose confidence and retreat. She is easy to handle and is very curious, showing that she is trying her best to be brave.

Tadpole relies on her kennel friends for comfort, so she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she continues to build her confidence. She will need a quiet home where she can learn about trust and settle in at her own pace. Tadpole can live with sensible, dog-savvy teens aged 13+ who will give her the time and space she needs.

She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to be patient and kind as she learns about house training and walking on a lead. Tadpole is a gorgeous little girl who is trying so hard to be brave, and we think she will blossom with the right family.

Tadpole has arrived with an abdominal hernia that has been repaired at the time of her spay.

Tadpole has been given the Gift of Life by Trudie Williams

description:

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before finding my forever home.

27-08-26 Sianon has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a worried girl who is unsure around humans and isn't used to being handled yet. She is going to need plenty of love, patience and TLC as she settles in and slowly begins to grow in confidence.

Sianon will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who understand that she will need time to adjust. Her new family will need to be kind and patient, allowing her to settle in at her own pace without putting pressure on her. She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her, and she will need gentle guidance as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training and how to walk on a lead and harness.

Sianon relies on other dogs for confidence, so she will need at least one other kind and confident resident dog in her new home to be her friend and help her feel safe. We hope having a canine companion by her side will help her learn that the world isn't such a scary place. Any children in the home will need to be teenagers aged 16+.

Sianon is a gentle girl who has lots to learn, but with the right home, a patient family and a lovely canine friend to show her the ropes, we hope she will gradually discover her confidence and enjoy all the wonderful things life has to offer.

Sianon has been given the Gift of Life by Dee Wickson-Dix

description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I am learning to get comfortable on a harness, but this will take time.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

13-08-26 Mika has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She is a very shy little lady who prefers to hide away and looks to her canine friends for comfort and reassurance. When left alone, Mika shakes like a leaf, and it is heart-breaking to see just how overwhelmed she can become.

Mika will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in the home that she can lean on as she learns about trust, companionship, and life in a family environment. She has never lived in a home before, so her adopters will need to have ex-breeder experience and be patient and understanding as she learns all about house training and settles into a new routine.

Mika has started to learn comfortability with putting on a harness, and has walked to and from the yard on a lead but she is still too nervous to venture out too far just yet. Her adopters will need to work with her on this and continue to build her confidence and work at her pace. She will need a calm, adult-only home where she can settle at her own pace and slowly begin to build her confidence.

Mika has so much potential and so much love to give. She simply needs someone who can see beyond her fears, give her the time she deserves, and help her find her paws in the world.

Mika has been given the Gift of Life by Carolina Olsen

description:
I can live with older children, aged 16+, who understand I need time to settle in.

I need a resident dog to help me settle in and I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I’ve never been on walks before and will need a gentle introduction.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I have an undershot jaw & I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

Sunny arrived with us very matted, but she was such a good girl during her grooming session and took everything in her stride.

Sunny is an amazing lady who has so much to look forward to and will make a wonderful addition to a loving and accepting home.

Sunny has arrived with an undershot jaw that does not seem to bother her, but will need to be monitored in her new home.

name: Toucan
description:
I would like a home with adopted experienced with rescue dogs.

I can be an only dog or live with a calm resident dog.

I’m active and would love a large, secure garden with 6ft+ fences to play in.

I have lots of energy and need an active home that loves adventures.

I am in a foster home and am house trained.

I am neutered and ready to find my forever home!

Toucan is a very handsome and active boy who originally came to us from a breeder. He was adopted for a short period of time, but unfortunately found himself back in rescue.

Toucan is a bright and friendly boy. He can be quite worried when meeting new people, but given time to build a bond, forms lovely relationships with his humans. He is affectionate and engaging, and with the right guidance, will make a wonderful addition to a committed home.

He is an active lad who loves his walks and exploring the world around him. At present, he can be strong on the lead as he is eager to get out and sniff everything he sees, so his adopters will need to continue working on his lead training and help him learn to walk more calmly. He is currently being trained to walk on a halti here. His absolute favourite thing in the world is playing with a ball and he just lives to play fetch! He would choose his ball over a treat any day and has proven himself to be the best ball catcher the rescue has seen!

Toucan is a clever boy who is picking things up quickly. He will benefit from a consistent routine and ongoing training to help him feel secure and understand expectations. Providing him with structure, alongside quiet resting spaces where he won’t be disturbed, will be key in helping him manage any anxieties. Although he has lived in a home, he may need some reminders about home life and skills like house training as he settles back into home life.

Toucan was adopted into a family home and though he loved the whole family, there was one isolated incident where he was snoozing in his bed and was accidentally startled by the older child in the home. Waking suddenly and feeling frightened, Toucan reacted in panic and gave a nip before immediately moving away. We believe this response was purely due to being startled while asleep, but for this reason, Toucan will be looking for an adult-only home where there are no visiting children. His adopters will need to provide him with a quiet, safe space where he can rest undisturbed and feel completely relaxed.

Toucan would be very happy to be homed as an only dog and may prefer this, but in the right circumstances we would consider homing him with a calm resident dog,

Our vets have noted that his back legs are slightly deflected outward, but this isn’t causing him any issues.

Toucan is a fun, intelligent, and affectionate boy who, with the right experienced adopters, routine, and understanding, will grow into a fantastic and rewarding companion.

Toucan has been given the Gift of Life by Alison Hale

Why is he still waiting? This handsome man would be perfect for anyone that has an active lifestyle as he has so much energy and just truly loves nothing more than being outside, with a ball.Toucan is walking on a harness and halti as he can be quite strong but with the halti he is much better, although he's not a fan and does try to get it off, he tolerates it as he knows it means outside time.He has met a few new people this week too and has done so well, he goes on long walks with one of our volunteers during the week, and also has playtime with other volunteers in one of our bigger yards and they have nothing but praise for him and really enjoy spending time with him.Toucan just needs that one person/family to take a chance on him. Someone that's going to show him what life should be like, he had a brief experience of that while living in a foster home, but now he needs his forever home with his forever people.

Another month has gone by here at the rescue and still Toucan remains, poor boy isn’t having any luck.

Recently he’s started going out for long walks with one of our experienced volunteers and to say he loves it is an understatement, come rain or shine this boy loves to be outside, either walking or running around the big yard chasing his ball.

The lady that was fostering him also comes up regularly to spend time with him and he gets so excited when he sees her, which shows that once he loves you, he loves you forever and you have a friend for life.

Toucan is a very smart boy and you can’t really fool him by pretending to throw the ball because he catches on quickly that you haven’t, also he is very good at knowing where I’m pointing to. I don’t mean if I’m next to something and pointing right at it, I mean if he can’t find his ball for example, I can point in the direction it went and he’ll look at me and go that way, very very smart boy.

As much as I love Toucan and really enjoy his company, it’s time now for him to find his forever home, I know there’s someone out there for him, the right person could be reading this right now. If you think it could be you but your hesitant, don’t be, honestly Toucan is an amazing dog and everyone that has met him has nothing but lovely things to say about him.

Toucan is a lovely boy who has settled in as though he’s always been part of the family. Once he knows you he’s very confident and affectionate, and has met family and friends - he loves everyone, including my 17-year-old nephew.

He has a big love of food (including everyone else’s!), so he is fed in his crate using a slow feeder bowl to help him pace himself. He needs to gain some weight, so we’ve been adding extra protein to his biscuits and he’s already starting to look healthier.

Toucan is house clean and travels brilliantly in the car, happily jumping in and out. He gets on amazingly well with the four dogs in the home as well as friends’ dogs.

He is comfortable with the crate and, although the door is now left open at night, he still chooses to sleep in there. Toucan can pull on the lead, which we’re currently working on. He isn’t bothered by loud noises and absolutely loves playing ball - he’s fantastic at fetch.

Toucan is a very handsome and active boy who originally came to us from a breeder. He was adopted for a short period of time, but has unfortunately found himself back in rescue. Toucan was adopted into a family home and though he loved the whole family, there was one isolated incident where he was snoozing in his bed and was accidentally startled by the older child in the home. Waking suddenly and feeling frightened, Toucan reacted in panic and gave a nip before immediately moving away. We believe this response was purely due to being startled while asleep, but for this reason, Toucan will be looking for an adult only home, where there are no visiting children. His adopters will need to provide him with a quiet, safe space where he can rest undisturbed and feel completely relaxed. Please don't let this put you off, as he is truly a wonderful boy and his previous adopters have said how wonderful he is and will be in the right home.

Toucan is is always on the go, eager to explore, and looking for his next task. He has a vibrant, happy-go-lucky personality and would thrive in an active home that can provide plenty of attention, as well as physical and mental stimulation. He is super smart and loves to use his brain and already knows "sit", "paw" and "down." He is a lovely boy who is very affectionate and really enjoys having cuddles and fuss once he gets to know you.

Toucan is confident enough that he could be homed as an only dog as long as his adopters had plenty of time to spend with him. He could also be homed with another kind resident dog and has shared his kennel well with dogs at the rescue. He can sometimes be reactive to other dogs when passing their kennels but is fine when out and about on lead. He still needs some training on the lead as he likes to be in charge, pulling us along on his travels.

Toucan has learned to walk on a harness, but he can pull and so will need adopters who can manage this and who are willing to work on this with him. He is obsessed with tennis balls and will play all day if you had the time, so he really hopes his new family will enjoy throwing balls for him!

Toucan can be a little greedy, so at the moment he is fed separately from any other dogs. He is a little and so he is now on a raw food diet to help him gain weight.

He had never lived in a home before his adoption and so home life is very new to him and he will need kindness and patience as he settles in. He was clean in his previous home but may have some accidents as he settles into a new home. With kindness, consistency, and plenty of opportunities to burn off his energy, he will make a wonderful, loyal companion for the right family.

Our vets have noted that his back legs are slightly deflected outward, but this isn't causing him any issues.

name: Maggie
description:
I'd like a quiet, adult-only home to help me relax and feel safe.

I can be an only dog or live with one dog my size or larger.

I'd like a secure garden to play in that has 6ft fencing.

I walk well on a lead and would enjoy one or two walks a day!

I have lived in a home so I know the basics.

I have been spayed and I’m ready for my new home! Read below for more!

Maggie is a very sweet girl who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

Maggie will be looking for a calm and quiet home with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and where she can settle in at her own pace. Unfortunately on one occasion in her previous home, Maggie became tangled in her harness and in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. This was purely through fear and was an isolated, one off incident, but due to this, Maggie will be looking for an adult only home.

When Maggie first returned to our care, she was a very shy girl who was unsure about new people, but since then she has settled in wonderfully and is an absolute dream. She is a very gentle girl who is so loving and confident, especially with her main carer, who has built such an incredible bond with her in a short period of time.

Maggie is now confident enough that we would consider homing her as an only dog in the right circumstances, with adopters who have experience with ex-breeding dogs and who have plenty of time to spend with her and to help her settle in. She could also live with another calm and confident resident dog, but they would need to be her size or larger. She has shared her kennel with quite a few different dogs since being back with us and she has been amazing with all of them and is happy to share food and toys. She even visits the big play yard with a larger group of dogs for a play date, which she really enjoys!

She is a playful girl and likes to keep herself entertained by playing with a tennis ball by herself, which is very sweet to watch! She does also like to run around and play with some of her dog friends too. She is also very food motivated and loves her treats.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with home life, but may need some reminders of house training. She can already walk on a lead and harness and will often check back to you for reassurance. She walks well without pulling and is lovely to take out on walks.

Maggie can be worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home, but with time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. We are ensuring she socialises with males here and she does have a male staff member as part of her care team and has bonded well with him, which is lovely. She is very people oriented and once she knows you and is comfortable with you, she will become your best friend. She absolutely adores her main carer and will follow her around like a shadow and loves a fuss and cuddle!

Since Maggie has been with us, she has shown that when she feels stressed or overwhelmed, she may try to find a way to escape by climbing. Because of this, she will need a very secure garden with boundaries of at least 6ft to help keep her safe and prevent any potential escape attempts.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and become the most lovely companion.

Maggie aka Magaluf, Magarita, Mags or Miss Maggie is a special girl. She's the kind of dog that once she's comfortable with you, you instantly feel the love she has for you from her and it's such a lovely feeling, she is very affectionate and loves her people more than anything, well, maybe not more than her food or treats but we're her second favourite.

Maggie's confidence has grown so much these past months that she's even helped some of our more shyer residents come out of their shells, and by them seeing how she is with us makes them realise that they too can be like that with us and have fusses and cuddles etc.

She is an incredible girl and it truly baffles me as to why she keeps getting overlooked. She is beautiful both inside and out and has such a fun personality. She is good with other dogs but won't necessarily need to be rehomed with another dog as we believe that she is confident enough to be an only.

Maggie will become a best friend and a true companion, and I know I'm probably a lot biased being one of her kennel mums but she truly is so so special and anyone would be lucky to have her in their life.

Maggie has settled into rescue life beautifully, but having spent over a year in a home, we are really desperate to get her back into one ASAP!

Since her arrival, Maggie has been kenneled with our lovely Bocker Eddie whom she gets along with wonderfully. She does enjoy her time with him, and would happily live alongside one resident dog - male or female, her size or larger!!

During Maggie’s time here she has formed a wonderful bond with her kennel mums who she absolutely dotes on. She’s even bonded with a kennel dad who has said she’s an absolute sweetheart, and he’s had no trouble with her too, which is so good to hear.

Maggie's kennel mummies describe her as loyal, affectionate, and loving. She really looks to them for reassurance, and when they’re around nothing else matters. Seeing as she’s grown so much in confidence, we’re happy to say she can now also be homed as an only dog too in the circumstance her adopters have lots of time to spend with her!!

Maggie isn’t really too fussed on playing with toys, but what she does love is her food & treats so gaining her trust will be a breeze!

A dog like Maggie is absolutely wasted in kennels, she’s already lived a life at home & we are so desperate to get her back into one!!

Maggie is a sweet Cockapoo who originally came to us from a breeder. She was adopted for around 16 months, but has sadly returned to us from a home following an incident with one of the smaller resident dogs in the home. During the evening, while out in the garden, Maggie was frightened by the other dog barking. Although we don't know exactly what happened, the interaction unfortunately ended in a fight and they struggled to make up or co-exist after this.

Maggie is a very shy and sensitive girl who is wary of strangers, although she does allow handling. She is trying very hard to be brave and is beginning to show small signs of progress, even getting close to taking treats from our hands, though she is not quite confident enough just yet.

Maggie is not yet confident enough to be an only dog, so we feel she would settle best in a home with one calm and confident resident dog of a similar size or larger, who can help her feel safe and reassured as she adjusts.

As Maggie has previously lived in a home, she will be familiar with the sights and sounds of a home environment. However, she may still need some support with house training as she settles into a new routine. Maggie can already walk on a lead, so she would enjoy one or two walks around the local area with the resident dog when she is settled in.

Maggie is particularly worried by men and did initially bark at the male resident in her previous home. With time, patience, and gentle handling, she slowly began to come around. Unfortunately, there was also an incident where Maggie became tangled in her harness and, in a panic, bit the hand of the male owner who was trying to help free her. Because of this, Maggie will need a calm adult-only home with patient and understanding adopters who have experience or understanding of the challenges that can come with rehoming ex-breeding dogs.

Once Maggie knows and trusts someone, she is a very sweet and happy girl. In the right calm and understanding home, with patient and dog-savvy owners who are willing to let her settle at her own pace, we are confident she will continue to make wonderful progress and slowly come out of her shell.

Maggie is currently being treated for an ear infection in the left ear.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Gail
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I could live with another calm dog, or be the only dog. I haven’t met cats

I will need a secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I am learning to walk on a lead and harness, and doing well with those I trust.

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I will be spayed before going to my forever home!

Gail has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She was a very scared little girl who found herself extremely overwhelmed when she first arrived, and it was clear she was not used to much handling or human interaction. At the beginning, Gail was very wary of people and would do her best to avoid being handled, often using warning signals to ask for space. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could panic and make poor decisions through fear. With time, patience and consistency from the staff she knows and trusts, Gail has made lovely progress and is beginning to show her softer, happier side.

Although still a nervous girl, Gail is progressing well with the staff she has built relationships with and now enjoys attention from the people she knows well. She will happily roll over for a tummy rub, which is a lovely sign of the trust she has developed, although she can still be a little unsure if she feels there is too much fuss or interaction. Her adopters will need to continue reading her body language and allow her to choose when she is ready for affection.

Gail is a happy little girl with plenty of character and a lovely playful side. She particularly enjoys carrying her favourite toys around, and these little glimpses of her personality are wonderful to see as her confidence continues to grow.

Gail spent some time recovering from a back injury, but she is now showing no signs of pain and is back to her normal self. She happily trots around as though nothing was ever wrong and has recovered brilliantly. We have also learnt a little more about Gail's feelings towards other dogs. Although she can find some dogs overwhelming, she has shown that she can cope well with a calm canine companion. She is currently sharing her kennel with a Cavalier and has even been spotted happily snuggled up in the same bed with her. This has been a lovely development and suggests that, with the right match, Gail may be able to live with another calm and respectful dog.

Gail's walking has also come on wonderfully. She is much more confident on her walks now, although she is most comfortable walking with the staff members she knows and trusts well. Her adopters will need to understand that she may need time to build the same confidence with them and should continue her training gently and at her own pace.

Gail will be looking for a calm and quiet, adult-only home with adopters who have experience of scared ex-breeding dogs and understand the importance of patience, time and reading her body language. She will need kind, understanding adopters who will allow her to take everything at a pace she feels comfortable with and continue building her confidence without putting her under pressure.

She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. She will need to learn all about home life, including house training and settling into a daily routine. Her adopters should be prepared for this to be a gradual process and give her plenty of time to feel safe and secure.

As Gail has had previous back issues, we have used a supportive back brace harness to help protect her while she builds her confidence on walks. This is something her adopters may wish to continue using in the future for extra support.

Gail is a very special little girl who has already come such a long way. She is still learning to trust and can be unsure at times, but beneath her worries is a happy, funny little dog who loves her toys and enjoys the company of those she knows. With the right people, plenty of patience and a gentle approach, we believe Gail will continue to blossom into a wonderfully rewarding companion.

Gail has been given the Gift of Life by Candice Sullivan

We're super pleased with Gail's progress over the last few weeks.

Initially, we started yarding her with other dogs. She coped really well but would tell them off if they were too lively and in her face. We then started kenneling her with a female Cavalier, and she coped very well and seemed happier in herself. We then added a lively Poodle, but Gail told her off, so now she's just with the Cavalier. So, we've learnt that Gail can cope day and night with a calm dog, and on night duty, I saw them snuggled up in the same bed.Gail's walking is much better, but only with the staff who know her well. She follows her nose on a walk and likes walking in longer grass. Gail will roll over for a tummy rub but is still a little unsure about too much fuss.Gail is a happy little girl, full of character, who loves to carry her favourite toys around, and she's not possessive of them.

Gail has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for her forever home. She is a very scared little girl who found herself extremely overwhelmed when she first arrived, and it was clear she was not used to much handling or human interaction. At the beginning, Gail was very wary of people and would do her best to avoid being handled, often using warning signals to ask for space. If she felt pushed beyond her comfort zone, she could panic and make poor decisions through fear. With time, patience and consistency from the staff she knows and trusts, Gail is making lovely progress and is beginning to show her softer side.

Although still a nervous girl, Gail is progressing well with the staff she has built relationships with and now enjoys attention from the people she knows well. She absolutely loves a tummy rub and has started to seek out familiar staff members for reassurance, showing that, given time, she is capable of forming strong bonds with the people she trusts.

Gail spent some time recovering from a back injury, but she is now showing no signs of pain and is back to her normal self. She happily trots around as though nothing was ever wrong and has recovered brilliantly. During her recovery she spent time on her own and, although she was later reintroduced to a previous canine friend, it became clear that Gail no longer enjoys the company of other dogs and does not like for them to invade her space. For this reason, she will need to be the only dog in her forever home.

She has never lived in a home before, so everything will be new to her. She will need to learn all about home life, including house training and settling into a daily routine. Gail has also recently started her lead training and has surprised everyone with how quickly she has progressed. After taking just a few tentative steps on her first outing, she was happily trotting around, sniffing her surroundings and even confidently walking over to one of her favourite people the very next day. She is proving that, with gentle encouragement, she is capable of making wonderful progress.

Gail is a very special little girl who still has plenty to learn, but she has already shown just how far she can come with the right people by her side. She is looking for experienced adopters who are willing to invest the time and patience she needs, and in return they will gain a wonderfully rewarding companion as they watch her confidence continue to grow.

This dog can be homed with a resident dog.

name: Crispin
description:
I would like a calm and quiet home where I can settle in.

I could live with other dogs, or be the only dog. I don't mind. I don't mind cats!

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on a lead and love being out and about!

I am in a foster home now so am learning all about home life and house training.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.

Since returning to us, Crispin has moved to a foster home and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be close to his people and enjoy all the love and affection he has missed out on. While he is still worried by some men due to his past experiences, once he trusts you his affectionate nature really shines through. Crispin lives alongside two cats in his foster home and he is not bothered by their presence.

Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He gets on wonderfully with the other dogs in his foster home and sleeps happily alongside them through the night. Although he enjoys their company, his foster carer feels he could also be very happy as an only dog, where he can soak up all the cuddles and attention he so craves. In the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he would thrive.

One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. He now walks beautifully on both a lead and harness, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.

As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. He has settled quickly into his foster home's routine and sleeps soundly through the night. He has had the occasional wee indoors first thing in the morning, but this has already improved over the last few days as he has established a routine. His adopters should still be prepared to continue his house training with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.

Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.

Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. Despite this, he gets around brilliantly, and you would hardly know he has any issues with his eyesight. He has also had all of his teeth removed, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.

Crispin really is a special little boy who has had a difficult start in life but has so much love to give. He is looking for a very special family who will understand his worries, cherish the affectionate little dog he has become, and give him the love and security he so deserves. In return, they will gain the most devoted and loving companion.

Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could potentially be a little older than this.

Crispin has been given the Gift of Life by Katrina Pirner

Crispin is smashing this home life. He is an absolute gentleman and will make a perfect best friend for an active person who is at home most of the time.

This week he has visited various secure fields, visited coffee shops and even popped into a pub for a cool drink while out on a street walk. He loves to be out and about with his human and then return home for snuggles on the sofa.

Although Crispin has a cataract in his right eye this does not seem to affect him at all. His luxating patellas also don't seem to bother him and his movement is 100%.

Crispin recently moved foster homes through no fault of his own. He is a gorgeous, well mannered, cuddly boy who loves his walks, his humans and his food.

He gets along with the cats and dogs in my home, though initially Crispin demanded all the attention and would push the other dogs out of the way to get his cuddles first but with careful handling this has improved over the week.

He loves to cuddle up on my bed with my own dogs and sleeps all night there. He lives for his walks and gets very excited when his lead/harness appear. He can walk on his own or with another dog for company.

He happily shares his food bowl with his foster friend Lemon Pie. Even the cats dig in with him sometimes. He is getting used to being left when I go shopping and I am extending these trips so he gets used to being without humans for a while. Crispin does bark initially when visitors come into my home but this soon subsides when he realises they will do him no harm. Keep up the good work Crispin, you've got this my boy

Crispin has been back in foster care for a week and has settled in beautifully. He is an incredibly loving, cuddly little boy who simply wants to be loved. Sadly, he was returned because he became anxious and barked whenever the man in the household moved around.

He walks beautifully on a lead and harness, sleeps soundly through the night alongside the other foster dog, and travels well. Although he is perfectly happy living with other dogs, he could also be an only dog so he can enjoy all the cuddles and affection he deserves. He has had a few little accidents indoors first thing in the morning, but over the last few days he has settled into a much better routine.

Crispin has no teeth, so he will need to remain on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He also has a cataract in one eye and the beginnings of a cataract in the other, but you would hardly know he has any sight issues as he gets around so well.

He really is a very special little boy who simply needs a loving home where he can feel safe, secure, and cherished.

Crispin originally came to us from a breeder last October. He was adopted for a few months but has come back into our care after his adopters sadly realised they were not the right match for him. Although they gave him every opportunity to settle, Crispin remained very worried whenever the male in the household was home and simply couldn't relax in his company.Crispin is a dear little boy who can still be worried and unsure at times. It is clear that he had very little socialisation in the past, and although he has made lovely progress since living in a home, he still needs patient adopters who understand that building trust takes time. He can be touch-sensitive when he is feeling anxious, so gentle handling and allowing him to approach in his own time will help him continue to gain confidence.Crispin will be best suited to adopters who understand the needs of scared ex-breeding dogs and who will give him all the time he needs to settle at his own pace. He would be happy to share his home with another kind and confident resident dog in his new home. However, in the right home, with owners who are around enough to reassure him and who have experience with ex-breeding dogs, he could also be the only dog in the home.One thing Crispin has discovered is just how much he loves going for walks! He gets wonderfully excited when it's time to head out, twirling around and eagerly waiting by the front door. Once out, he walks beautifully on a lead, is very sociable with other dogs he meets, enjoys exploring new places, and travels well in the car. Walking has become one of his favourite activities and is a lovely way to watch his confidence shine through.As Crispin has now experienced life in a home, he has become familiar with many of the sights and sounds of everyday living. However, he hasn't quite mastered house training yet, so his adopters will need to continue helping him learn with patience, consistency, and plenty of encouragement.Crispin has also shown that he forms incredibly strong bonds with his favourite person. He loves to be close by and wants to be involved in everything they are doing. Because of this, he showed signs of separation anxiety in his previous home when left for more than a couple of hours. His ideal home would therefore be one where someone is around for most of the day, and where any time left alone can be built up very gradually, helping him feel safe and secure.Crispin has a cataract in his right eye and is developing a cataract in his left eye. He has had dental work and unfortunately did need to have all of his teeth removed, so he will need to stay on a soft diet for the rest of his life. He has Grade 2 patella luxation in both hind legs, although this may continue to improve with gentle exercise as he builds muscle.Crispin is a gentle soul who has had a difficult start in life, but he has already shown that, with kindness and patience, he is capable of making wonderful progress. He is looking for a very special person who will understand his worries, celebrate his achievements, and enjoy watching him continue to blossom into the loyal and loving companion we know he can be.Crispin has a travel document, which says he is 7 years old, but we do feel he could be a little older than this.

name: Pushkin
description:
I need a calm and quiet, adult-only home where I can settle in at my own pace.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I walk well on harness but I can be spooked. Let's take it slow!

I have never lived in a home so I will need help to learn house training.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She can be nervous when meeting new people and situations, but her confidence has grown so much during her time with us. She simply needs a little time to warm up and figure people out, and once she feels comfortable her wonderful personality starts to shine through.

Pushkin is a truly lovely girl with a fun, quirky nature and a very affectionate side. She has become a firm favourite with the staff who know her, and once she trusts you she is incredibly rewarding to spend time with. She loves being around people she knows and has a gentle, sweet temperament that is impossible not to fall in love with.

Pushkin takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and help guide her through life. She gets along beautifully with other dogs and has happily shared kennels and enjoyed play dates with a variety of canine companions. She is respectful around toys and eats well alongside other dogs, making her an easy companion to have around.

She is now walking on a harness and has made lovely progress, although some things can still make her nervous when out and about. Her adopters will need to be patient and reassuring, helping her to feel safe and encouraging her when she encounters new experiences. She gains confidence from having another dog alongside her and would benefit from a calm canine friend to help her navigate the world.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life. She will need help with house training and learning the everyday routines that most pet dogs take for granted. She enjoys treats, so positive reinforcement will be a wonderful way to help her learn and build confidence. She will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

Pushkin is a special little lady who has so much love to give. With plenty of patience, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, she will continue to blossom into a wonderful companion. She has brought so much joy to those caring for her, and we know that the lucky family who adopts her will absolutely adore her.

Pushkin has been given the Gift of Life by Cherry Lewis

The last two weeks or so Pushkin, along with her kennel buddy Maggie, has been joining the big play group down the big play yard everyday (weather permitted) and she absolutely loves it. She enjoys saying hello to the other doggies there and play chases with some of them, it's so cute to watch, it makes my heart melt. It's amazing to see how much her confidence has grown, she really is blossoming.

She is quite attached to me, and does get excited to see me, she loves getting fusses from me, and is never too far from where I am if we're in a yard together, so if you like having a little extra shadow following you around she could be the girl for you.I took her out today on just a lead instead of a harness and she did amazingly, that being said for safety reasons and until she is comfortable and feels safe with you adopters would need to walk her on a harness for a while.Pushkin is just an amazing girl, I can't praise her enough and I'm always more than happy to talk about her with anyone who is interested in adopting her.

This beautiful lady brightens up my days, and as this has been a difficult week for me personally, she has been there to put a smile on my face through it.She can be nervous when you meet her initially but her confidence has grown so much she just needs time to warm up to you and figure you out, but once she's comfortable and her personality comes out she's just so much fun, and so loving. She has such a quirky personality and I absolutely adore her.Pushkin does walk on a harness, although some things do make her nervous still when out on a walk so adopters will need to be aware of this and let her know she is safe as well as some encouragement.Pushkin gets along with pretty much all dogs, any dog she has been kennelled with or introduced to for a play date she has always been so good, is fine with toys around and also eats well around the other dogs.She has never lived in a home before so her new family will have to show her the ropes and help her with her house training, be encouraging and use positive reinforcement, she does enjoy treats so they should be a big help.I'm not lying when I say I genuinely get excited to see her everyday I'm at work, she really is a little ray of sunshine.

Pushkin has come to us from a breeder and is now searching for a loving forever home. She is initially quite nervous and unsure, but once you spend some time with her she starts to come out of her shell and even begins to enjoy a fuss.

Pushkin is a sweet girl who simply needs understanding and the chance to build her confidence at her own pace. She will be looking for a calm and quiet home where she can settle in gradually and continue to blossom. She takes a great deal of comfort from the company of other dogs and becomes quite worried and stressed when left on her own. Because of this, she will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home to take her under their wing and show her that the world isn't such a frightening place.

Pushkin has never experienced life in a home before, so her new family will need to be kind, patient and understanding as she learns all about home life and new skills such as house training. She has made lovely progress with her harness training and is now walking on a harness, although she is still a little nervous when out and about. She is much more confident when she has another dog alongside her, so having a calm canine companion to help reassure her on walks will be a real benefit. She will need an adult-only home with adopters who have experience of ex-breeding dogs and who will allow her to settle in at her own pace. She will also need a secure garden with fencing of at least 6ft to ensure her safety while she adjusts to her new home.

With plenty of love, reassurance and the support of a canine friend, Pushkin will continue to grow in confidence and become a wonderful companion. She is a lovely girl with so much potential, and we can't wait to see her enjoying the happy life she truly deserves.

description:
I need an adult-only home where I can feel safe and loved.

I will need a kind resident dog to take me under their wing. I have never met cats.

I will need an extra secure garden while I get used to my new home.

I have never been on walks, but may be too scared and will need some time.

Please be patient with me, I'm nervous and learning everything from scratch.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

14-08-26 Chickpea is a gorgeous but worried little lady who has come to us from a breeder and is now looking for a loving and safe forever home. She is beginning to settle into her new surroundings but isn't comfortable around us humans just yet. She will often run away when approached and prefers to hide away in the hope that nobody notices her, and it is so heart-breaking to see.

Chickpea can be worried about being handled, and this is something that will need to happen at her own pace. Chickpea relies heavily on her canine companions for reassurance and will need at least one kind and confident resident dog in her new home that she can lean on as she learns about life in a home. Gentle garden sniffs may be a good place to start while she continues to find her paws in this big world.

Because Chickpea is such a nervous and flighty little lady, she will need an extra secure home and garden to help keep her safe. She is looking for a calm, adult-only home where she can settle at her own pace and receive all the love, patience, and TLC she needs to blossom.

Chickpea has been given the Gift of Life by Lynn McClory

description:

I can be an only dog or live with other dogs. I have never met cats.

I would like a secure garden to spend time in.

I have never been on walks, but I would love to learn!

I am learning about house training in my foster home, but will need more training.

I have a bilateral Grade 2 patella luxation.

Ursula takes comfort from having a kind and confident dog around her and will need a resident dog in her new home who can help her understand that new things are not always scary. She would benefit greatly from having a canine companion to look to for reassurance as she continues to settle and build her confidence. With the right support, we are sure Ursula will continue to become more comfortable and show her lovely personality.

She happily sleeps through the night without any accidents and is essentially house trained, which is fantastic progress. Her adopters will still need to be patient and understanding as she continues to learn about home life, lead walking and all the new experiences that come with being part of a family. She will need an adult-only calm and quiet home that can allow her to settle in at her own pace.

Ursula was underweight when she arrived but is gradually gaining weight and becoming healthier and stronger. She is a gentle little girl who needs a calm and understanding home where she can continue to build her confidence at her own pace. She may still become overwhelmed from time to time, but she is learning that she is safe and that her people will be there to reassure her.

Ursula has bilateral Grade 2 luxating patellas, but with gentle exercise this is currently not causing her any problems. Her adopters will need to be aware that this is a pre-existing condition and a disclaimer will apply, meaning it may not be covered by insurance. She also arrived with an umbilical hernia, which has since been repaired during her spay.

Ursula is a sweet and gentle little girl who has already made some lovely progress during her time in foster. She will need a family who can offer her patience, kindness and plenty of reassurance as she continues to find her confidence. With a kind resident dog by her side and a calm, loving home, we are sure Ursula will blossom into a wonderful companion.

She is gradually increasing her weight as she was underweight when she arrived.

description:
I could live with dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 +, who respect my space.

I need a doggy friend in my new home. I haven’t met cats so I’m unsure.

I'm new to lead walking and need some practice!

Please be patient with me, I need to learn house training and lead walking.

Lollipop is a lovely Bichon Frise who has come into our care from a breeder in search of a new start. She is an inquisitive and funny little girl who is already showing glimpses of her playful personality. Lollipop will happily come over to lick our fingers before darting away again, as if she's still deciding whether people are quite as interesting as her kennel friends.

Lollipop is still a nervous little girl, but she has been making lovely progress and is gradually becoming more curious about the people around her. The more time you spend with her, the more interested she becomes in you, and it is lovely to see her slowly coming out of her shell.

She definitely prefers the company of other dogs at the moment and relies heavily on her kennel friends for comfort and reassurance. She is happy to follow their lead and takes great comfort from having them around. As Lollipop gets on wonderfully with her kennel friends, she will need a kind and confident resident dog in her new home to help guide her and give her the reassurance she needs as she settles into family life and finds her paws.

Lollipop has also been making lovely progress with her harness training. She is easy to put her harness on and recently went out for her very first walk. Considering how nervous she can be, she did incredibly well! She will need plenty more gentle practice to help her become confident and comfortable with walking, and her adopters will need to continue this at her own pace.

As Lollipop has never lived in a home before, she will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. Her adopters will need to be patient and understanding as she adjusts to a whole new world and gains confidence in her surroundings.

Lollipop could share her home with older, dog-savvy teenagers aged 16 and over who can appreciate and understand that she will need a gentle, quiet introduction to the home and her own space to settle in.

She has arrived with a Grade 2 luxating patella, but her mobility appears unaffected and this may improve as she builds muscle tone. Lollipop has also arrived with severe periodontal disease and has had seven teeth extracted.

Lollipop is an active and spritely little girl with a bright future ahead of her. With the support of a kind canine friend and a patient family, we hope her confidence will continue to grow and her charming personality will shine through even more.
