name: Dutch
description:
I could live with dog-savvy teens aged 16+ who respect my space.

I need to be the only dog in my new home. No cats please!

I walk well on a lead and muzzle trained. I would enjoy an active lifestyle!

Please be patient with me, I haven’t lived in a home before.

I am already vaccinated and neutered and ready for my new home!

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet, with a heart as big as his personality. Dutch simply wants to be close to his people, whether that's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up beside you for cuddles. Being with the people he loves is all he really wants.

Dutch would love to find a home with adopters who are around for most of the day and can include him in everyday life. He thrives on human companionship and will make a wonderfully devoted shadow to his new family. He will need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and understand typical breed traits, including prey drive and the need for appropriate mental and physical enrichment.

Dutch would be best suited to life as an only dog. Although he can socialise well with other dogs of a similar size, he can become overexcited and mouthy, which may lead to frustration. Because of this, he is muzzle trained and wears a muzzle during social interactions to help him continue building positive experiences. He cannot live with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need support with house training and learning the general routines of family life. He is such a clever boy and always tries his very best to do the right thing, so we are confident he will enjoy learning with patient, positive guidance.

Dutch already walks well on a lead, although he can occasionally be reactive when passing other kennels. This is understandable in a busy rescue environment and may be something his adopters will need to continue working on. He is an energetic, happy-go-lucky boy who is more than ready to start exploring the world with his new family. An active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, training and quality time with his people would suit him perfectly.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate that he will need a gentle introduction to his new surroundings and his own space to settle in.

Dutch is bright, affectionate and full of love. He has so much to offer and is simply looking for someone to love as much as he loves them. For the right family, he will be an incredibly loyal, fun-loving and devoted companion.

Dutch has a passport and travel document.

Dutch has been given the Gift of Life by Louise Southward

Dutch, or as I like to call him, Dutchy, is honestly one of the most loving and affectionate boys you could ever hope to meet.

He's the kind of dog who just wants to be close to you. Whether it's following you around, leaning into you for fuss, or curling up for cuddles, being with his people is all he really wants. Watching him have to go back into his kennel after spending time together is heartbreaking because kennel life is just no place for a boy like him.

What makes it even sadder is that he hasn't received a single application. If I'm honest, my biggest worry is that he'll become one of our long-stay dogs, and my heart breaks at the thought of that because he simply doesn't deserve it.

He's such a clever boy and always tries so hard to do the right thing. He recently went on his first long walk with one of our wonderful regular volunteers and was an absolute angel. He took everything in his stride and made everyone so proud.

He's also been having play dates with our lovely girl, Swanny, to help him burn off some of that doggy energy while learning good doggy manners.

At the end of the day, Dutchy is just a baby. He's got the biggest heart, so much love to give, and he deserves a home where he'll be someone's whole world instead of waiting behind kennel doors. I know his family is out there somewhere; I just hope they find him before he spends another day wondering why no one has chosen him.

Dutch is an incredible boy who has come into our care from a pound in Ireland in search of a fresh start. Unfortunately, we don't know much about his history, but what we do know is that he is one of the most loving and affectionate dogs you could ever hope to meet.

He would love to find a loving home with adopters who are around most of the time and would have plenty of time to spend with him. He would need adopters who have experience with similar breeds and experience with his typical breed traits like prey drive etc.

Dutch would be best suited to being homed as an only dog as although he does socialise well with other dogs of his size, he can become over excited and mouthy which can lead to frustration. For this reason he is being trained to wear a muzzle when socialising. He cannot be homed with cats or small furries.

As Dutch has never lived in a home before, he will need to learn all about house training and the other basics of home life. With patience and guidance, we think he will adapt well and enjoy all the comforts a home has to offer.

Dutch can already walk well on a lead, though he can be a little reactive when passing other kennels, this is understandable in a busy rescue environment, but may be something his adopters will need to work with him on. He is an energetic and incredibly lovely bo who ie is happy-go-lucky in nature and is more than ready to start adventuring with his new adopters. He would love an active home where he can enjoy plenty of walks, enrichment, and quality time with his people.

Dutch could share his home with older, dog-savvy teenagers who can appreciate and understand that he will need a gentle and quiet introduction to the home, along with his own space to settle in.

He is a bright, affectionate, and fun-loving boy who is sure to make a wonderful and loyal companion for a lucky family.

Through the generosity of a Gift of Life sponsor, this dog was able to leave behind an uncertain future in Ireland and find safety and care at Many Tears. Every sponsorship helps us rescue and save more dogs in desperate need. If you would like to become part of a rescue story, please consider donating to our Gift of Life fund.

name: River
description:
I need an experienced, adult only home with no visiting children.

I would prefer to be an only dog, but I have lived with another dog. See more below.

I would like a secure garden in a quiet area.

I can walk well on a lead and would like an active home.

I need experienced adopters to work on my reactivity with me.

I am spayed and ready to find my forever home.

River originally came into our care in 2020 from a breeder and was adopted into a loving home. Sadly, her family later found they were unable to continue meeting her needs, and River has now returned to us.

River is a highly intelligent, affectionate girl who forms very strong bonds with her people. According to her previous home, once she feels safe she is extremely loving, enjoys close contact and seeks reassurance from those she trusts. She loves cuddles, gentle scratches, and being near her humans, and is very in tune with their emotions, often offering comfort when someone is feeling down.

River is a clever and enthusiastic learner who already knows a wide range of cues and enjoys training, enrichment and mental stimulation. She loves her toys, especially balls and tug toys, enjoys scent games such as “find it”, and is very food-motivated, peanut butter is her absolute favourite! She settles well at home, enjoys routine and structure, and is clean and non-destructive.

River enjoys her walks and would suit an active home with access to quieter walking routes. She walks nicely on a halti and enjoys being out and about, but can find busy environments overwhelming and may be reactive to dogs, vans or motorbikes when anxious. She will need confident handling and continued training, and should remain on lead unless in a secure area.

Although affectionate and loving, River is a sensitive dog and can struggle with unfamiliar people, visitors and loud or sudden noises such as fireworks. When frightened she may bark or retreat. For this reason, River is looking for acalm, quiet, adult-only homewithvery few visitors, ideally in arural or semi-rural setting. Her adopters must beexperienced with reactive dogs, patient, and willing to work at her pace while respecting her boundaries.

We are advised that River can occasionally display guarding behaviours towards her trusted humans, such as growling if another person enters the room while she is settled. This will need calm, confident and experienced management.

River is currently looking for a home as anonly dog, although she has previously lived with another small dog and may be able to live with a calm companion following careful introductions.

River may not be suited to everyone, but for the right home she will be an incredibly loyal, affectionate and rewarding companion who has so much love to give.

A bit about River from her previous home:

Quiver, Trevor, Clever Trevor, Trev, Piggy, Pig, Squirrel, Egg Nog Dog

Riverwill need more than one meet and greet with her prospective adopters to allow her time to build a bond and feel comfortable with them before being adopted.

River is honestly the sweetest girl once she knows and trusts you.

Recently, I’ve been taking River around our reception area and spending some quiet time with her, helping her learn that people she doesn’t know don’t have to be scary.

River is now happily taking treats from numerous members of staff she doesn’t know, something that might seem so small to some, but for River and everyone who knows her it’s a massive achievement!!

Once River lets you into her world and that special bond is built, she will be your best friend for life. She has so much love to give; she just needs someone willing to take the time to earn it!

I really, really hope River’s people find her soon. It’s heart breaking to see such a loving girl waiting in kennels when I know just how much happiness she could bring to someone’s life.

River may need a little time to trust you, but i can promise you, she will be worth every second.

Just wanted to share quick update for our wonderful River! Her kennel mum has been working on showing River that visiting the vets isn’t always a scary ordeal. Today, I popped in with her to see how it was going. I was SO impressed!

Although she was hesitant to come in, once in the vets she settled enough to have the biggest cuddles (River gives the BEST cuddles). We spent 5 minutes or so telling her how beautiful and amazing she is and made sure to head out before she got too worried.

River is honestly one of those special, once in a lifetime dogs. Once she bonds with you, she has this incredible ability to make you feel like the most important person in the world. She gives you her whole heart. Whoever adopts her will be so lucky to have her in their life!

Our gorgeous girl River is still on the search for a new home and family and hopefully her forever one. River is continuing to do very well here at the rescue and has progressed so much since being back with us.

Having lived in a home River knows a lot of commands and has been very well taught. She's clean in her kennel and isn't destructive at all. Although, she has lived in a home before she does still struggle at times with busy environments and people she doesn't know. When shes greeted by someone she doesn't know she will bark out of uncertainty but if you offer her a treat she tends to make friends with you pretty quickly. There were only a couple of people who could work with River initially when she came back to us due to her being so overwhelmed and worried but now half the rescue can work with her so shes made massive progress and I couldn't be any prouder of her.

She walks lovely on the lead and absolute loves going out for walks or down the big yard where she also loves to play fetch. We have been training River to understand that going to the vets isn't all that scary. We have been desensitising her by walking her up the vet steps and just sitting there for a moment praising her. Before, she wouldn't even go up the steps so for her to do this and sit there for a moment is massive for her. Our next step will be to open the vets door and go from there. River is such a special girl and when she trusts you she loves you with her whole heart and she genuinely does make you feel so loved. Being Rivers Kennel Mum is honestly the best and having all that love and affection from her is just utterly amazing.

River is continuing to do incredibly well here and is trusting more and more people she meets each day. It’s been lovely to see her confidence grow as she builds good relationships with other people. As part of her ongoing desensitisation, we’ve been walking River around the front of the rescue and gradually up towards the vets. This helps her learn that these environments are safe and nothing to worry about. Throughout this training we give her plenty of praise and tasty treats, and she is responding really well.

Considering everything she’s working through, she’s doing brilliantly. River is muzzle and Halti trained, as she can be reactive to certain dogs and can be strong when she first heads out on walks. We are working on her reactivity daily, and she is improving.

Her future adopters will need to continue with this training to help her keep progressing and feeling secure. River is an absolute darling. She has such a loving nature and truly makes you feel so loved when you spend time with her. With the right support and understanding, she would make a wonderful companion and a very special addition to the right home

River is a gentle girl who has previously lived in a home and is already kennel clean, giving her a great foundation for her next chapter. She can be a little cautious with new people at first, but with time and patience, she soon shows her sweet, affectionate side. Once she trusts you, River forms a lovely bond and just wants to be close to her people. She’s looking for a kind, understanding home that will give her the reassurance and love she deserves.

These wonderful souls may be older, have medical needs, or come with a few unique quirks—but they have endless love to give. Full of personality and deserving of a second chance, they come with a reduced adoption fee to help them find the perfect home. Could you be the one to give them the love they’ve been waiting for?

name: Kira
description:
This is Kira — a beautiful girl with a glossy, shiny coat. She was found as a stray in Cyprus and has been at a shelter ever since.

Kira is a large female dog who is a confident girl. Kira is super friendly and loving with people she knows and strangers alike. She gets on well with children but we would recommend any children in the home to be aged 10+ due to her size.

Kira enjoys the company of male dogs of a similar size to her. She can be picky with female dogs, but only if they are reactive with her. We also don’t recommend that she is homed with small dogs due to her size.

She is a beautifully well rounded girl who is quite easy going and just happy to be in your company. She takes treats calmly and gently and we suspect she will be a joy to train once you have formed a bond with her. Kira already walks well on the leash.

Kira is healthy, ready, and waiting for someone who sees the incredible companion she can be. She thrives with leadership and will reward the right person or family with loyalty, protection, and deep affection.

Kira will need an experienced handler who understands strong breeds and can continue guiding her with structure, consistency, and love.

Kira is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. She is fully vaccinated and spayed.

name: Rose
description:
The sweetest Rose, nearly 4 years old, neutered, medium-sized, German short haired pointer.

Sweet Rose has been in our Cyprus shelter since September 2025, quietly waiting for someone to see her.

She’s the kind of dog people walk past without realising how much she’s hurting — gentle, sensitive, and trying her best to cope in a place that overwhelms her.

Rose can be frightened at times, and the truth is, shelter life will never help her grow in the way she needs. The noise, the chaos, the constant movement… it’s simply too much for a soft soul like hers.

What she needs is a calm, patient home where she can finally exhale and learn that the world isn’t scary.

She isn’t a difficult dog — she’s a worried one. And worried dogs blossom beautifully when given love, kindness, and time. And, knowing what pointers are like, she is desperate to show some affection to humans that she can trust.

Rose would thrive in a quiet home with people who understand that progress comes in gentle steps. Someone who will celebrate the small wins, offer reassurance when she’s unsure, and show her what safety feels like.

Once she trusts you, her sweetness shines through. She is frightened of children so she can only be homed with a family if children are over the age of 15 yrs old.

This girl has waited long enough. She deserves that certain someone/couple or a family who will help her feel safe, wanted, and cherished.

Rose is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and has been tested for infectious diseases. She is fully vaccinated and spayed.

name: Donald
description:
DONALD — EVERYTHING A FAMILY DOG SHOULD BE!

Donald is a three year old male cross breed.

Donald is the dog people describe when they tell us what they are dreaming of. A gentle dog. A calm dog. A dog who loves people, understands other animals and can be trusted around children.

A dog who walks into a room and brings peace with him. Donald is all of that. He is three years old, middle-sized, and has the most beautiful nature we could ever wish for in a dog.

He adores people. He is wonderfully gentle with children, fantastic with other dogs and friendly with cats.

But those words still do not explain what it feels like to be around him.

Being with Donald feels like being close to something completely good. He looks at you with that radiant smile, comes near with such softness and settles beside you as though being together is the most natural thing in the world.

Loving Donald happens before you even realise it. We can see him beside a child, quietly watching over them. We can see him sharing his home with another dog and becoming their closest friend. We can see him carefully greeting the family cat.

We can see his smiling face waiting at the door, his head resting in someone’s lap and his beautiful presence becoming part of every ordinary day. And that is what breaks our hearts.

Because Donald should already have this life. He should already have someone who knows the sound of his paws walking through their home.

Someone who kisses his head before bed. Someone who looks at that beautiful smile every morning and knows they chose one of the finest dogs they could ever have found.

Donald is one of our rescue’s favourite dogs. We know him. We know the goodness he carries. We know how easy he is to be around and how deeply he deserves to be loved.

He asks for so little from the world, yet he brings kindness into every place he enters. All we want now is for Donald to find a home where that kindness will finally come back to him.

A home that will love him with the same gentleness he gives to everyone else. A family who will understand that they have not adopted just a wonderful dog. They have been given a gift.

3 years oldMiddle-sized boyCalm, loving, gentle and deeply kindWonderful and gentle with childrenFantastic with other dogsCat-friendlyAdores peopleRadiant, smiling and beautifully easy to share life withOne of our rescue’s most loved dogs

DONALD’S HEALTH:Fully vaccinatedNeutered4D testedBrucellosis testedMicrochippedFull RBU

Please message us if Donald feels like the calm, loving boy your home has been waiting for! He really is a one-of-a-kind boy!

name: Willow
description:
WILLOW — A LITTLE DOG WITH EVERYTHING YOU COULD EVER WISH FOR!

Willow is a two-year-old female cross breed.

Some dogs are easy to love from the very first moment.

At only two years old, this beautiful middle-to-smaller girl has the kind of character people spend years hoping to find.

She is loving.Kind.Gentle.Clever.Eager to please.

But more than anything, Willow is simply a joy to be around.

She gets along beautifully with other dogs, loves people and is wonderful with children. She has such an easy, lovely way about her — friendly without being overwhelming, affectionate without demanding, happy just to be included and close to those she loves.

Willow is smart and willing to learn. She listens, she connects and she wants to make you happy.

She is the kind of little dog who would bring warmth into a home without ever asking for much in return.

A walk beside you.A soft place to sleep.A family to call her own.

And Willow would give back everything she has — her trust, her loyalty, her happiness and her whole gentle heart.

Willow does not need to become the perfect family dog.

She is simply waiting for the family who will finally see that she belongs with them.

WILLOW — AT A GLANCE:2 years oldMiddle-to-smaller-sized girlLoving, kind, gentle and affectionateSmart and eager to pleaseWonderful with other dogsGreat with childrenLoves people and family lifeA joyful, easy and truly special little dog

WILLOW IS IN PERFECT HEALTH:Fully vaccinatedSpayed4D testedBrucellosis tested

Please message us if you believe Willow could be the little girl your home has been waiting for.

name: Ted
description:
Meet Ted – A Little Frenchie Who’s Finally Ready to Be Loved

He came into our care as a UK rescue after being pulled from a local pound by one of our trusted pound pullers.

Before that, Ted had been seized by the Metropolitan Police as part of a cruelty case, and when he arrived with us, it was clear he’d endured a great deal of neglect. His little body was covered in fleas and he was suffering from a severe flea allergy.

His skin was red, sore and painfully itchy, and he’d lost much of the fur across his back and around his face. It must have been incredibly uncomfortable, but despite everything he’d been through, Ted’s gentle nature still shone through.

Fast forward to today, and this handsome little man is a completely different dog.

Ted has now been fully assessed by our vet, has been castrated, is responding brilliantly to treatment, and his beautiful coat is growing back nicely. Best of all, his happy, affectionate personality is beginning to shine brighter every day.

What Ted is Like • Exceptionally affectionate and loving

Loves nothing more than cuddles and human company

Loves being close to his favourite person Ted has formed an incredibly strong bond with our General Manager and absolutely adores her.

He thrives on companionship and is happiest when he’s close to the person he loves. He can sometimes bark when meeting strangers, but this isn’t aggression—it’s simply his way of letting everyone know they’re there.

Once he realises everything is okay, his lovely personality quickly takes over.

Ted’s Ideal Home Although Ted gets along well with other dogs, we feel he’d truly flourish as an only dog where he doesn’t have to share his favourite person’s attention.

His perfect home would ideally be with a single person, preferably a lady, who is looking for a devoted little companion.

Someone who is home for much of the day would suit Ted perfectly, as he simply loves being part of everyday life and doesn’t ask for much more than a comfy bed, gentle walks and plenty of cuddles.

A calm home where he can continue to feel safe, secure and cherished would be everything this little boy has ever dreamed of.

Why We Love Ted Ted is proof that kindness can change a life.

Despite the neglect he suffered, he hasn’t lost his trust in people.

Instead, he greets each day with a wagging tail, a hopeful heart and an endless supply of love to give.

He isn’t looking for a life of excitement or adventure. He’s looking for his person. Someone who will adore him just as much as he’ll adore them.

After everything this little boy has endured, we so desperately want to find him the forever home he has always deserved. Could that be with you?

Could You Give Ted His Happy Ending? If you think you could offer Ted the safe, loving home he’s been waiting for, please visit: www.savingandrehomingstrays.org

Potential adopters must be willing to travel to Ayr to meet and collect Ted. Let’s make sure the rest of Ted’s story is filled with nothing but love, comfort and happiness.

name: Laura
description:
Our extra special girl Laura is approximately three years old and the most stunning medium sized cross breed. Laura weighs just twelve kilos and measures twelve inches from shoulder to paw.

Having been found abandoned on the streets, Laura has been in our Cyprus shelter for one month.

Laura can be best described as incredibly close to canine perfection.

Her smile is perpetual, her eyes are bright and engaging, her ears are prize winning, her teeth are shining white, and her glorious tri-colour coat is enhanced by an array of freckles and a pigmented tummy.

She adores her play time with her friends and engages beautifully with her bubbly sweet personality. If ever there was a prime adoption candidate designed to make a family unbelievably happy it’s Laura.

She walks nicely on her lead and enjoys her time in the car. Laura seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Daisy
description:
DAISY — SHE NEEDS A HOME TO SHOW WHO SHE REALLY IS!

Daisy is a three year old cross breed female.

Daisy is always smiling. Even in kennels, even while keeping herself just a little apart, that beautiful smile is there. She is three years old, small, gentle and full of the sweetest little character.

She loves other dogs, enjoys being around people and carries a quiet happiness that never seems to leave her face. But we do not believe kennels show us the whole Daisy. She is not scared. She is not timid.

She simply keeps a little distance around people, as though she is waiting for life to become softer before she gives us everything that is inside her. And we truly believe that life will begin in a home. Away from kennel noise.

Away from constant movement. Inside a peaceful space where she can learn the rhythm of her people, find her favourite bed and finally understand that she belongs there.

That is where Daisy will bloom. We can already see glimpses of the girl waiting underneath.

A loving little soul. A smiling companion. An adorable character who wants to be close, but needs the right surroundings to fully relax and shine. Daisy is wonderful with other dogs, and a calm, friendly dog may help her settle beautifully into family life.

She is never pushy or demanding. She simply needs a home where closeness can grow naturally.

Kennels are keeping Daisy waiting between two lives. She has left the kill shelter behind, but she has not yet reached the life she was saved for. She should be waking up in a warm home.

She should be walking beside her people. She should be carrying that lovely smile from room to room, slowly becoming more affectionate, more confident and more herself with every passing day.

Daisy does not need fixing. She needs the chance to live. And we believe that once she steps out of kennels and into the right home, this beautiful little girl will finally show everyone just how much love, happiness and personality she has been carrying all along.

DAISY — AT A GLANCE:3 years oldSmall mixed-breed girlWonderful with other dogsLoving, gentle and always smilingAdorable, never pushy and full of quiet characterNeeds a calm home where she can relax and truly bloomCould happily live with a friendly canine companion

Fully vaccinatedSpayed4D testedBrucellosis testedMicrochippedFull RBU

Please message our adoption page if you can give Daisy the home life she needs to become everything we know she can be. Daisy is already smiling. Now she needs a home that will give her every reason to shine!

name: Captain
description:
Captain is a 5 year old male Cross-Breed.

Captain came into our care from another rescue and since being with us has ensured every day is full of fun and excitement.

He is obsessed with food and isn’t guilty of stealing your lunch.

Very bouncy and full of joy Captain will require a home with older teenagers due to his long legs and is happy as the only animal.

Sadly, he is avoidant of other dogs and prefers human companionship.

His prey drive is very high, and he is potentially Bull lurcher in breed, so he is walked on lead with a muzzle and enjoys off lead exercise within a secure field.

name: Kylo
description:
Kylo is a 4 year old, medium sized, lab-cross and is literally the friendliest boy. He simply adores being around humans and will be the best companion.

Oh and he knows some tricks! When he arrived at the shelter he was microchipped so he had some sort of home at some point in his life.

He craves love and attention from everyone he meets, even if just meeting for the first time. He’s very smart and will be a joy to train.

Kylo is a very sweet boy and has a puppy-like energy where he is just happy and excited to be with you and show off his tricks. And he’s very food oriented!

Some dogs in the shelter he accepts, others he doesn’t. Although this can be a product of the stress of shelter life, it’s best if he is an only dog.

Kylo can be quite energetic and will likely need an active home. He would even make a good running buddy. He already walks well on the leash.

Kylo can be adopted in the UK or Cyprus. His adoption fees are sponsored so, if travelling to the UK, we are just asking for travel costs to be covered.

He is ready to fly. He is vaccinated, castrated, and has had a full health check and blood tests for infectious diseases.

Full rescue back-up is provided by Saving Souls Animal Rescue, a UK-based registered charity.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Hannah
description:
Our extra special girl Hannah is approximately three years old and a cross breed at the very bottom end of medium with a strong beagle appearance.

Hannah weighs a perfect eleven kilos and measures thirteen inches from shoulder to paw. Having been found abandoned on the streets, Hannah has been in our Cyprus shelter for three weeks.

Having clearly been preloved, Hannah is finding shelter life not to her liking. She is longing for her forever home away from the noise and bustle.

Hannah leans towards being timid but will thrive and blossom with her very fortunate adopting family. She yearns for peace and routine and will repay love and kindness with huge premiums.

Hannah’s appearance is exceptional in every aspect. Her tricolour coat is just glorious with some freckles and the loveliest ears ending in a point. Her kind, empathetic and loving nature abounds. Hannah is a truly wonderful adoption candidate.

She enjoys her time in the car and walks nicely on her lead. Hannah seems to mix perfectly well with other dogs, cats and children.

name: Iris
description:
Iris is 9 weeks old female Presa Canario and ready for her new home.

Iris and her brothers and sister were born here at Ravenswood, so have had the best start possible.

They have been well socialised , handled and have been wormed regulary.

Iris is a happy, confident puppy, she will need a home with large breed experience. She will need to be well socialised and needs a home that are willing to continue her training throught her life.

Presa’s are big strong dogs, and need homes that are happy to take that on.

Iris will have her first vaccination, and be chipped prior to leaving. She will have to be neutered when old enough and we will require proof this has been done.

If you think you can offer Iris her forever home please get in touch.

name: Lyric
description:
Lyric is a medium sized crossbreed aged around four years old. Lyric fostered Norwich Norfolk.

We discovered this absolute beauty queen in the Botosani public shelter when we visited in March. It’s taken a few weeks for her turn to come to arrive in the UK, she’s here now and ready for a new life.

Lyric is a sweet and gentle girl with a cheeky side that’s just beginning to emerge.

Once settled she does tend to love her human a little too much and can become possessive/protective over them if allowed to and will therefore need an adopter who is experienced with shepherd types or similar natured dogs.

Lyric is living very happily with multiple other dogs in her foster home but could become bossy if allowed to “rule the roost”.

She can live with dog savvy, confident cats but would be likely to chase more timid or skittish cats. She needs an adult home environment and would be best suited to a single person or couple.

name: Raggie
description:
Raggie is a medium sized crossbreed aged around ten years old. Raggie fostered Norwich.

Raggie was rescued from a kill shelter in Romania when he was a youngster and has lived in a private shelter since then.

Despite having a nice place to stay all these years it was not a proper home and we really want his retirement to be something more comfortable.

Raggie is a sweet and inquisitive boy who enjoys the company of other dogs and is absolutely fine with the safe rescue cat. He would like a quietish home environment with at least one other calm dog in residence.

He is not really used to a lot of human contact but is adapting well to human interaction and beginning to really seek it out. He has surpassed all expectations as we expected him to be much more independent.

He’s just a dear old chap that doesn’t really ask much out of life at all.

name: Malia
description:
Malia is a medium sized crossbreed aged around two years old. Malia fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Malia and her mother were rescued from a crowded shelter in Romania. Her mother came to the UK before her and has since been rehomed.

Malia was very shy and distrustful on arrival due to lack of social interaction in her early life. She has since gotten used to her foster carers and is gentle and attentive with them though still a little hand shy.

She will continue to grow in confidence in the coming weeks and months with kindness and patience.

Malia mixes well with other dogs and will need another steady dog in full time residence in her forever home. She walks nicely on a lead but needs more practise and experience as she’s still playing a little catch up.

She doesn’t like cats and would like a home with no children under the age of twelve.

name: Toffee
description:
Toffee is a medium sized crossbreed aged around eighteen months old. Toffee fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Toffee came into our care a few months ago from another rescue who we regularly work with. Sadly they had no foster place for him and he was not progressing in a kennel environment.

He arrived, like many have before him, scared of humans because his last experiences with them hadn’t been good ones. It took many weeks to get him to walk on a lead and even longer to accept human touch.

Finally we feel he is ready to find his forever home.

He is now a fun loving and cheeky chap who enjoys the company of the humans he’s learnt to trust. He will need an experienced adopter who will be willing to follow advice and wait patiently for that trust to extend to them too.

Believe me he is worth the wait! He is playful and friendly with other dogs and will need at least one full time canine companion in his forever home.

He could live with respectful children aged twelve plus.

If your dog pulls on the lead, then we can advise you on training methods that avoid harm.

name: Fry
description:
Fry is a small crossbreed aged around five years old.

Fry initially came into our care several months ago from the Botosani public shelter in Romania. He was a submissive little chap who had quite a hard time in there.

He was quite quickly adopted and for a while things went well. Unfortunately as he found his feet he became possessive over beds etc and has recently been returned for this behaviour.

Since his return Fry has been learning that possessive behaviour isn’t accepted here and with firm rules and boundaries and confident handling the issue is manageable.

He will however need an experienced adopter who will not be phased by “stroppy terrier” behaviour.

Fry gets on well with other dogs but would be quite happy as the only dog in the home. He wouldn’t want to live with any dog that was too boisterous or in his face.

He ignores the safe rescue cat and will need an adult home environment. Fry enjoys his walks and is good on and off lead. He is an affectionate little boy who enjoys cuddles and fuss.

name: Boris
description:
Boris is a large crossbreed aged around ten to eleven years old. Boris fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Boris has come into our care recently after spending many years in a private shelter in Romania. This big bear of a dog has spent much of his life confined in a pen. To watch him experience the new freedoms of a foster home is really very special.

Boris is a dear old chap who loves every body he meets. He is getting on well with the other dogs in his foster home but would be very happy to live as the only dog in the home. He will need a cat free home but loves children of all ages.

name: Conga
description:
Conga is a medium sized crossbreed aged around four years old. Conga fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Previously to arriving in the UK recently, Conga has spent the whole of his life in the Botosani public shelter in Romania.

Astonishingly he has retained a happy disposition and love of humans despite the awful conditions there.

Conga is a loyal and loving boy who will follow you to the ends of the earth once you show him kindness. He will need some basic training to stop him jumping up to gain attention which we have started here.

He gets on well with other dogs and would benefit from another dog in his forever home but we don’t feel it’s essential. He could live with respectful children aged twelve plus.

name: Lilly
description:
Lilly is a medium sized collie cross aged around six years old. She originally came from Botosani Public shelter in Romania – and has surprisingly been with us in foster for over a year now, patiently waiting her turn. Lilly fostered Milton Keynes.

She is a very calm, obedient and quiet girl who doesn’t ask for much. Doesn’t even jump on the furniture!

Loves to run and play with the resident dogs and would love to have a dog companion in her forever home.

She’s still a bit shy around new people but her confidence is growing each day.

What Lilly likes:country walks;rolling on the grass;treats in a kong toy;gentle strokes;calm environment.

What Lilly doesn’t like:traffic;loud or sudden noise;

Lilly pays no attention to the cats in her foster home. Whenever they approach she shows no interest.

name: Gabriel
description:
Gabriel is a medium sized crossbreed aged around eight years old. Gabriel fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Wow, I can’t believe I’m typing this boy an album, I don’t think anyone ever thought that I would….

Since the very building of the shelter, Gabriel was the heart and soul of Crivatu, he was moved there before the shelter was even finished being built and we have known and loved him since meeting him after lock down on our first visit there.

He was an integral part of my family summer holiday there a couple of years ago and a favourite with my adult children. He is special, I can’t tell you why he is but he just is and he is family to us all.

Every time we left at the end of a trip and he had to go back to spending his nights in a pen it hurt us and he cried for three days. He is perhaps not the easiest dog and he needs someone with a good level of experience.

He can be the only dog in the home or he can share his home with another non too boisterous dog. He can object when told to get off furniture, but he is very manageable to anyone who has dealt with these issues before.

He is a pleasure to walk, never reacted when the street dogs followed us down the street yapping at him, but he doesn’t like large vans or Lorries passing him. He is not good with cats.

This boy is just something special and anyone adopting him will have the most loyal friend. He lives for his walks and is so grateful for all time put into him.

name: Lizzie
description:
Lizzie is a medium sized crossbreed aged around two to three years old. Lizzie fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Lizzie was one of multiple dogs seized by the police in Romania from a hoarder who kept about ninety dogs in a caravan and a car. She has been waiting in a private shelter since she was a pup for an offer of adoption to no avail.

Lizzie arrived in our care a few months ago and was adopted shortly after. Sadly she was returned to our care a few weeks ago.

She’d been doing so well there and they loved her but unfortunately got protective of her female owner against visitors to the home.

We feel that she now needs a home with another dog in the hope that she doesn’t feel solely responsible to keep her family safe.

We have waited a few weeks to repost her for adoption to reassess her. She has been an absolute joy back in her foster pack. She is friendly and playful with everyone and loves to play with the other dogs and is an absolutely perfect house guest.

She will need an adult only environment with experiences adopters.

name: Duke
description:
Duke is a six year old male Pointer. Duke is a very handsome boy!

Duke was handed in to the shelter we work with in North Spain by a hunter as he was no longer wanted. He has a slender and elegant figure, he is of medium size and a balanced character and is respectful of the other dogs at the kennels.

Duke currently shares his kennel with a female Setter. He shares the space without problems including at dinner time.

Duke is a little shy if he doesn’t know you, but he quickly gains confidence and approaches timidly seeking cuddles and caresses.

His recall is good within the confines of the shelter but it would be a different matter on an exciting walk. He loves to run around the enclosure and stretch his long legs.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Duke a home, he is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Duke is currently in Spain but he is ready to travel to his forever home in the UK.

name: Mandy
description:
Mandy is a 5-year-old female Cross-Breed. She’s a calm, gentle soul who has already been spayed and fully vaccinated, weighing around 23 kilograms.

Mandy is currently safe in a private shelter in Romania after being rescued from a kill shelter earlier this year — and now she’s patiently waiting for her forever home.

This lovely girl has a relaxed, easy-going personality. She loves simple pleasures like pottering around a garden and finding a comfy spot to nap in.

Mandy doesn’t need a high-energy household; she’s happiest in a calm environment where she can enjoy her surroundings and be close to her people.

She gets along beautifully with other dogs and has no trouble sharing her space with feline friends either. Mandy’s sociable yet serene nature makes her a wonderful companion for homes with other pets.

She could also live with dog-savvy children aged 10 and above, as long as they understand her gentle and steady temperament.

Although Mandy enjoys the company of other dogs, she doesn’t necessarily need one in her home. She’s quite content being the only dog as long as she receives love, care, and companionship from her humans. What she does need, however, is a secure garden — a place to wander, relax, and soak up the sunshine.

Mandy represents everything lovely about a rescue dog: calm, affectionate, and grateful for every bit of kindness shown to her.

Her adopters will also receive full rescue backup and support throughout the adoption process and for the lifetime of the dog, ensuring Mandy’s smooth transition into her new life.

Home checks and an adoption donation apply, as the rescue ensures every placement is the perfect fit. Whoever opens their home to Mandy will be rewarded with a loyal, gentle friend who embodies peace and love in every wag of her tail.

name: Reyna
description:
Reyna is an eight year old female Border Collie. Reyna is in a wonderful foster home in Cambridgeshire.

She shares her foster home with several resident dogs and although we think she’s lived a sheltered life without much interaction, with their guidance, she’s really learned how to interact and enjoy the company of other dogs.

Although very nervous when she first arrived, she has slowly but surely come out of her shell with the guidance of her foster family and has even been for some little adventures to a cafe!

She can still be shy of new people but she’s affectionate with everyone, especially her foster mum who’s a firm favourite since she does all the walks!

Her character is coming out as she gains confidence and she can be a lovable cheeky monkey! She’s a real joy to watch as she grows and learns that the world can be a fun and safe place to be.

She travels well in the car, eager to jump in for a walk! She’s also picked up house training very well too. Her foster mum calls her the perfect dog.

She gets on well with all the resident dogs but the other resident collie is a firm favourite! She is looking for a home with a kind and patient family who can carry on all the amazing work of her foster home

Reyna is a Border Collie. Her Spanish passport says she is eight years old but the vet thinks she might be younger.

Reyna was given to the shelter in Spain along with her three puppies (Ares, Sena and Zeus) by a family who kept her outside her whole life. We think she had been chained up for most of that time and hadn’t had the chance to interact with humans much or other dogs.

Reyna’s Spanish passport says she’s almost 8 years old but the vet thinks she might be younger.

If you are interested in giving wonderful Reyna a home, she is available at Setter Brittany Pointer Rescue. Reyna is currently in Cambridgeshire but she is ready to travel to her forever home. Will that be with you?

name: Francis Rossi
description:
Our very own Francis Rossi is looking for an adoring, fun-filled home to match his great big heart! He is 3 years old, 70cm from floor to shoulder, and weighs about 45kg.

Francis is the epitome of a loving companion. He will make you laugh while simultaneously melting your heart. He was fearful to begin with, but now greets people with a bright eye and a very bushy tail.

Francis walks well on a lead, doesn’t pull, and is not bothered when meeting or walking with other dogs. He’s good around horses and sheep too. He hasn’t been cat-tested but has a low prey drive.

Francis loves a zoomy so he’d like a home with a big garden where he can really go for it and impress you!

Francis is a healthy boy – vaccinated, castrated, and blood tested. He is currently in foster in West Sussex but can be adopted anywhere in the UK. He will have full rescue backup from Mastin Matters.

If you’d like to see some videos of this gorgeous boy, please get in touch!

name: Casper
description:
Casper is a 5-year-old male Cross-Breed. He sadly lost his home after his owner passed away, and the family who remained couldn’t take him when they moved.

He had previously lived with Stella and was adopted not long after her, so all this upheaval has been a lot for him to handle.

Casper is a 5-year-old no gender Cross-Breed. Even with everything going on, he stays incredibly friendly and absolutely adores people and other dogs.

He’s house trained too, which makes things so much easier for anyone welcoming him into their home.

Casper is a 5-year-old no gender Cross-Breed. He’s currently in Bosnia and will be able to travel mid-January, ready for a fresh start with someone who can give him stability again.

He has already been vaccinated, blood tested, microchipped, neutered, and treated for fleas and worms.

Casper is a 5-year-old no gender Cross-Breed. Meadow of Hope Dog Rescue in the UK is providing rescue support for him, ensuring he’s backed by a team that genuinely wants the best for him.

Anyone interested in adopting him will need to complete an application and home check, but he’s truly worth it.

name: Skye
description:
Skye is a 2 year old female Cross-Breed and is large in size. She can live with confident cats, can live with other dogs following successful meets, and would be best suited to a home with children aged 16 years and over. She is based in Cheshire.

Skye is reactive to new people visiting the home, so she will need a household with minimal visitors. Her new family will need to continue working with her on this.

With the people she knows and trusts, Skye is a happy, loving, and affectionate girl. She is a big puppy at heart with a goofy personality. She loves playing with her toys and enjoys enrichment such as kongs and lick mats.

Skye accepts a collar, harness, and lead. She is very strong on the lead and does pull. She can be highly reactive on walks, particularly towards other dogs and people.

However, she has made friends with a small dog near her home and is good with them.

Skye is toilet trained and crate trained. She does display destructive behaviour towards items such as furniture and remote controls. The cause of this is unknown, but it is improving over time.

She can be left alone but needs to be crated to prevent destruction. She settles well overnight and travels well on short car journeys.

Skye can also be reactive to people walking past the home, so a quiet location or a property with a private entrance would be ideal. She may show guarding behaviour around high value treats such as bones with other dogs, so these should be avoided.

name: Alba
description:
Alba is a 11 year old female Terrier Cross. She is a playful and affectionate dog who adores spending time with people and children, making her a delightful companion in a family setting.

Alba is house trained, which shows she is well-behaved indoors, and she also walks well on a lead, demonstrating good leash manners that make outings enjoyable for both her and her owner.

Alba has a history of being reactive towards other dogs, but she has made significant progress and can now go on walks alongside other dogs without issues.

She shows a preference for male dogs, which is important for potential adopters to consider when introducing her to new canine friends.

Alba is best suited for families with children over 8 years old and she cannot live with cats, ensuring a safe and harmonious home environment.

Alba is microchipped and fully vaccinated, including rabies, infectious diseases twice, and will receive the Bordetella vaccine before transport.

She has been castrated and tested negative for Mediterranean diseases and Brucellosis, and she received nasal treatment for kennel cough before travel.

Her health and safety are carefully monitored, reflecting the high standard of care provided by Ninas Haven.

Adopters should note that an adoption fee of £150 applies, along with a home check, and full rescue backup is provided by Ninas Haven.

Alba’s well-rounded personality, progress with dog interactions, and affectionate nature make her a fantastic companion for the right home.

name: Freya
description:
Freya is a 3 year old large female Cross-Breed.

Freya doesn’t like people walking past her kennel. She is quite nervous of people but once she gains trust she is very happy and loves cuddles.

She is very treat oriented which is good but she does try and snatch the treats. She’s great with lead and collar and walks well no problem at all. She’s fine on walks and walking past people but she starts barking at dogs and is unsure.’

Freya can be nervous of people coming into the home which will cause her to bark and growl, she is best meeting people out on a walk first so she can become comfortable with them.

She is then generally okay within the home however she can sometimes bark if visitors make sudden movements which startle her so will need to use her safe space longer term. She is not crate trained so would prefer a dog bed.

Freya is toilet trained and travels well in the car. It is felt Freya could do very short periods on her own but this would need to be built up very slowly in her new home. Therefore, she will need someone that is home all day.

Freya needs a female primary carer, ideally in a female only home or with a confident, very dedicated male who can slowly build a relationship with her.

Using a safe space long term so that she feels safe, builds confidence and has somewhere she can go if she feels overwhelmed before trigger stacking is absolutely vital for Freya.

Her new home will need to be committed and dedicated to allowing her to go at her own pace in order to settle and become comfortable in her new home.

Once she has built up a bond based on trust she will show how loving and affectionate she really is.

name: Barry
description:
Barry is a 9-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a medium-sized boy who is described as friendly and happy once he knows and trusts you. When he feels comfortable, his warm and affectionate personality really comes through.

Barry is a 9-year-old male Cross-Breed who was rescued off the streets by UK volunteers during a recent trip. This background means he will need understanding and patience as he settles into a home environment.

Despite his past, he shows a strong desire for human connection.

Barry is a 9-year-old male Cross-Breed who absolutely loves attention and enjoys being fussed over. He thrives on affection and would enjoy a home where he can receive plenty of one-to-one interaction.

His loving nature makes him very endearing once a bond is formed.

Barry is a 9-year-old male Cross-Breed who can feel a little nervous around new people. He may take some time to relax, but with calm handling and reassurance he is able to build trust. A patient and consistent approach will help him feel secure.

Barry is a 9-year-old male Cross-Breed who cannot live with other dogs. He is best suited to being the only dog in the household, where he does not have to share attention or space. This setup will allow him to feel more settled and confident.

Barry is a 9-year-old male Cross-Breed who cannot live with cats or children. He would be best suited to an adult-only home where his needs and boundaries are clearly understood.

In the right environment, he would make a loyal and affectionate companion.

name: Jess
description:
Jess is a 7-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a medium-sized boy who lacks confidence when out on the lead and currently will not go very far. This is something that will need continued work and patience in his new home.

Jess is a 7-year-old male Cross-Breed who will need a secure garden with direct access. Having a safe outdoor space will help him feel more comfortable and reduce pressure while his confidence builds. A quieter home environment would suit him best.

Jess is a 7-year-old male Cross-Breed who has shared a kennel with various dogs during his time at OSH. He prefers calmer and quieter dogs and would be best matched with a similar canine companion. Busy or overly energetic dogs may overwhelm him.

Jess is a 7-year-old male Cross-Breed who has recently begun waiting at the front of his kennel to go out. He gets very excited around food and has started barking more as a result. These behaviours appear linked to his increasing engagement with his surroundings.

Jess is a 7-year-old male Cross-Breed who is slowly making improvements overall. The kennel environment is noisy, which can be challenging for him and affect his confidence levels. A calmer household would likely help him continue progressing.

Jess is a 7-year-old male Cross-Breed who cannot live with cats and would be best suited to a home with children aged 15 and over.

Older children are more likely to understand his need for space and reassurance. With time and consistency, he has the potential to settle well in the right home.

name: Barney
description:
Barney is an 5 year old male Cross-Breed.

He has spent his entire life in a foster shelter, where he has been well cared for and socialised.

As a friendly and affectionate dog, Barney has lovely markings that make him stand out, including a distinctive patch over his eye that adds to his charm.

Despite his time in the shelter, Barney remains a cheerful and loving companion who is eager to find his forever home.

He has been cat-tested and has shown he can live harmoniously with cats, which is a positive trait for potential adopters with feline friends.

He is friendly with other dogs, friendly but nervous of humans.

Barney is expected to be a smallish adult, making him a suitable choice for those who prefer a smaller dog.

He is microchipped, vaccinated, and has undergone various tests to ensure his health and well-being.

Additionally, Barney comes with a pet passport, which can be advantageous for future travel or if moving abroad.

Being one of several siblings also awaiting adoption, Barney’s sweet and friendly nature makes him a wonderful candidate for any family looking to add a loving dog to their home.

name: Raegan
description:
Meet Raegan. Raegan is a 9 month old female Cross-Breed and is small to medium in size.

Raegan is a lovely girl to someone she builds a bond with but is nervous of strangers. She will do better in a home with fewer people and not many visitors.

But someone able to dedicate time to her and help with training for her guarding would be considered too.

Raegan is toilet and crate trained. She wears a harness whilst out and walks well. She is doing well with other unknown things around her when she’s with confident dogs.

She showed anxiety when left alone previously but in her foster home she can be left with other dogs for up to 4 hours; if she was living without dogs, any alone time would need to be built up gradually.

She sleeps well overnight in the foster’s room but in a dog bed or with other dogs dotted around the home. She travels well in the boot of the car with no travel sickness. She has not been destructive.

Raegan’s foster says, ‘Raegan is a dear little dog, she’s feisty and full of personality. She loves living with other dogs but is not so confident with humans (besides me). She plays all day and is a typical cute puppy’.

name: Marvel
description:
Marvel is a 6-year-old male Cross-Breed. He’s a medium-sized lad with a sensitive streak, especially when it comes to meeting new people at home. Despite this, his first family said he settled quickly and was happy to greet visitors once he felt safe.

Marvel accepts a collar and has previously used a harness without issue. His lead manners are mostly decent, with only the occasional pull, and even then it’s nothing dramatic.

He does, however, become fear-reactive around lively dogs on walks, so he needs space and understanding from other dog walkers.

Marvel is fully toilet trained, though he’s not crate trained, and he’s never shown any destructive behaviour. He can be left alone for a few hours without trouble, although he will bark at outside noises.

He sleeps soundly overnight with his owner and travels well in the car.

Marvel is great with food and loves his treats, showing no signs of resource guarding at all. His former families describe him as a loving, snuggly boy once trust is built. They also say he’s clever, affectionate, and happiest chilling beside his humans.

Marvel thrives best in a calm environment without small children or other dogs. With patience and reassurance, he’ll grow into a loyal and devoted companion. His gentle nature shines through once he feels safe and understood.

name: Sadie
description:
Sadie is a beautiful, fun loving girl pup ready to join her new family both outside on walks and on the sofa of an evening.

She was rescued in Cyprus when she was 5 months old. But no home offers were made so we have recently flown her to a foster home in Milton Keynes in the hope that now she can be met by prospective adopters she may find her perfect family.

Sadie is a stunning, very clever, big puppy with the sweetest nature. She’s incredibly well behaved, gets along perfectly with all dogs, and is already showing wonderful obedience for her age.

This gorgeous girl is also super cuddly, she loves nothing more than being close and showering her people with affection.

Sadie really is the full package: smart, social, gentle, and loving.

She is a mixed breed, possibly with a bit of Anatolian Shepherd, weighing 26 kg at present and expected to be around 32kg when fully grown.

So she will be a large girl. When you look at her photos you will see just what a beautifully stunning model girl she is, long legs to boot!

Sadie was a very happy, playful girl in our kennels, enjoyed playing with the other pups and dogs and being with our volunteers. Now she is in the UK this is translating well into her foster home and she is learning about home life quickly.

Already learned the basic about house training, sleeping soundly at night, she is now learning to walk on the lead and enjoy her time out and about, meeting other dogs nicely and enjoying a weekend treat of a puppuccino from the local coffee shop!

She is living happily with teenagers and in view of her size we would prefer any children in her new home to be dog savvy and older.

Sadie is a typical pup who will benefit from her adopters spending quality time with her to help her settle in her new family life and continue on her journey to learn what is expected of a family dog.

Her foster family say she is a beautiful, well balance puppy with lots of fun and zest!

If you are looking for a good sized pup with potential, please when contacting us tell us a little about yourself:

3. Your garden and fencing (height at lowest point)

5. Ages of children in the home or who visit

6. How long Sadie may be left alone, and how she’ll fit into your lifestyle

Sadie is vaccinated, and microchipped. A minimum adoption donation of £300 applies.

Adoption is subject to a satisfactory application, home check, neutering agreement at his adopters expense when she reaches the appropriate age as agreed with your vet and agreement to our adoption conditions.

We are committed to the lifelong care of our dogs and will always accept their return when space allows. In situations where space is limited, we will endeavour to rehome the dog directly from its current home.

Under no circumstances may the dog be transferred to another UK rescue organisation.

name: Bruno
description:
Meet Bruno – A Gentle Soul Looking for a Fresh Start

Bruno, a 3 year old male American Bulldog, came into our care through no fault of his own after his owner sadly passed away. Following this, poor Bruno experienced a very distressing situation when he was removed from his home.

He was at risk of being euthanised in police kennels, but thankfully we were able to step in just in time and give him the second chance he deserved.

Understandably, Bruno arrived feeling nervous and unsure of the world. But with patience and kindness, he’s been growing in confidence every day.

He’s formed lovely bonds with our staff, enjoys meeting new volunteers, and absolutely loves his gentle walks—plodding along, taking in the scenery, and having a good sniff.

Once he gets to know you, Bruno shows his true nature: a sweet, affectionate boy who loves fuss and closeness. Despite his size, he walks beautifully on the lead—you sometimes forget he’s even there!

As we don’t know much about his background, Bruno will need a quiet, calm, child-free and pet-free home where he can fully decompress, feel safe, and learn to enjoy life again at his own pace.

Bruno is currently staying in our Wrexham kennels, but what he truly needs is a loving home of his own. He’s been through so much, yet he still has so much love to give.

Could you be the one to offer Bruno his forever home?

A link to our adoption process can be found below:

https://celandinewoodanimalrescue.org.uk/adoption-processes/

Once we have received your application this will be reviewed by our dog team and if you are a suitable match one of our volunteers will be in touch within 7 days to discuss your application in more detail.

You will then be invited to meet the dog, and we encourage 2-3 meet & greets for you to get to know your chosen dog, we are happy to introduce you to multiple dogs on the day of they are suitable matches.

We do request all household members attend meet & greets including resident dogs.

If successful we will request a home check at this stage along with proof of identification and address. We will require written permission from a landlord for all applicants in rented accommodation.

Please note we require all resident dogs to be neutered and up to date with vaccinations before we will proceed with the adoption.

name: Bear is a male 2
description:
Bear is a 2-year-old Belgian Malinois Cross American bulldog

Bear is currently in our kennels in Wrexham, North Wales

Bear, our 2-year-old heartbreaker, struts his stuff on the leash like a pro, gives paw like a true gentleman, and even tucks himself in at night!

We suspect he’s part Malinois, part bull breed, and all mischief. Sure, he can jump a 6ft obstacle and redecorate with the best of them, but hey, who doesn’t love a bit of chaos?

Bear’s health is top-notch, and his intelligence is off the chats—now if only we could convince him to use it for good!

Bear is fine with other dogs when out and about but we would not rehome him with another dog in the home. He will benefit from still being socialised with other dogs outside the home.

He is best suited to a home with older children only, where he can enjoy structure, calm, and consistency.

Someone with breed experience is important as Bear is a high energy dog who is very intelligent – his new owner will need to be able to give him enough physical and mental stimulation and in reward you will have an amazing dog!

Bear is house trained, crate trained and good with everyone he meets

name: Lenny
description:
Lenny is a 4-year-old small sized American Bulldog cross.

Lenny is currently in our kennels in Wrexham, North Wales.

Lenny is a 4-year-old American Bulldog cross with a sweet and gentle nature. Although a little unsure when meeting new people, once he feels safe, he blossoms into a playful, affectionate boy who loves nothing more than a good toy session!

If you are happy to throw a squeaky toy for him all day long then you will very quickly make a new best friend. He really is a gem with so much potential.

Lenny is crate trained and finds comfort in having a safe space of his own. He’s also house trained and keeps his environment clean, making him a joy to have around the home.

He travels well in the car, making him a great buddy for road trips or vet visits without the stress, in fact he seems to get more excited about being In the car than the actual walk!

He’s shown himself to be neutral and polite with other dogs when out and about on a walk, and seems disinterested in cats, but would be best as the only pet in the home,

Lenny can be a little pushy in certain situations, particularly when asked to do something he’s unsure about – a trait that’s not unusual for his breed.

Because of this, a confident, calm owner would really help him thrive. Previous experience with American Bulldogs or similar breeds would be helpful, though it isn’t essential.

He would benefit from multiple meet & greets to help build a strong bond before going home, and he’s currently available for either adoption or temporary foster.

With all the change he’s experienced lately, he’s bound to be a little confused and would really flourish in a stable, loving environment where he can feel safe and settled again.

Lenny is neutered, vaccinated, flea and wormed.

name: Max
description:
Max is a small to medium-sized 1 ½ year old male Patterdale cross Staffordshire bull terrier

Max is currently in a foster home in Chester, Cheshire

Max is a beautiful 1 ½ year old Patterdale Cross Staffordshire Bull Terrier who’s ready for a brand-new start after a rough beginning.

This sweet boy came into our care after being taken to the vets to be put to sleep — through absolutely no fault of his own.

Max adores human company and loves nothing more than curling up on the sofa with his people. He’s happiest when he’s with someone and would love a home where his family is around most of the time, especially while he settles in.

He can find being left alone a bit stressful and isn’t keen on spending time in his crate just yet, so patient adopters who can help him build his confidence will be perfect for him. A Patterdale/Terrier experienced home would be beneficial.

At night, Max sleeps soundly downstairs and during the day he’s calm and settled as long as he has company.

He’s toilet trained (with the occasional little accident while he’s settling), walks nicely on the lead, and gets very excited when he sees his harness — walkies are one of his favourite parts of the day!

He’s friendly with people and can live with older children, and he enjoys meeting calm dogs out and about, though he prefers to avoid bouncy or excitable ones.

Max is currently living with another dog in foster care, and could live with another pending successful meets. He could possibly also live with dog savvy cats too!

Max is a bright, agile boy — he can jump over baby gates and even open doors! Because of this, a secure garden with a 6ft fence is essential.

Despite his difficult start, Max has such a big heart and so much love to give. He’s looking for a patient, caring home where he can feel safe, loved, and part of the family. In return, he’ll give you endless cuddles, loyalty, and affection.

A link to our adoption process can be found below:

You will then be invited to meet the dog, and we encourage 2-3 meet & greets for you to get to know your chosen dog, we are happy to introduce you to multiple dogs on the day of they are suitable matches. We do request all household members attend meet & greets including resident dogs.

If successful we will request a home check at this stage along with proof of identification and address. We will require written permission from a landlord for all applicants in rented accommodation.

Please note we require all resident dogs to be neutered and up to date with vaccinations before we will proceed with the adoption.

name: Poppy
description:
Poppy is a 3-year-old female Staffordshire Bull Terrier Cross-Breed. She’s a shy but deeply affectionate girl who lights up with warmth once she feels safe. Her loyalty runs deep, and she loves nothing more than curling up close to her favourite person.

She was a star in her foster home — clean, house-trained, and gentle around the home. Like many Staffies, she’s not a fan of rainy days, and she can be wary of household items like hoovers or mops, though reassurance helps her feel more settled.

She also enjoys cheekily sneaking off with socks or small objects, occasionally guarding them, so an experienced home is ideal.

Poppy is clever, food-motivated, and thrives with calm boundaries and positive reinforcement.

Out on walks, she has improved massively and now enjoys exploring quieter routes. Busy environments can overwhelm her, so rural or peaceful surroundings suit her best.

She travels well, loves little adventures, and even enjoyed holidays in the Lake District, happily joining longer walks. At the same time, she’s equally content snoozing during downtime.

Socially, she’s selective with other dogs and needs to be the only pet. She also cannot live with cats due to a strong chase instinct.

Poppy can show mild separation anxiety but mainly because she longs for connection and security. She’s seeking an adult-only, calm home where she can settle, feel protected, and continue growing into her confident, loving self.

name: Mia
description:
Mia is a 3-year-old female Staffordshire Bull Terrier Cross. She’s a vibrant, spirited girl whose tail seems to run on its own electricity, wagging constantly once she trusts you.

Beneath her bouncy enthusiasm is a sensitive sweetheart who needs patient people to help her feel safe.

She can be wary of unfamiliar faces or busy environments, so she thrives best in a calm household with gentle routines. Mia blossoms with positive guidance and stability, showing her affectionate side proudly once she feels secure.

Her playful streak makes her a fun companion for someone who enjoys an active but structured lifestyle.

Mia has shown frustration-based reactivity around other dogs, so she’ll need to be the only pet for now. She’s also displayed some resource guarding behaviours, meaning an experienced home is essential to support her training.

With consistent reassurance and kindness, she learns quickly and grows in confidence.

Alongside her adventurous side, Mia loves cosy moments and quality time with her people. She would suit someone who can give her attention, ongoing training, and plenty of encouragement.

Foster homes are welcome too, giving this sweet girl a chance to settle while she waits for her perfect match.

name: Miracle
description:
Miracle is a 2-year-old female Cross-Breed. She’s a gentle soul who starts off shy but quickly transforms into a deeply loyal companion once she feels safe. Her soft nature shines brightest in quiet spaces where she can build trust at her own pace.

Miracle is loving, affectionate, and happiest when she gets calm company and steady reassurance. She travels beautifully in the car and greets strangers with a friendly attitude, though she still appreciates being given room to settle.

Her housetraining and lovely manners make her easy to have around.

On walks, Miracle is polite on the lead but can show reactivity towards some dogs, usually due to excitement or frustration.

Continued socialisation will help her feel more relaxed in those moments. She has previously lived with a male dog and could again if their personalities suit.

She has also lived with a cat, but her food guarding means she may be better in a cat-free home or one that can manage feeding routines carefully.

Miracle has recovered from a past leg injury and toe surgery, and although she still enjoys her walks, she benefits from a home that understands her physical limits.

At her core, Miracle is thoughtful, loyal, and eager for a peaceful environment where she can fully flourish with patient people by her side.

name: Bob and Charlie
description:
Bob and Charlie are 5years old and a bonded pair male Podenco cross.

We have the sad story of Bob and Charlie, who are 5 and a half year old Podenco mix brothers. They have the traditional, tan, short coats and they are gentle lads, with big hearts and very kind natures.

They are a little chunky atm, but we think that’s a reflection of how much they have been loved and how contented they are.

They love all people, no matter the age, and small kids will have their face licked off if the dogs can reach. They do not jump up, but will certainly welcome you and be happy to meet you.

As big as they are, they think they are lap dogs. At night, they love their owners so much, that they both like to sleep in their bedroom to be close.

The very sad part is that the boys owner just died, and their mum will have to downsize and maybe to a flat. She doesn’t want to let them go but she can’t see how she will cope and is looking for a home, if possible for both to remain together.

They have only known themselves for the last 5 and half years and we are looking for one owner for both, but I’m sure they wouldn’t mind being split if it meant not having to go into a shelter.

So to start, let’s just look for one new mum and dad and see how that goes!

There is a lot of information we need to get for them – ie how tall? Weight, But for now lets get them out there to show you all.

Charlie is more dominant, he looks after his brother. he does like his love, especially his shoulders being massaged, but not as much as Bob. Bob could be tickled all day long, even to pulling your hand to keep stroking him when you stop.

They will sit watching while you eat, but they do not beg. If you open a biscuit tin or packet of cheese, does not matter where they are, they will smell or hear it.

Their senses are amazing! They can be left for a few hours, they will just sleep and I have had no complaints of any barking when i leave the house, the neighbours know when i arrive home though, they bark to greet.

They are good guard dogs, they only bark if there is a knock on the door or if someone is passing, but they are only saying hello we are here there is not a dangerous bone in their body.

They are good with other dogs, they used to have a little play mate, she ran them ragged. Although cats they would chase out of the garden.

They do need training on the lead, due to circumstances they have not been walked enough and not for a long time either. Bob will settle on the lead but Charlie tends to pull a lot and he is very strong, but I expect a halti will sort that.

They get excited in the car. Bob is very scared at the vets. Charlie has no problem. They have their passports Overall they are very laid back and relaxed dogs and will be sorry to see them leave.

name: Vera
description:
Meet the energetic and intelligent Vera. Vera is a two year old female Malinois Cross, medium/large in size, who is very nervous at first but settles to become friendly once she trusts people.

Vera is very nervous of people when she first meets them. She can sometimes nip when overexcited or when taking treats, so her new family will need to continue working on this with her.

Vera accepts a collar, harness, and lead, though she can be excitable on the lead and tends to pull, especially at the start of walks.

She has shown some reactivity toward other dogs and people while on walks but is generally good with dogs she knows, though she may growl if they come too close.

Vera will need a very active family due to her high energy level and breed traits, with lots of long walks and mental stimulation through training.

Vera can have poo accidents in her kennel, so her new home will need to work on toilet training.

She previously suffered from severe separation anxiety, including when left alone in a separate room while her family was still present, causing barking and yelping.

She has managed to be left for up to four hours with another dog but still shows signs of separation anxiety in kennels.

Vera has never shown food aggression, but she is known to counter-surf and steal food lying around, including other dogs’ food. She will need continued training and should be fed separately from other dogs.

name: Penny
description:
Meet the sweet and affectionate Penny. Penny is a two year old female Collie Cross, large in size, who is loving and playful once she gains trust.

Penny is such a sweet girl once she gains trust. She is a bit nervous but loves cuddles and playing. If her trusted staff member took her to the paddock, Penny would run around with them and really enjoy herself.
