Hilda was in the private shelter in Crivatu Romania the very first time we visited and has been there until just a few weeks ago when she came to the UK.

The story of how she came to be rescued, if indeed it’s true, is too horrible to put into print so I will just say that she has been through a lot and, although understandably scared of people, treats us with nothing but gentleness.

Hilda is a large dog with a calm presence. She moves with grace and poise and is quite regal in her demeanour.

Hilda will avoid strangers if she can but once she is used to the people in the home she will choose to be close by and always looks like she wants to come for a fuss but she’s just not quite ready yet.

When you go to her she is happy to be fussed and groomed and will fall asleep with her head on your lap. Hilda walks nicely on a lead but can panic when spooked so we are looking for a rural home for her as she will not cope with a lot of traffic or crowds.

Despite her fears, Hilda is such a gentle dog, that she will need a calm and quiet environment with no children under twelve and with at least one other dog. Anyone considering adopting her must be calm and patient in gaining her trust but will be rewarded with a dog with a heart of gold in the not-too-distant future.

name: Sara
description:
Sara is a 2 year old female Cross-Breed. She is fostered in Norwich Norfolk. She came into our care from Romania as her carer there was moving to the UK and she was worried for her future.

Sara is a placid and sensitive girl who can be a little cautious of new people. She quickly warms up to family though and is an affectionate and friendly girl. Sara mixes well with other dogs but could also live as an only dog.

This combination eliminates all reactivity and she walks beautifully. Sara needs a calm and quiet home environment as she can be very anxious around visitors to the home.

name: Meggie
description:
Meggie is a medium sized female crossbreed aged around three years old.

Meggie was brought to the UK from Bosnia back in October 2022 by another rescuer. She came with her siblings, all were scared but Meggie was the most afraid and never came out from the back of a crate in her foster home.

We have worked with the rescue many times and they asked if we could help her.

It’s taken a very long time but Meggie is only now ready to find her own home.

She is still wary of strangers and unlikely to show herself well when potential adopters come to see her, but actually if someone could just give her a chance she’s very “normal” once she’s settled and gotten to know everyone.

In her foster home she is very playful and affectionate. She walks nicely on a lead but can be a bit jumpy in new places and situations. She continues to grow in confidence though and we believe that with the one to one time she will receive in her forever home all of her nervousness will go over time.

Meggie will need another permanent resident dog in her forever home, she simply wouldn’t cope as an only dog. She will need an adult home environment that’s not too hectic. She has a lovely character once relaxed and will make someone a very loyal and loving family addition with a little kindness and patience.

name: Jenkins
description:
Jenkins is a medium sized crossbreed aged around three years old. Jenkins fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Jenkins has come into our care recently from the Botosani public shelter in Romania.

Jenkins is a quirky boy who forms strong bonds with his “person”. If he was a human I guess he would be classed as a little OCD which can lead to some peculiar behaviours.

He is somewhat oblivious to the concept of personal space and can be a trip hazard around the home due to always having to be “right there”.

He is currently living alongside other dogs in his foster home and will play happily with the pack.

As a creature of habit he can become unsettled when new dogs come into the home and over stimulated when things get chaotic and therefore a quiet and steady how with little coming and going would suits his needs best.

As time passes he is becoming more relaxed, he is an extremely loving and affectionate boy who would be great company for a single person or couple. He is ok with cats, could live with or without another dog but will need an adult home environment.

name: Matilda
description:
Matilda is a huge Romanian Shepherd aged around seven years old. Matilda fostered Norwich Norfolk.

We met Matilda on our trip to the Botosani public shelter in Romania back in March. Generally we don’t willingly take Rommie shepherds as they are a specialist breed that require experienced adopters.

Because she was a middle aged dog we just couldn’t leave her there to live out her retirement years.

Matilda is now in the UK and looking for that experienced adopter. She is the most beautiful, calm, quiet of dogs who requires only gentle exercise and a garden to potter in.

However her genetic program to “protect her flock” is still lingering and she will bark protectively when strangers approach her family.

Of course barking is not going to physically hurt anyone, but she is a big dog with a big booming bark and that can of course be intimidating.

She needs a home where visitors are not a common occurrence and she needs to be put in her own safe space when they do come to prevent any situations where people feel threatened.

Matilda is the most loving and sweet girl with her family. Despite her size her movement is slow and seldom so it’s kind of like having a large rug that gets up and moves itself to another room sometimes.

She is fine with cats and dogs and is very steady around goats and horses….. again her descendency from protecting sheep in the mountains serves her well. Shes just an all round great dog who takes her family duties quite seriously. She will need an adult home environment.

name: Benji
description:
Benji is a small to medium sized crossbreed aged around nine years old. Benji fostered Fakenham Norfolk.

Benji was originally adopted from us a few years ago and has been very well loved and cared for. Sadly he has recently had to be very reluctantly returned due to insurmountable personal reasons.

Benji is a very sweet natured and a quiet dog. he’s no trouble whatsoever. His owners will need to be with him most of the time, as he can be anxious when being left on his own for more than a couple of hours.

He can live with respectful children aged eight plus.

Benji gets on with most dogs out and about but there are a few he takes exception to. He has lived happily as the only dog. Benji loves people, he walks well on the lead enjoy his walks.

name: Gertie
description:
Gertie is a large crossbreed aged around five years old. Gertie fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Gertie came to the UK from a squalid shelter in Romania. She is a big girl but calm and placid around the home. Gertie gets on well with other dogs and ignores the safe rescue cat. She walks nicely on a lead.

She would prefer an adult family – but visiting children is fine. Large breed experience preferred.

name: Jellybean
description:
Jellybean is a medium sized crossbreed aged around four years old. Jellybean fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Jellybean has spent all of her life in the Botosani public shelter until she came to the UK to a foster home a few weeks ago.

Due to the limitations of shelter life poor Jellybean has had to get used to pretty much everything. She has done so well in the short time she’s been here so we are confident that over the coming months she will continue to shine.

She is cautious of new people and a bit bemused about human affection generally as she’s never experienced it, but it’s dawning on her more and more that it’s a nice thing and not so worrying after all.

She will need another dog in her forever home to learn from and for reassurance as she encounters more new life experiences.

Jellybean is not bothered by the safe rescue cat. She will need a calm home environment with no children under the age of twelve. She walks beautifully on lead but is still a little wary of the big wide world.

name: Trinity
description:
Trinity is a medium sized female cross breed aged around 2/3 years old. Trinity is fostered in Norwich Norfolk

I met Trinity during a trip to a Romanian shelter back in October last year. She was living outside on the street along with a few other dogs and was pregnant, not for the first time sadly.

When the rescuer captured her inside the gates of the shelter she asked if we would take her and of course we agreed.

Unfortunately the neighbourhood were not kind to the dogs in that street and would throw rocks at them to chase them away as they didn’t want them around.

As a result of this Trinity is extremely wary of men and will bark at them. In time she can learn to trust individual men but we sadly cannot erase these memories altogether.

Ideally an all female home would be best but a very patient and understanding man could win her trust over time.

It is only barking, it’s like she’s trying to warn the others that there’s a man around and they should be scared, the others ignore her and carry on with their day lol.

Trinity is currently living with many other dogs and for the most part is ok. She can be a little jealous over food and fuss though so maybe a home as the only dog would be easier.

She would need a home with no children under the age of twelve. Trinity walks nicely on a lead and is loving her new domestic life.

name: Solomon
description:
Solomon is a smallish whippet/sheltie type crossbreed aged around five years old.

Solomon was brought to the UK from Romania as a puppy by a private adopter who then couldn’t cope with him so we were asked to step in. He was rehabilitated and adopted back in 2020 but has recently been returned to our care due to a change in domestic circumstances.

Solomon is quite whippety/sheltie like in behaviour as well as looks. He is a bit of a worrier and tense around new people but very loving to his family. In a pack he is very playful but a little bossy with smaller dogs so would like a home with a dog either his own size or larger. He will need an adult only family. Solomon loves his walks and getting out and about but will need a confident and experienced adopter.

name: Lindsay
description:
Lindsay is a 1 year old pup who we think will grow to be medium sized but parentage is unknown.

Lindsay has come into our care recently from the Botosani public shelter in Romania.

She is a gentle girl who’s had a difficult start in life, but she’s shown such courage and strength along the way.

After recovering from a broken leg, she’s now doing really well and is expected to make a full recovery.

Though a little shy when meeting new people, Lindsay’s affectionate and playful side soon shines through once she feels safe.

She would be happiest as the only dog in her new home, but this isn’t essential and could live with children aged 12+.

Lindsay has been patiently waiting for her chance, and now she’s ready to find her forever home.

name: Carrie
description:
Carrie is a 9 month old pup who we think will grow to be medium sized but parentage is unknown. We met Carrie in our last trip to Botosani public shelter in Romania.

She is such a sweet girl and really looked for fuss when we entered the pen. Given the time and space, she will be such a loving girl.

Carrie would be happy with or without a resident dog and would be suitable with children 10+.

name: Albie
description:
Albie is a medium sized crossbreed aged around eight years old. Albie fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Albie came into our care initially in 2021. He’d been previously abandoned in a field in Romania and was saved by rescuers there.

He was adopted quite quickly but has now been returned five years on because he’s not adjusted well to life with a new baby.

Albie is ok with other dogs but not hugely interactive with them and would be quite happy as an only dog. He has previously lived with cats.

Albie needs an adult family as can be jumpy with sudden movements. He enjoys his walks and absolutely loves to be groomed.

name: Isadora
description:
Isadora is a two to three year old medium sized crossbreed.

Isadora was taken into the Botosani public shelter in Romania, along with an unremembered number of siblings, when she was just a baby. She is an example of why we work so hard to get all pups out while they are still pups.

She grew up there, spent her adolescence there, never seeing the outside of her concrete pen. She missed out on the silliness and care free attitude of youth because she was concentrating on staying alive.

When we met her at two years old she had learnt to be cautious of some people and she hadn’t experienced as much as the feeling of grass under her feet. She arrived here a few weeks ago and she had to learn it all from scratch.

As you can see from her pics, the girl has learnt well and she has learnt pretty fast! She is now a cheeky character who dares to push herself forward in the pack in her foster home.

She is the instigator of most of the games, she tries to take our cake when we have a coffee break (cardinal sin) and she is generally curious about everything.

Isadora loves to be around us, she will get so excited when anyone comes round and she will boop them with her nose, but she is still very tense when stroked and will try to change any attempts of love and affection into another game.

The loving bit will come with time and it’s something she can learn over the first weeks and months in her forever home. She will need a patient and understanding adopter with at least one other dog that will match her playfulness and energy.

She is gaining confidence on walks and we will, of course, continue her lead training while she’s with us. But she is ready to move on now and continue her development and growth in the environment she gets to spend the rest of her life in.

Isadora will need an experienced adopter who will understand all that she was deprived of in her early life. She will need patience and guidance but is already showing how great she will be once her last fears are overcome. She could live with respectful children aged twelve plus.

name: Levi
description:
Levi is a male medium sized crossbreed aged around 18 months old. Levi came to us a from the Botosani public shelter in Romania. Having been discarded like rubbish as a baby, he spent his first weeks and months in the squalid conditions there with little to no human interaction.

When he arrived in the UK he was terrified of humans and it has taken several weeks to get him to the point that he’s ready to find his forever home.

Levi is fostered in North Walsham, Norfolk.

Levi is now a fun loving pup who enjoys being around people he knows well. He is cheeky and playful with us but still very tense and unsure of human touch, this will come with time.

Levi is recovering really well from an operation on his leg which he is expected to make a full recovery from. The vet believes trauma at a young age prevented the femoral head developing properly and was thus causing pain when moving against the hip socket.

Levi loves to play with the other dogs in his foster home and will need a reasonably playful companion in his new home. We would not consider a home for him that doesn’t already have a resident dog.

He’s learning really quickly how to walk on lead and responds well to direction even in these early days. This is definitely his most favourite time of day. He’s a pleasure to take out and it’s lovely to see him enjoying life to the full with his foster pack.

He will be very cautious when anyone comes to see him and so needs someone who can see beyond this to the dog he will one day become.

He is making such good progress, learning that human contact is actually a really good thing and something to be enjoyed. You can see him visibly relax once cuddles commence, asking for more when it stops.

He’s come such a long way in a short space of time and will continue to thrive with someone willing to give him time, love and sausages

Levi will need a home with no children under twelve.

name: Queenie
description:
Queenie is a medium sized collie cross aged around five to six years old.

I felt like Queenie was a hidden gem, lost in the crowds at the Botosani public shelter in Romania when we visited in October. I don’t even know if she was there on previous trips, if she was I didn’t see her.

As I was stood outside a pen I saw the flicker of a wag of a tail from inside one of the dog houses, and then her little nose poking out daring herself to come and make friends. I entered the pen and bobbed down to her level and after just a few seconds of talking softly to her she crept forward and put her head on my knee.

Queenie is a submissive girl that would like a quiet home environment. She can live with other dogs but likes dogs that give her a bit of space and don’t jump all over her or get in her face. She’d be very happy to be an only dog in the home. She would like an adult home environment with someone with collie experience.

name: Barney
description:
Barney is a medium sized crossbreed currently aged 1 year old (born Jan 25)

Barney came into our care recently from the Botosani public shelter in Romania. On arrival he was shut down and terrified of us and we did think we had a long road of rehabilitation ahead of us.

However the lure of the fun of the pack in his foster home was too strong to resist and within days he was running around, playing and getting into mischief like all pups should!

He’s pretty comfortable around people too now, with the help of food and treats, but he will need further convincing about fusses and cuddles because he isn’t really appreciating those just yet.

This little boy is so comical and fun and his facial expressions are highly entertaining. He will need at least one other playful dog in his forever home. He can live with respectful children aged twelve plus and wants to play with the cat.

name: Maggie
description:
Maggie is a small to medium-sized crossbreed of around 8 years old fostered Norwich Norfolk.

Maggie came to us from the Botosani public shelter in Romania. She had been in there almost all her life and her existence in the dire place had left her shut down and afraid of humans.

It’s taken a long time but Maggie is now a cheeky and confident girl in her foster home. She is still afraid of people she doesn’t know but is comfortable being touched and groomed by those she knows. She is not yet asking for fuss and attention but this will come later in a more one-to-one environment.

Maggie has met cats and was fine with them.

Maggie needs a home experienced with nervous dogs. She is enjoying her walks now and would like quite an active exercise routine.

It is essential that Maggie lives with at least one other dog so please do not apply unless you have a dog full time in your home. Maggie could not cope with the noise and unpredictability of small children but would be ok with dog-savvy children of ten plus.

Maggie has recently started showing an interest in toys and enjoys chewing on a Nylabone, this has been so lovely to see. She is a massive lover of food and when the treats come out or dinner is being prepared she will push her way to the front and bark, demanding hers.

Maggie often goes to an enclosed field where she can run around off-lead. She used to spend her time at these by herself but now likes to stick with the group, only falling behind if she’s found something good to sniff.

Unfortunately, Maggie had a falling out with another resident dog in her adopted home and this has caused others to initiate bullying behaviour towards Maggie and she is regularly picked on, causing her a lot of stress on a daily basis. She needs somewhere with a nice doggy friend where she can gain confidence with her humans in her own time.

name: Cristina
description:
Cristina is a medium to large sized crossbreed, she is around a year old.

Cristina was rescued as a pup from the streets of Crevedia in Romania. She came to the UK last September and was quickly adopted. She has recently been returned because she didn’t have a good relationship with the man in that household.

Cristina was cared for by a man in Romania and there is also a man in her current foster home, both of which she gets on well with.

Cristina lived with a cat and a small child in that home and loved playing with them but sometimes got “a bit much” as she’s still an overgrown puppy.

She is a sweet and loyal girl who needs a little further training on puppy behaviours. She is a leggy, clumsy, lovable fool who just needs a little time invested in her.

Cristina is loving playing with the other dogs in her foster home and would benefit from a young playful dog in the household but could live as an only dog if sufficiently exercised and stimulated.

She is a beautiful-natured little girl who loves people and has been socialised with children aged eight plus. Cristina mixes well with other dogs but could also be the only dog in the home.

Cristina has begun to learn to walk on a lead but will need further practise. She will need all the usual socialisation and training that every pup should receive.

name: Frida
description:
Frida is a medium size very pretty crossbreed girl of just 4 years.

She is very loving, intelligent, affectionate and obedient, a real people dog. She can live alongside other dogs but would be happier I think as an only dog.

She is very well behaved on the lead, not reactive and is confident, well behaved and responsive on her walks. Frida is kennel clean and would make a great family friend for adventures and fun.

Frida would be okay to live with dog savvy children 12 years and over. Would consider families with younger children too.

She is neutered, inoculated, microchipped, etc and is available for meet and greets from our premises in Wistaston, Cheshire by appointment only.

name: Champ
description:
Champ is a 1 year old male Patterdale Terrier Cross.

Cheeky Champ is looking for a terrier loving home that will be able to keep his active mind entertained. He is a young boy who will need continued training and guidance to help him grow into a well rounded gentleman.

Champ’s new adopters would benefit from a good understanding of terrier breeds, particularly Patterdales who often thrive on purpose and activity.

Champ loves learning and is looking for new owners who have the time and patience to give him plenty of mental and physical outlets and opportunities to practice behaviours natural to him.

He is affectionate and loves time with people but still shows lots of puppy and adolescent behaviours so will need a patient home to share their calm.

Champ copes well in his world and has especially enjoyed his trips to the park so would love someone with easy access to places he can explore and build skills slowly.

He quickly steals the heart of anyone he meets and will make a wonderful companion for anyone ready for a rewarding journey.

Champ can live in a ground floor flat as long as there is direct access to a private garden. He can live with dog savvy, older teenagers of 16+ who will give him space when needed and help with his training.

His new owner will be expected to continue his training and socialisation and will receive three free 1:1 sessions with our Mayhew Animal Behaviourist to help guide them.

Champ was found to have previous pelvic fractures after coming in to us which were already healing well so did not require surgery.

Champ now has an unusual gait but after a pain medication trial, it is believed he is comfortable and is not in need of meds at this time.

Due to these fractures, Champ may be more at risk of developing osteoarthritis later in life and may need medical management at any time.

Champ also has enamel hypoplasia on some teeth which means thinning or deficiency of the enamel layer. New adopters will need to be extra vigilant to dental hygiene.

Champ has been microchipped, neutered, will have received his first vaccination and is up to date with flea & worming treatment.

He has also been health checked and behaviourally assessed. Lastly, every dog adopted from us will go home with 4 weeks free pet insurance.

name: Ted
description:
Ted is a 1 year old male German Shepherd mix and he has had a tricky start to his new life in the UK.

Although he had a potential home in the pipeline, it unfortunately fell through and we’re back to square one. Ted is an amazing young dog.

He is full of character, loves humans, picks up new things quickly, and would make an incredible companion in the right home.

Being a Shepherd, we’re looking for a confident and committed family who can give him the structure, training and enrichment he needs to really thrive.

Ted is a highly intelligent, affectionate and adventurous young dog with a huge personality.

He is very people focused and loves being involved in whatever his humans are doing, whether that means exploring somewhere new, learning something, enjoying a cuddle or simply sitting on a lap.

He has no idea that he’s a little too big for that!

Ted is curious, confident, energetic and agile, and as he has settled into his foster home, his cheeky personality has really started to come through. He is very bright and observant, and responds particularly well to training in the home.

He already knows sit, down and leave it, is learning wait and stay, and has a good recall around the house and garden. He is extremely food motivated, and he enjoys long lasting chews and activities that give him something to think about.

He is less interested in traditional dog toys and much more fascinated by whatever he can find himself, so his adopter will need to keep tempting household objects safely out of reach!

Ted has shown himself to be a very affectionate and friendly dog with people. He loves meeting people and will generally want to say hello, enjoy a fuss and find out whether they have any treats.

He can be very enthusiastic with licking and affectionate mouthing, but this is playful behaviour can be redirected with appropriate training.

He has been very good with older children and would be best suited to children around eight years and upwards who understand how to interact appropriately with an excitable young dog.

Ted’s main area for improvement is his behaviour when walking on lead. He is strong, energetic and easily distracted outdoors, and he can become highly focused when he sees another dog.

If another dog approaches while he is on lead, he may stare, jump, growl and attempt to move towards them, so this needs to be worked on.

We can give some recommendations on appropriate harnesses that will help, and we also feel this will start to decrease with a more confident handler.

In comparison, his behaviour is notably different when he is settled. He has been able to relax underneath a pub table with lots of dogs around him and has watched dogs passing calmly while settled at a café or picnic area.

He also now largely ignores the neighbour’s dog after becoming accustomed to it.

Ted originally came from a shelter where he was sharing his space with plenty of other dogs, so he is not a dog who has simply been unable to live alongside other dogs.

His current difficulty appears to be much more closely associated with being on lead, the movement of passing dogs and the excitement and frustration that this creates.

His foster feels that with the right guidance and professional support, there is plenty of scope for him to make progress.

He is a clever dog who learns quickly, and giving him clear boundaries, consistency and plenty of exercise is likely to make a huge difference.

Ted is a very active young dog which is not a surprise with him being a Shepherd.

He also has higher enrichment requirements than some other breed types due to him being so smart, and would be particularly well suited to an active person who enjoys spending time outdoors.

A semi-rural home with easy access to fields, countryside, riverside walks or other open spaces would be ideal. A busy city or heavily built-up residential area is unlikely to suit him.

Ted is already is housetrained, crate trained, travels brilliantly in the car and has settled well into his foster routine.

He is super loyal, affectionate, responsive and eager to be involved with his family, and he has already shown how much he can learn in a short space of time.

For someone prepared to give him that time and guidance, Ted has the potential to develop into a fantastic, devoted companion.

name: Lilo
description:
Meet Lilo – The Little Poppet Who Wants to Be Your Whole World

This gorgeous little Frenchie has recently come into our care and is an absolute poppet. She’s affectionate, playful, wonderfully people-focused and has a huge personality packed into her little body. Lilo absolutely ADORES her people.

She wants to be involved in everything you do and would happily spend her days following you around, cuddling up beside you and making sure she doesn’t miss out on anything.

She becomes very attached to her humans and is a sensitive little soul, so we’re looking for a family who will really enjoy having her as the centre of their world.

And if meeting new people is involved? Even better! Lilo loves people and will happily greet visitors with her favourite toy in her mouth. It’s her way of saying, “Hello! I’ve brought my toy — now let’s be friends!”

Loves her people and wants to be with them

Loves carrying and greeting people with toys

Playful, sensitive and full of character Lilo is also a lovely little walking companion. She enjoys getting out and about and meeting the world, so her new family will have a brilliant little adventure buddy on their hands.

One Little Quirk Lilo had issues with food around the large dominant female bulldog in her last home but has not shown this since being in the rescue. This isn’t something that needs to stop her living with another dog, but feeding should be monitored to begin with.

Lilo’s Ideal Home Lilo could suit lots of different family homes, but there is one thing that is particularly important to us — her people need to be around for most of the time.

This little girl really thrives on human companionship.

She becomes attached to her family and wants to be involved in their everyday life, so we’re looking for someone who genuinely wants a dog who will be their little shadow.

Lilo has previously lived with children over the age of five and has been great with them.

She has also lived with cats and gets along well with other dogs, subject to appropriate introductions and separate feeding.

As a young dog, she will also need her family to continue working on her house training.

Moving into a new home is a huge change, so adopters will need to be patient and understanding if she has a few accidents while she settles in and learns her new routine.

Lilo will be spayed before adoption and is already fully up to date with her vaccinations.

Why We Love Lilo Lilo is the kind of little dog who wants to be part of your life, not simply live alongside it.

She wants to walk with you, play with you, greet your friends, cuddle on the sofa and generally make sure she’s involved in whatever is happening.

She’s affectionate, funny, sensitive and completely adorable.

We’re looking for someone who will fall head over heels for this little girl and, in return, let her fall head over heels for them. If you’re looking for a Frenchie who wants to be your companion, your shadow, your walking buddy and your cuddle monster all rolled into one… Lilo could be your girl.

If you think you could offer Lilo the loving, committed home she deserves, please visit: www.savingandrehomingstrays.org

name: Dexter
description:
Dexter, a 9 year old , is an absolutely adorable border collie boy. He is a lovely older gent that just wants some humans to share his retirement with him.

Dexter sadly came to us as part of a welfare case.

Dexter is a wonderful dog, and I absolutely adore him! He is just a happy go lucky kind of guy, very laid-back, just wants to please. His favourite thing is a gentle stroll, and then a snuggle on the sofa; he adores his humans!

Dexter will make a very rewarding addition to his new family. He is absolutely adorable. He is an older boy but still loves a trot around in the fields, but will also happily have a steady lead walk.

He is an amazing companion dog and will be a best friend to anyone who is lucky enough to adopt him; he gives the best cuddles!

Dexter is house trained, walks well on the lead is not destructive and can be left for short periods. ?

He is a perfect family pet however, due to his older years we feel he would prefer a home with teenage children – he would love a friend to play and snuggle with him. Dexter is currently on a diet as he is quite plump!

Dexter is a very social lad so could live with other dogs or would be equally happy as the only dog with lots of human company.

Personally, I think he would love a home as the only dog so he gets all the attention, but he is currently living with other dogs without issues, as long as he gets his slot on the sofa!!

Dexter is very responsive, and well trained. He loves his home comforts and a cuddle. Dexter travels very well in the car, whoever adopts this lovely lad will be very lucky indeed as he really has the most amazing well-adjusted nature and such a beautiful face.

Dexter is neutered, microchipped, de flea and wormed and vaccinated.

Can you offer this beautiful lad the retirement home he so desperately deserves?

name: Nala
description:
Nala is a 3 year old female Staffordshire Bull Terrier Cross, who came into our care when her owner – local to us – was very tragically found dead in his flat.

There were two dogs there – Bear, who we rehomed a while back, and young Nala, whose mum was a typically loving Staffordshire Bull Terrier and her dad a Ridgeback x.

We’ve had quite a bit of interest in Nala but sadly nothing has quite worked out. Always very near misses though as there is much to love about Nala: she’s not huge energy; is a real love-bug, obedient and well-trained.

She loves the car. She is well socialised and is calm and comfortable walking in busy places – with just the occasional bark/minor reaction if another dog is in her face.

Shouty, unpredictable young children can also spook her (there’s no aggression; she just finds them a bit scary which is why we’ve specified no children in her new home).

We think she would do best either as an only dog or with a nice confident older male dog in a quiet, adult home with some bull-breed experience and without tons of visitors. (She’s very friendly/loving but can find a lot of comings and goings stressful).

She is fine to be left for a 2/3 hours once settled.

Nala has now been in a fabulous foster for some weeks and foster mum Amanda has nothing but praise for her – describing her as a very easy dog once she is settled.

Nala will be three in November. She is spayed, chipped, fully-vaccinated and treated for parasites. She weighs 30kg.

Nala is currently in Wittering nr Peterborough but can travel for the right home.

name: Kyle
description:
Kyle is an approximately 12-month-old Collie cross, although he looks mainly Collie, currently being fostered in Gloucestershire in an adult home with other dogs.

Kyle started his journey in Spain as a stray. When I met him in June he was still only a baby and, although lovely with the other dogs, he was very shy and cautious with people.

I knew he needed to leave the kennel environment and experience home life to give him the chance to learn to trust.

He arrived with us in August and what a difference a month has made!

Kyle has embraced home life beautifully. He quickly bonded with our dogs and, although initially very cautious with us, he has always been gentle and friendly.

Everything outside the home was new to him, but he approached it all with curiosity rather than fear.

Fast forward a month and Kyle is now a Garden Centre and café pro! He walks off lead, meets new people and dogs, travels happily, walks well on a lead & collar and even climbs into the car himself.

His confidence has grown enormously – and yes, he now gives me kisses! and now strangers too.

Kisses for a lovely lady who worked at the Garden Centre

He is clean in the house, sleeps well, travels well and is happy to be left. For a Collie, Kyle isn’t particularly high energy. He loves his walks and enjoys sniffing, but is equally happy to settle on the sofa while I work.

We have even cat tested him with no issues.

Quite simply, Kyle has no red flags. He is good with other dogs, good around people, has no issues with food, is clean in the house, travels well, can be left and settles beautifully. He takes treats incredibly gently and has a lovely, respectful nature.

Kyle reads other dogs beautifully. He has walked in different packs and is happy to play when invited, but equally happy to respect a dog that doesn’t want to play. He isn’t pushy or in your face and simply takes his time when meeting someone new.

His only consideration is that he is naturally reserved and needs a little time to get to know you and feel comfortable in new situations. This isn’t fear or nastiness – he simply likes to assess things first before deciding everything is okay!

Kyle would suit an adult home with a person or couple. We don’t feel a busy family environment with lots of people coming and going would be right for him.

He does need another dog or dogs in his new home, as canine companionship is very important to him.

He could be a lovely little dog for someone wanting to enjoy activities such as scent work, agility or simply lots of adventures together. He loves using his nose and has the Collie brain, but he isn’t the typical sharp, highly driven Collie.

We absolutely adore this brave little dog and are so proud of how far he has come. He has worked incredibly hard to discover the world and now deserves the right home to continue his journey. We will not compromise on finding that home.

Kyle is neutered, vaccinated, blood tested with clear results and has his Pet Passport.

name: Andres
description:
Meet Andres, a big, lovable 9 year old male crossbreed boy weighing around 45 kg, who’s ready to find his perfect match.

Andres absolutely adores people — and if you’re a woman, you might just become his favourite human instantly. He’s a friendly, easy going companion who fits beautifully into daily life.

Great with dogs and gentle with kidsHouse-trained and clean indoorsTravels well in the carWalks like a dream on the leashLoves water and bath timeCan stay home alone calmly (may bark if he hears unusual noises outside)Confident and relaxed in busy city environments — crowds and traffic don’t bother him at allPlease note: Andres cannot live with cats or small animals.

We’re looking for an experienced large-dog owner — ideally a woman — who can offer:

A home with a gardenAnother calm, confident dog companionUnderstanding of big dog needs and behaviour

Currently located outside of the UK, Andres is a wonderful, balanced dog who will bring loyalty, companionship, and a lot of love into the right home.

name: Mischa
description:
Mischa is a shy and reserved girl who, along with her sister Raina, was thrown over the wall of a kennels in November 2024 when they were only young pups. At around eight months old now, Mischa will be a large-sized adult dog, but she is a complete softie.

Mischa and Raina were abandoned in the right place with the right people. For the first few weeks, they were glued to each other, but as they’ve become more settled, they are becoming braver and coming into their own personalities.

Mischa tends to hang back while Raina takes the lead, but she’s improving each day. Routine and consistency will be key in helping her feel settled in a new home. She’s gentle, sweet, and soft, just needing reassurance and confidence building to blossom into a confident dog.

When it comes to other dogs, Mischa is very playful and enjoys interacting with her sister and other kennel dogs. She loves playing in the paddock and has bursts of speed, often being chased by Raina.

Mischa would be best suited to a semi-rural home with a calm household atmosphere and a moderately active lifestyle. She needs a garden and a resident dog to help her adjust to a companion lifestyle.

Mischa is currently based in Cyprus, has a clean bill of health, and is ready to travel to her forever home.

name: Trico
description:
Trico is a 4 year old male Gascon Saintongeois Cross.

After a really long wait at the pound, TRICO was recently released and he is proving to be the sweetest soul!

Currently in a foster home, his carer says he is a timid chap with people, but friendly with other dogs and super clean indoors.

Trico never gets into trouble! TRICO passions, so far, are food and he loves a scent too.

TRICO is such a lovely little man who needs a family of his own, a patient owner who can help him blossom.

TRICO he is castrated, vaccinated, microchipped, blood tested, he has a passport and he can pack his bags if the right family appears.

He is currently in Spain but can travel abroad, the charity arranges all the paperwork and transport.

name: Milo
description:
Milo is a 5 year old male Spanish Hound Cross.

Milo is such a good boy, friendly, calm and clean.

Even cats are no issue for him! Milo would really like to have a loving home at last, someone who sees what a wonderful boy he is.

Milo is castrated, vaccinated, microchipped, blood tested, he has a passport and he can pack his bags if the right family appears.

He is currently in Spain but can travel abroad, the charity arranges all the paperwork and transport.

name: Raina
description:
Raina – 8 month old female Cross-Breed is a large-sized puppy who will grow into a large adult dog. She was abandoned alongside her sister Mischa at a kennels in November 2024 when they were young pups.

Raina and Mischa are only just beginning to explore their independence. For weeks, they stuck close together, but now they’re starting to show their own personalities.

Raina, the more confident of the two, is soft, squishy, and sweet-natured. While she may be a little shy initially, she warms up with time, trust, and reassurance, showing potential to become a wonderful companion.

Raina is playful and enjoys running in the paddock with other dogs, often cheekily stealing toys from her sister. She’s food-oriented, making her a good candidate for basic training using treats as motivation. Her experience on the lead is limited, so her new family will need to help her with training and routine.

Raina is looking for a semi-rural home with a calm atmosphere, a garden, and an active yet balanced lifestyle. Although not essential, she would likely adjust more quickly with a resident dog.

Raina is currently based in Cyprus and has a clean bill of health. She is ready to travel once she finds her forever home.

name: Daisy
description:
Daisy is a six month old female cross breed puppy who currently weighs around twelve kilograms and is expected to reach approximately twenty kilograms when fully grown.

She is fostered in a home in Bulgaria, where she has settled beautifully and is ready to travel to the United Kingdom once the right family is found.

Daisy is fully vaccinated, microchipped, neutered, clinically healthy, and will travel with an EU pet passport and all required documentation.

Daisy is an exceptionally calm, gentle, and easy-going puppy. Despite her young age, she has wonderful house manners and has adapted brilliantly to life in a home.

She is clean indoors, settles well, and happily stays home alone for a few hours without causing any damage or becoming distressed.

name: Sadie
description:
SADIE – FOUR YEARS OF LOVE, STILL WAITING FOR HER PERSON

Four years. That’s how long Sadie has been waiting. Four years of wagging her tail for every visitor, hoping today might be her day.

Four years of pressing her head into the hands of rescuers, desperate to be someone’s dog. Four years of watching others leave while she stayed behind.

Sadie is love in its purest form. She is human-oriented in every way, craving touch, affection, and closeness. She is cuddly beyond words, the kind of dog who melts into your arms.

She is loyal and devoted, ready to give her whole heart to the person who finally chooses her. But Sadie has never been chosen. She doesn’t understand why.

She doesn’t know that dogs like her—dogs who don’t like sharing their humans—often wait the longest. Because Sadie isn’t just loyal—she is fiercely devoted.

She doesn’t just want love—she wants to protect it. She doesn’t want to share her human—she wants to belong to them, and only them.

Sadie is not a dog for just any home. She is a dog for someone who wants an unbreakable bond. Someone who will be her world, just as she will be theirs.

At 6 years old, Sadie is still waiting. She is not meant to be one of many. She is meant to be someone’s one and only. Sadie needs to be the only dog in the home.

She will love her person beyond measure—and fiercely protect them from every other dog. She is waiting for the human who needs her as much as she needs them. Could that person be you?

6 years old (March 2025) – four years of waiting for her chanceMiddle-sized, stunning, and full of loveDeeply affectionate, cuddly, and human-orientedLoyal beyond words—ready to give her whole heartNeeds to be the only dog in the homeWill protect her human from every other dog

Fully VaccinatedSpayed4D TestedBrucellosis TestedMicrochippedFull RBU

Sadie has waited long enough. Could you be the one to finally take her home? Please get in touch today!

name: Max
description:
A strikingly handsome, loyal, intelligent boy who is ready for his new life.

Max is the kind of dog who makes an impression the moment you meet him — confident, affectionate, and beautifully connected to his people. At 30 kg, he’s a solid lad with a gentle heart and a playful spirit.

Great with other dogs — social, friendly, easy-going

Very loyal and smart — bonds deeply, learns quickly

Loves being brushed, fussed, and played with

Excellent at the vets, calm and cooperative

Plays happily with our 14?year?old work experience student

Has interacted with small dogs and younger children with no issues

Car rides aren’t his favourite yet — most likely because he was abandoned and fears it may happen again. But he’s improving every week, learning that car trips now mean safety, not abandonment.

And truly… he has the best set of pearly white teeth we’ve ever seen.

Max is an all?around super boy who will thrive with:

An active family, Someone home often, Children 10+ due to his size – A home that values companionship, routine, and fun

Max is fully vaccinated, neutered, and ready to fly on August 2nd. For everyone’s comfort and safety, children in the household must be 10+ due to his size.

name: Newton
description:
Newton, approximately 4 yrs old, large, crossbreed.

Newton can only be described as a cuddly bear! He loves people, adores attention, and thinks he’s still a pup. Despite his size he will try to climb on your lap for cuddles.

Newton is a stunning boy with the softest coat and the most loving nature. He’s incredibly cuddly, adores human interaction, and will happily lean in for a good neck scratch and cuddle any chance he gets.

His affectionate personality makes him a truly special companion and it is a testament to him, given the situation he has found himself in.

Newton has been with shelter for a while and, sadly, no one ever came forward to claim him. Given his loving and gentle nature, we think he had a home before and had humans that he loved, even if this wasn’t reciprocated.

Despite this, he remains full of love and is quite happy-go-lucky.

He is a strong boy, so he will thrive in a home with experienced owners. He walks nicely on the leash. Newton gets along well with female dogs of a similar size but can’t live with males or smaller dogs.

He’s not just looking for a home—he’s looking for someone who understands him, can guide him, and will give him the love and structure he needs to truly flourish.

In return, you’ll gain a loyal, affectionate companion who will be by your side through everything. He would suit an active family (children 10+ due to size), single person, or a couple.

Newton can be adopted in the UK or Cyprus. His adoption fees are sponsored so, if travelling to the UK, we are just asking for travel costs to be covered.

He is ready to fly. He is vaccinated, castrated, and has had a full health check and blood tests for infectious diseases.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Roy
description:
Roy is a 1.5-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is an amazing, happy and friendly boy who is looking for his forever home. With his cheerful personality and beautiful smile, Roy is hoping to find a family who will love him for the rest of his life.

Roy is very friendly with people and enjoys spending time with them. He also gets on well with other dogs and is suitable to live in a home with canine companions. His happy nature makes him a wonderful companion.

Roy has not yet been tested with cats, so it is not known whether he could live with them. He is suitable to live with older children, making him a good match for families with sensible older youngsters.

He is looking for a home where he can continue to be happy and loved.

Roy is currently based in Cyprus but can travel to the UK or elsewhere in Europe once he has been adopted. He is ready to make the journey to his forever family when the right home comes along.

He is waiting for someone to give him the chance he deserves.

Roy will be adopted with a full adoption package. This includes vaccinations, a microchip, blood tests and neutering before he joins his new home. Rescue backup and support will be provided, and a home check applies as part of the adoption process.

name: Hermes
description:
Hermes is a 1.5-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a sweet, gentle and friendly young dog who is looking for his forever home. He gets along beautifully with everyone he meets and has a lovely nature.

Hermes enjoys being around people and makes a wonderful companion. His friendly personality means he is happy to spend time with those around him. He is also social with other dogs and is suitable to live with them.

Hermes has not yet been tested with cats, so it is not known whether he could live with them. He is suitable to live with older children, making him a good match for families with sensible older youngsters.

He is looking for a loving home where he can continue to thrive.

Hermes is currently based in Cyprus but is able to travel to the UK or anywhere in Europe once he has been adopted. He is ready to make the journey to begin a new life with his forever family.

He is hoping to find a home where he will be loved and cared for.

Hermes will be rehomed with a full adoption package. His vaccinations are up to date, and he is microchipped, blood tested and neutered.

Full rescue backup will be provided, and a home check is required before his adoption can be completed.

name: Artie
description:
Artie is a gentle, one-year-old Shepherd mix from Cyprus who is ready to start a new life after being found abandoned in a municipal pound.

Artie is a true sweetheart who is looking for the opportunity begin again. He’s a young dog, estimated to be no more than one year old, and he has already experienced more hardship than any dog should.

He was found abandoned in a municipal pound before being taken in by one of our shelter partners when space became available. Understandably, he arrived frightened and unsure, with signs that he had not received the kindness or care every dog deserves.

Despite his difficult start, Artie has shown himself to be a calm, gentle and sensitive boy. He is not naturally trusting of new people and tends to hang back when meeting someone for the first time, but his shy nature is never defensive. Instead, he quietly observes, waiting until he feels ready to approach.

He will come to you ever so gently and slowly when he’s ready, you just have to earn it! With time and understanding, he begins to show interest, especially if you happen to have a biscuit in hand. Treats have become an important part of his confidence building journey and are really helping him learn that people can be kind.

Among other dogs, we have noticed that Artie has a naturally soothing presence and has formed some lovely bonds with other dogs in the shelter, particularly those who are nervous or have similar temperaments.

He has been a quiet source of comfort to many of them, offering calm companionship and helping them to feel at ease. For this reason, we believe Artie would thrive in a home with another friendly, well-adjusted dog to show him the ropes and offer reassurance.

He is still learning to trust the world around him and will need an adopter who understands the importance of moving at his pace. Artie would do best in a peaceful, semi rural home with access to a secure garden and without too much hustle and bustle.

A household with older children, ideally aged ten and above, would suit him better at this stage, as younger children may feel overwhelming for him. He has not yet been tested with cats so we have no insight as to how he may react to a resident feline.

Artie is a work in progress, but what he lacks in confidence he makes up for in heart. He is a gentle boy with no malice in him, only the quiet hope that life might finally offer him the love and safety he has missed out on so far.

With time, consistency and lots of patience, we believe Artie will come into his own and become a truly devoted companion.

If you are looking to make a real difference to a dog’s life and believe in the quiet power of kindness and patience, Artie may just be the one.

name: Mura
description:
MURA is a medium size loving German Shepherd crossbreed girl of 5 years who has sadly had to grow up in the shelter in Spain since she was a puppy.

She adores people and is slowly growing in confidence as she is finally getting out to explore the world. She is well behaved on the lead and is quickly adapting to new situations but needs more life experience.

We are confident Mura will make a fantastic family dog given time. She is intelligent, obedient, eager to please and quick to learn and kennel clean.

Mura’s brother was adopted a couple of years ago in the UK and has grown into the perfect dog and companion. Mura would be okay to live with dog savvy children 12 years and over and is suitable to train to live with a cat if required.

She is neutered, inoculated, microchipped, etc with no known health issues and is available for meet and greets from our premises in Wistaston, Cheshire by appointment only.

name: Bianca
description:
Bianca is a 3-year-old female Husky-Cross. This medium-large girl, weighing approximately 25kg, has already been through more than most dogs should ever have to.

Found starving and alone on the streets of Cyprus, she was so desperate for food that she was eating scraps alongside a colony of cats.

Emaciated, weak, and suffering from leishmania, she had clearly been abandoned once her illness made her “inconvenient.”

But despite the pain and neglect she endured, Bianca never gave up. She quietly accepted her rescue, knowing on some deep level that things were about to change.

Thanks to an incredible foster family, Bianca has transformed. With love, vet care, and proper medication, she has overcome her leishmania — now fully recovered and thriving.

She just needs a simple tablet twice a day to keep the condition in check. It’s manageable, doesn’t increase insurance premiums or affect her quality of life, and is absolutely worth it for a dog who gives love as fiercely as Bianca does.

For the past1 year, Bianca has been living in a foster home and learning how to be a dog again. She’s fully house trained, understands basic commands, and walks well on the leash.

She’s food motivated, making her very trainable — and she’s totally obsessed with squeaky balls. Her ideal day? A long sniffy walk, a fun play session, and cuddles with her favourite humans.

Bianca is incredibly affectionate and loyal to her circle, though she can take a little time to warm up to strangers. Once you’re in her heart though, you’re there for life.

She’s not keen on other animals and must be the only pet in the home. That said, she’s all the dog you’ll ever need — her love runs deep.

Her perfect match would be someone who loves big, bold personalities with even bigger hearts. An active home is ideal, with people who appreciate her breed’s intelligence and energy.

While experience with dogs — especially Huskies — is helpful, it’s not a strict requirement. What matters most is a loving, understanding home that’s ready to give this beautiful girl the second chance she’s waited so long for.

Bianca can be adopted in Cyprus or the UK. She has been tested for other infectious diseases, is spayed, will travel with a passport, be vaccinated, including rabies, and receive regular flea and worm treatments.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Dante
description:
Dante is a 6-year-old male Cross-Breed. He is a medium-sized dog who is described as handsome, loving and affectionate. Dante is also obedient and quick to learn, making him a wonderful companion for a family looking for a friendly and sensible dog.

He is very good on the lead and has no known fears. Dante is sociable with all dogs and enjoys being around other canine companions.

His happy nature and confident personality help him settle well into different situations.

Dante is kennel clean and has no health issues reported. He is a cheerful and well-balanced dog who appears to take life in his stride.

His affectionate temperament means he enjoys spending time with people and forming strong bonds with those around him.

He could live with other dogs in his new home and would be suitable for families with dog-savvy children aged 12 years and over. Consideration may also be given to families with younger children.

His loving and sensible nature suggests he would enjoy being part of an active and caring household.

Dante has been neutered, inoculated and microchipped. He is available for meet and greets by appointment from the rescue premises in Wistaston, Cheshire. He is a happy, affectionate and sociable dog who is ready to find a loving forever home.

name: Kayan
description:
Kayan is a very handsome boy of 7 years young who is a large size Mastin cross.

He is very loving and affectionate dog, a real gentle soul in a large body. He is very good with other dogs and would be suitable to live with dog savvy children 12 years and older.

Kayan is a very happy dog who is very obedient and quick to learn. He is kennel clean and well behaved on the lead and is not reactive.

He loves his walks and is desperate for a family of his own, he has waited a long time.

He is neutered, inoculated, microchipped, etc and is available for meet and greets from our premises in Wistaston, Cheshire by appointment only.

name: Gaston
description:
Gaston is a two year old Labrador mix who arrived recently after being found running among traffic.

Once again, without a microchip, there was no way to know if anyone was missing him, and he was admitted to the shelter in the hope a family might come and claim him as their own.

Unfortunately, that never happened, and now we’re looking for Gaston’s forever home.

At the moment Gaston shares his kennel with a number of other dogs, both males and females. He has slotted in really well and gets on with everyone he meets.

He has an energetic, silly style of play and loves a bit of rough and tumble with other dogs, but he can also read the room and knows when it’s time to stop.

Gaston is still a young dog, and he’s therefore looking for a more active lifestyle with a family who can take him on long walks and engage in some basic training with him, to help him let off some steam and to give him some mental focus too.

Although he comes across as quite the goofball, there are some brain cells in that big head of his, and he does actually like to learn. He loves being made a fuss of and gets very excited when he’s praised for being a good boy.

Gaston is still working on lead training, and he can be quite strong when he pulls so this is an area that may need some continued work by his new family.

He is responsive to positive reinforcement, and unsurprisingly for a Labrador type, he loves food as a reward! He can also get over-excited quickly and will jump up without realising his size can be a bit overwhelming!

With this in mind, he would be better suited to a home with slightly older children who are used to being around dogs. We’re confident this behaviour can be improved with training, but there’s only so much we can achieve in a shelter setting.

Gaston is a very friendly, loving, goofy and sociable dog, and he would make a lovely companion in the right home.

We’re unsure if Gaston has lived in a conventional home setting before, so he will need some patience as he adapts to a new lifestyle, but as he’s so people oriented we’re sure with lots of reassurance he will settle in quickly.

The ideal home for Gaston would be based outside of the city with direct access to a secure garden.

He’d really benefit from some introductory training to improve his manners and build a strong bond with his new family, and he would also love a fairly active lifestyle.

He loves rolling around in the grass at the shelter, napping under the shade of the trees, and digging in the dust, so a family who spend a lot of time outside would be perfect for him.

He is such a silly love bug with a heart of gold, and we’d love to see him find the forever home he deserves.

name: Danny
description:
Danny is a beautiful and handsome, young Collie/Pointer cross Mastin boy, with a short, black and white flecked coat. Poor boy has had a terrible experience of life so far, but now things are turning around for him.

Danny is very sweet natured, with a big heart and lots of trust and affection to humans being kind to him.

Danny started life scavenging for scraps, terrified of people. A kind volunteer began leaving out food for him and he would eat it and even play with her dogs, but he would bolt the second she got close.

When a cruel neighbour started throwing stones at him and threatening his life, she knew she had to save him from that place and move him urgently.

When he arrived in foster care, Danny was a different kind of broken — frozen with fear, hiding in corners, too scared even to be moved. But with his foster housemates by his side, Danny slowly started to come back to life.

Fast forward a few weeks, and this boy is unrecognisable. He is now playful, affectionate, cheerful, and SO ready to give and receive love.

He’s still a little shy in new places and with loud noises which is understandable but he’s intelligent, eager to learn, and already walking beautifully on the lead, trotting alongside a bike, and settling nicely in the car.

Danny loves his doggy friends but has not yet been tested with cats.

Danny didn’t have an easy start, but he never stopped trusting that good things were possible. Now he just needs someone to give him the home he’s been waiting for. And needs someone with time and patience to let him blossom.

Danny is neutered, up to date with vaccinations and had clear blood tests, and tested negative for Brucella

We are looking for a family with another friendly dog for Danny to play with and learn from, and older calm children no younger than 11yrs to suit his level of confidence.

Good on lead, good with bikes, good in the car Good other dogs and people. Smart, affectionate, and blossoming every day.

name: Orion
description:
Orion is a 1 year old, medium-large, male, Cross-Breed, who is a sweet, friendly, lovely boy waiting for his forever home. He has never truly known what it means to be a carefree puppy.

He should be enjoying life in a loving home, cared for and cherished, warm at night instead of sleeping on a concrete floor.

Confiscated from his owners, Orion and his three siblings have all been in the shelter since they were just young pups. Arguably, it was the best thing to happen to them, but now they each really need a home and family to call their own.

Orion is a medium-large dog who will need ongoing training to help him settle into home life. He has gotten used to walking on a lead and is well behaved on walks.

He is also wonderful with other dogs and children. Even though he is young, Orion and all of his siblings give off a lovely calming energy and we suspect they will be medium energy once in a home.

Orion is far too young to spend his days in a shelter and has missed an important stage of learning and exploring, but it’s never too late for dogs! He could live with a single person, a couple, or a family. A secure garden and nice walks would be ideal.

Orion can be adopted in Cyprus or the UK. He will be tested for infectious diseases, is castrated, will travel with a passport, be vaccinated, including rabies, and receive regular flea and worm treatments.

Please help give this lovely boy the life he deserves.

Full rescue back-up is provided by Saving Souls Animal Rescue, a UK-based registered charity.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Willow
description:
Willow is a 1 year old, medium-sized, female Cross-Breed who is a friendly, happy girl eagerly waiting for her forever home. She does not know what being a puppy truly means.

She should be enjoying life in a loving home, cared for and cherished, warm at night instead of sleeping on a concrete floor.

Confiscated from her owners, Willow and her three siblings have all been in the shelter since they were just young pups. Arguably, it was the best thing to happen to them, but now they each really need a home and family to call their own.

Willow is a medium-sized dog who will need ongoing training to help her settle into home life. She has gotten used to walking on a lead and is well behaved on walks. She is also wonderful with other dogs and children.

Even though she is young, Willow and all of her siblings give off a lovely calming energy and we suspect they will be medium energy once in a home.

Willow is far too young to spend her days in a shelter and has missed an important stage of learning and exploring, but it’s never too late for dogs! She could live with a single person, a couple, or a family. A secure garden and nice walks would be ideal.

Willow can be adopted in Cyprus or the UK. She has been tested for infectious diseases, is spayed, will travel with a passport, be vaccinated, including rabies, and receive regular flea and worm treatments.

Full rescue back-up is provided by Saving Souls Animal Rescue, a UK-based registered charity.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Freya
description:
Freya is a beautiful Segugio Italiano cross, estimated to be around 4-5 years old. She’s on the smaller side of medium and has been patiently waiting for almost three years to find her forever home.

Found abandoned and severely underweight, Freya has been cared for by a local boarding kennel in Cyprus, where she’s blossomed into a gentle, affectionate, and sweet-natured dog.

Freya is slightly reserved and shy when meeting new people, but she has made significant progress in building her confidence, thanks to her kennel mate, Ira. She thrives in calm and predictable environments and would do best with a patient family who can help her continue to grow.

Freya gets along well with other dogs and has a submissive nature in group settings. She enjoys canine company but is also content living as the only dog, provided her adopters give her plenty of attention and reassurance. If there is a resident dog, it might help Freya settle in faster, but it’s not a requirement for her to thrive.

Freya would be best suited to a semi-rural home with a garden where she can engage in scentwork and sniffing games, which help her relax and exercise her natural instincts. Busy households or homes with younger children might overwhelm her, so a calm home with children aged 10+ would be ideal.

True to her scent hound heritage, Freya loves to explore her surroundings, sniffing and searching for treats. She is very food motivated, which is a fantastic way to build trust with her. Freya takes treats gently and patiently waits her turn, endearing herself to everyone she meets.

Although she might be shy initially, Freya’s sweet and affectionate nature will shine once she forms a bond with you. Watching her transition from kennel life to a loving home will be incredibly rewarding.

Freya is healthy and ready to travel from Cyprus to her forever home. Could you be the one to give this lovely girl the peace and happiness she deserves?

name: Casper
description:
Meet Casper, a 5 year old male Cross-Breed who’s been waiting far too long for his shot at happiness. He’s currently based at Simba Shelter in Cyprus and has sadly become one of their longest residents.

Well over a year he has been in the shelter and you can actually see the sadness in his eyes.

How can a dog that looks like Casper have been in the shelter for all this time. Is it his age? The fact that he’s not small and fluffy? He deserves a second chance in life just as much as the desirable-looking dogs.

And the most heartbreaking thing is his affinity for humans. He doesn’t get out of his kennel much but, when he does, he relishes at the opportunity for some human affection.

In his current situation, he shows less interest in his actual walks and more interest in humans.

Casper is a profoundly wonderful dog on so many levels. Not only is he incredibly handsome, but he’s also clever and eager to please. He would suit an adopter willing to take the time to get to know him, train him, and invest in his potential.

Casper has shared his space with female dogs but has shown to be generally quite selective with canines. As a result, he requires a pet/dog-free home.

As with any rescue dog, Casper needs time and structure to settle into home life. In return, Casper will give back tenfold — loyalty, love, and gratitude in abundance.

Having known hardship and the loss of a family (we think he had a home before), Casper will be one of those eternally grateful dogs.

They are simply a joy to take under your wing and watch thrive in a home. And we, as volunteers, love to see this. It is exactly why we volunteer in dog rescue, to see dogs like Casper come out the other side and get their happy ending.

We provide full rescue back up and provide guidance and support throughout a dogs life.

Casper’s adoption fee is sponsored due to the length of time he has been in the shelter.

Casper is located in Cyprus and, if adopted in the UK, will travel with a passport and be tested for infectious diseases. He is fully vaccinated and castrated.

Foster placement, foster view to adopt, and adoption all considered.

name: Lucy
description:
Lucy is a 7-year-old Beagle cross, likely mixed with a smaller terrier breed. She’s on the smaller side of medium, full of personality, and ready to find the forever home she so deserves.

Rescued from the streets of Cyprus while pregnant, Lucy’s puppies were quickly adopted, but she has been waiting in kennels for over two years. Despite this, her zest for life and love for people remains unshaken.

Lucy is a people-oriented dog who adores human interaction. She’s confident, friendly with new people, and her playful, cheeky personality makes her a joy to be around.

When let out of her kennel, she sprints like a rocket but quickly circles back to you for belly rubs. Her favourite pastime is splitting her energy between zoomies and lounging in the dirt for cuddles, always with her tail wagging furiously.

Lucy is energetic but not overwhelming, and with a more active lifestyle, she’s ready to thrive. She loves being outdoors, exploring green spaces, or playing in a secure garden. Her ideal home would be outside the city, with access to safe spaces where she can run and play.

While she does need some basic training (like curbing her tendency to jump up in excitement), Lucy is eager to please and already well-behaved in many ways—she returns to her kennel without protest after playtime.

Lucy is good with other dogs but doesn’t need a resident canine companion to be happy. She’d also be a lovely fit for families with children aged 6+ due to her friendly temperament, though her playful energy might require supervision at first. An adult-only home with plenty of love, cuddles, and treats would also suit her well.

Though currently living in a kennel, Lucy’s adaptable nature means she’ll likely settle quickly into a home environment. She has a clean bill of health and is ready to travel from Cyprus to meet her new family.

name: Ivan
description:
Ivan is a one year old Greek Harehound, and unfortunately he is looking for a new home as soon as possible. He arrived in the UK in June 2025 at the age of five months old, and has been in a loving, supportive home since then.

But very sadly, the arrival of a baby has led to Ivan being relinquished back into our care. Our deadline to find Ivan a foster home is the middle of May, and if we’re unable to do so he will have to go into kennels.

Due to the significant life changes his family are going through, Ivan has not been given adequate attention or training over recent months.

With his family now functioning on reduced sleep, they have admitted that they no longer have the time for him and that he’s spending more and more time in his crate.

All of this change has resulted in his behaviour deteriorating as he’s found situations more overwhelming to deal with. We recognise that his environment is also not the most conducive to his needs, and this too plays a role in him needing a new home.

Ivan is looking for a semi-rural home where he has more space, a nice garden to run about in, and a family who understands hounds. He is currently living in London and is struggling with the suburban surroundings.

There are a lot of factors that he finds overwhelming and this is causing pent up frustration and anxiety. He would be much happier outside of the city where he can enjoy long walks in green spaces.

Ivan needs some time to reset, adjust to a new environment, and decompress. He is extremely food motivated, which really helps with training, and he has learnt a few tricks too.

He is also housetrained and crate trained, but does unfortunately struggle with the car which needs some continued desensitisation training.

In true hound fashion, Ivan is incredibly affectionate with his family, loves a snuggle on the sofa, and is happiest when chasing after a ball.

He’s an energetic boy and needs an active home, but he also responds well to mental stimulation and enrichment with his food, such as stuffed kongs and scatter feeding.

Ivan’s main struggles relate to reactivity and anxiety. Before leaving the shelter and in his initial UK foster home, Ivan was brilliant with other dogs and socialised with males and females of a variety of ages.

Unfortunately this hasn’t been the case since being adopted, and he is now very selective with other dogs. It is possible that in a calmer environment this may improve, and he has had good relationships with mature female dogs.

Although Ivan currently lives with a newborn and has been very adaptable to the new arrival, we’re looking for a home with older children simply to keep his environment a bit more predictable and relaxed.

Ivan is looking for a family that can give him the time, patience and training to settle in at his own pace.

We feel a change of environment will really be integral in supporting his onward progress, and we won’t be considering urban homes given his struggles in London.

We know how loving, sweet natured and friendly Ivan can be and we’re looking for a home where he can enjoy lots of adventures, a calm home atmosphere, and has the attention and understanding of a more experienced adopter.

name: Ally
description:
Ally is a four year old German Shepherd mix. Poor Ally came into the shelter over a year ago after being rescued running scared in the roads.

She was so sad in the shelter when she first arrived and would sit by the kennel bars and cry for hours.

We think she has previously had a family and was desperate for them to come and get her, but of course that never happened, and months later she’s still without a home to call her own.

Ally is a lovely dog who through no fault of her own has just been overlooked time and time again. By nature she’s an active, intelligent and very loyal girl.

She’s eager to please and is so bored in the shelter, so she would thrive in an active home with someone who wants to explore with the company of a canine best friend.

Shepherds have great stamina, so long hikes and camping holidays will be no problem for a dog like Ally – she’d love it! She’d also love any kind of training, as she loves to please and learning new things is great fun for intelligent breeds like herself.

Ally shares her kennel with another dog and although she seems to enjoy his company, it’s clear that humans are her first love.

She is content around other dogs, happily to walking alongside them when outside the shelter and sharing her space with them, but we feel she would be fine either with or without a resident dog to live with.

Ally’s ideal home would have a garden where she can let off some steam and stretch her legs, but even if her garden is small as long as she’s based outside of the city surrounded by plenty of places to explore, she’ll be happy.

We have no doubt that she will be so loyal to her new family, but she may have some separation anxiety to overcome due to her abandonment based on her behaviour in the shelter.

With patience, reassurance, routine and consistency this is something that can be overcome, and who can blame her for feeling worried after experiencing being dumped before?

Ally would love a family home where she can experience the security of feeling loved, wanted, and a sense of belonging.

She has a soft heart and although her abandonment should have broken her trust in people, she’s been nothing but forgiving and resilient. We would love for her to find the family she’s been waiting so long for.

name: Jasmine
description:
Our extra special girl Jasmine is approximately one year old and a delightful small cross breed. Jasmine weighs a humble seven kilos and measures eleven inches from shoulder to paw.

Having been found abandoned on the streets, Jasmine has been in our Cyprus shelter for three weeks.

Jasmine is stunningly attractive. She has incredibly delicate features and the most beautiful facial expressions. This blends so well with her bubbly and fun-loving disposition.

Jasmine’s coat and markings are sublime. She has some classic black and tan with a distinctive white flash to her chest. And then there’s the gorgeous half tone brindle along her back. If ever a dog were to stand out from the crowd it would be Jasmine.

She is youthful, fun loving, affable and affectionate. Jasmine so yearns for human interaction and will make a glorious family dog.
